llm_summary: Researchers examined whether a heart medication called vericiguat works differently depending on what other heart drugs patients were already taking, since doctors need to know the best order to prescribe medications for people with weakened heart pumps. The study looked at over six thousand patients with heart failure who were already on standard heart medications and tracked whether adding vericiguat reduced their risk of death or hospitalization compared to a placebo, or dummy pill. The results showed that vericiguat did not significantly reduce the risk of death or hospitalization regardless of which heart medications patients were taking or how high their doses were, even though most patients were already on multiple heart drugs. The findings suggest that vericiguat's effects do not appear to depend on a patient's other medications, which means doctors cannot use this information to decide when to add vericiguat to a treatment plan. The researchers emphasized that these exploratory results should not be used to change how doctors currently recommend heart medications, and more research with better design would be needed to fully understand how vericiguat fits into heart failure treatment.

title: Building trauma-informed physical therapists: a mixed-methods evaluation of a multimodal training module in hybrid DPT education.
abstract: Trauma-informed care (TIC) remains inadequately integrated into health professions education despite its clinical relevance, limiting opportunities for graduates to develop the skills necessary to support individuals with trauma histories.This gap is particularly pronounced in Doctor of Physical Therapy (DPT) education, where hands-on clinical practice creates unique conditions that could evoke trauma-related responses or retraumatization. This study evaluated a multimodal TIC training module embedded in a hybrid DPT curriculum.Using a convergent mixed-methods design, this study evaluated a multimodal TIC training module embedded in the third semester of the first year of a hybrid DPT curriculum across two consecutive cohorts (N = 142). Quantitative pre-post surveys measured changes in self-reported TIC-related knowledge, attitudes, and confidence; qualitative data were drawn from post-intervention open-ended survey responses and student self-reflection essays.Significant improvements were observed across all three domains, with large effect sizes replicated across both cohorts (Hedges' g = 1.39 for knowledge familiarity; g = 1.31 for confidence). Qualitative analysis yielded four themes: developing a trauma-informed professional identity, intentional relationship-building as core clinical practice, applying TIC principles in clinical decision-making, and recognizing the role of the clinician's inner experience. Integration of quantitative and qualitative data revealed strong convergence and complementarity across strands, and identified a confidence-complexity paradox; large measured gains in physical examination confidence alongside persistent qualitative uncertainty about managing trauma responses during hands-on care.These findings support embedding TIC training in DPT education, with implications for professional identity formation and mitigation of physical therapist burnout.

llm_summary: Trauma-informed care, which means understanding how past traumatic experiences affect patients and adjusting treatment accordingly, is not being taught well enough in physical therapy schools even though it is clinically important. Researchers tested a training program that taught trauma-informed care principles to first-year physical therapy students across two groups totaling 142 students, using both surveys before and after the training and written reflections from students. The training significantly improved students' knowledge, confidence, and attitudes about trauma-informed care, with these improvements being large and consistent across both groups of students. The study found that students developed a stronger professional identity around trauma-informed practice and learned to build better relationships with patients, though some students still felt uncertain about handling trauma responses during hands-on physical examination. These results suggest that physical therapy programs should include trauma-informed care training in their curriculum, which could help new therapists provide better care and reduce their own stress and burnout from the work.

title: Follicular lymphoma and the microenvironment: potential targets and biomarkers.
abstract: Follicular lymphoma (FL) is an indolent B cell malignancy characterized by recurrent genetic alterations, yet its clinical course is highly variable and not fully explained by tumor-intrinsic features alone. Increasing evidence highlights the tumor microenvironment (TME) as a critical regulator of disease progression, therapeutic response, and immune escape.FL TME is composed of diverse cellular elements, including T cell subsets, tumor-associated macrophages, stromal cells, and follicular dendritic cells, which collectively provide survival signals and shape immune dysfunction. These interactions have led to the identification of potential therapeutic targets, such as immune checkpoint molecules, macrophage polarization pathways, and stromal-tumor signaling axes. In parallel, microenvironment-derived biomarkers, including specific immune cell compositions, spatial organization patterns, and gene expression signatures, are emerging as important predictors of prognosis and treatment outcomes. Advances in single-cell and spatial profiling technologies have further refined our understanding of TME heterogeneity, enabling the discovery of clinically relevant targets and biomarkers.Together, these insights support a more integrated model of FL biology and provide a foundation for developing microenvironment-directed therapies and precision medicine approaches.

llm_summary: Follicular lymphoma is a slow-growing blood cancer that develops from B cells, which are immune cells that normally fight infection, and while the cancer cells themselves have specific genetic changes, doctors have noticed that the overall disease progression varies widely between patients for reasons not yet fully understood. Researchers examined how the tumor microenvironment, meaning all the other cells and structures surrounding the cancer cells in the body, plays a major role in determining how the disease progresses, whether treatments work, and how cancer cells escape immune detection. The tumor microenvironment contains many different types of immune cells, support cells, and specialized cells that work together to help cancer cells survive and prevent the body's natural defenses from attacking them, which led scientists to identify several potential targets for new treatments including immune checkpoint molecules that act like brakes on the immune system. These discoveries have also revealed that specific patterns of immune cells, their spatial arrangement within tumors, and particular gene expression signatures, which are the genes that are actively turned on or off, can serve as biomarkers to predict which patients will have better or worse outcomes and which treatments will work best. title: Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy Is a Time-Sensitive Operation: National Outcomes Associated With Delayed Surgery.
abstract: BackgroundCompetition for urgent and emergent operating-room access is a significant challenge in many hospitals. Evidence-based benchmarks for early intervention are well established for emergencies like acute appendicitis or hip fracture. In contrast, laparoscopic cholecystectomy for acute cholecystitis or symptomatic cholelithiasis is often delayed. The purpose of this study was to evaluate the clinical and economic impact of delays in laparoscopic cholecystectomy across the US.MethodsThe Nationwide Readmissions Database was queried for patients aged ≥18 years admitted between 2021 and 2022 undergoing urgent or emergent laparoscopic cholecystectomy. Patients were stratified based on operative timing (<3 vs ≥ 3 days). The primary outcome was 30-day readmission. Secondary outcomes included VTE, SSI, and total cost. Propensity score matching (1:1) was performed using 46 covariates. Linear regression assessed the cost associated with each additional hospital day prior to surgery, with a subgroup analysis of safety-net hospitals.ResultsAmong 136,893 patients, 24,496 (17.9%) experienced delayed laparoscopic cholecystectomy. After matching (n = 48,992), delays were associated with increased odds of readmission (9.5%; OR 1.22 [1.15-1.29], P < 0.001) and VTE (1.5%; OR 1.51 [1.30-1.77], P < 0.001). SSI (0.2%) was not significantly different. The mean total cost was $25,957 ± $21,609 for delayed patients vs $20,784 ± $20,027 for early surgery. Linear regression revealed an incremental cost of $1,695 per additional hospital day prior to surgery, rising to $2071 per day in safety-net hospitals (P < 0.001).DiscussionDelays in laparoscopic cholecystectomy have significant clinical and economic impacts, underscoring the urgent need for national benchmarks to standardize operative timing and reduce disparities for patients in safety-net hospitals.

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether delays in gallbladder removal surgery affect patient outcomes and hospital costs across the United States, since many hospitals struggle to schedule these operations quickly even though they are considered urgent. The study looked at nearly 137,000 patients who had gallbladder surgery between 2021 and 2022, comparing those who had surgery within three days to those who waited longer, and used statistical methods to ensure fair comparisons between the two groups. Patients who experienced delays in surgery were significantly more likely to be readmitted to the hospital within 30 days and to develop blood clots, though surgical site infections did not differ between the groups. The delayed surgery group also cost hospitals about six thousand dollars more per patient, with costs increasing by approximately seventeen hundred dollars for each additional day the patient waited before surgery, and this financial burden was even higher in safety-net hospitals that serve low-income populations. These findings suggest that hospitals need to establish clear national guidelines for how quickly gallbladder surgery should be performed and work to reduce delays, especially for patients in under-resourced hospitals.

title: Infections in ECMO: A Comprehensive Review of the Epidemiology, Diagnosis, Management and Prevention.
abstract: Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) provides life support for severe respiratory and cardiac failure, including failure from severe infection such as sepsis and acute respiratory distress syndrome. Additionally, ECMO-acquired infections are frequent and associated with prolonged hospitalization, increased healthcare utilization, and higher mortality. This review summarizes current evidence regarding the epidemiology, pathophysiology, diagnosis, prevention, and management of infectious adverse events during ECMO. Future work should aim to refine ECMO-related infectious adverse event definitions, improve harmonized multicenter data collection, and to invest in high-quality, well-designed studies.

llm_summary: Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, which is a machine that takes over the work of the heart and lungs for patients with severe respiratory or heart failure, can save lives but also carries a significant risk of infections. Researchers reviewed all available evidence about how often infections occur in patients using this life-support machine, how these infections develop, and what doctors can do to prevent and treat them. The review found that infections acquired while on this machine are common and lead to longer hospital stays, higher medical costs, and increased death rates among patients. Understanding the causes and patterns of these infections is important because it can help doctors better protect patients who depend on this technology for survival. Future research needs to establish clearer definitions of what counts as an infection during this treatment, collect better data from multiple hospitals, and conduct high-quality studies to find the most effective prevention and treatment strategies.

title: Textbook outcomes as a composite quality metric following fenestrated-branched endovascular aortic repair.
abstract: Fenestrated-branched endovascular aortic repair (FB-EVAR) has been increasingly utilized to treat complex abdominal aortic aneurysms (CAAAs) and thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysms (TAAAs). Textbook Outcome (TO) is a composite quality metric designed to reflect the ideal postoperative course. The aim of this study was to evaluate the incidence of TO following FB-EVAR and to identify predictors of TO failure.Consecutive patients enrolled in a prospective, non-randomized sponsor-initiated investigational device exemption study to assess FB-EVAR for CAAAs and TAAAs between 2013 and 2025 were reviewed. TO was defined as the absence of major complications, early reintervention, prolonged hospital length of stay (LOS; based on the 75th percentile of the cohort), non-home discharge, and early mortality (death within 30 days or during index hospitalization). The primary endpoint was incidence of TO. Secondary endpoints included identification of predictors of achieving TO, individual TO component contributions, early morbidity and mortality, and overall survival.A total of 609 patients (422 [69%] males, median age 74 years [IQR 68-79]) were analyzed. Aneurysm extent included CAAA in 164 (27%) and TAAA in 445 (73%). Early mortality was 1.3% (n=8) and 30-day MAE rate was 10.2% (n=62). TO was achieved in 64.2% of patients (n=391). The most common components of TO failure were prolonged LOS (23.6%) and major complications (17.9%), and 48.2% of non-TO patients failed due to a single component. Independent predictors of failure to achieve TO on multivariable analysis were female sex (OR, 0.52; 95% CI, 0.35-0.77; p=.001), increased age (OR, 0.97; 95% CI, 0.95-0.99; p=.013), COPD (OR, 0.58; 95% CI, 0.39-0.85; p=.006), CKD stage 3-5 (OR, 0.63; 95% CI, 0.44-0.92; p=.015), chronic postdissection aneurysms (OR, 0.53; 95% CI, 0.29-0.97; p=.041), larger aneurysm diameter (OR, 0.97; 95% CI, 0.96-0.99, p=.001) and Extent I-III TAAA (OR, 0.51; 95% CI, 0.29-0.89; p=.019). TO achievement was independently associated with improved overall survival (adjusted HR, 0.58; 95% CI, 0.43-0.78; P<.001), with unadjusted 1-year survival of 96% in TO versus 83% in non-TO patients.FB-EVAR was performed with low early mortality, and TO was achieved in nearly two-thirds of patients. The primary components of TO failure were major complications and prolonged LOS. Several independent predictors of TO failure were identified, and TO achievement was associated with improved overall survival. These findings establish a benchmark for TO after FB-EVAR, and a practical framework to guide risk stratification, patient counseling, and targeted quality-improvement efforts.Copyright © 2026. llm_summary: Researchers examined a new surgical technique called fenestrated-branched endovascular aortic repair, which is used to treat dangerous bulges in the aorta (the main blood vessel from the heart), to see how often patients had ideal recovery outcomes without major problems. The study followed 609 patients who received this procedure between 2013 and 2025 and measured success by tracking whether patients avoided serious complications, needed emergency follow-up surgery, had unusually long hospital stays, went home after discharge, and survived the first month. About two-thirds of patients achieved this ideal recovery, while the remaining third experienced problems, most commonly spending too long in the hospital or developing major complications. Patients who were female, older, had lung disease or kidney disease, or had larger aneurysms were less likely to have ideal recoveries, and those who did achieve ideal outcomes had much better survival rates one year after surgery, with 96 percent still alive compared to 83 percent in those with complications. These findings provide doctors with a clear standard for measuring success after this procedure and can help them better prepare patients for surgery and identify which patients need extra attention to improve their outcomes.

title: 2026 ASNC guideline for stress testing in single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT) and positron emission tomography (PET) myocardial perfusion imaging.
abstract: Stress testing is among the most frequently performed cardiac diagnostic procedures and is widely utilized in both outpatient and inpatient settings performed with and without myocardial perfusion imaging (MPI). Since the 2016 American Society of Nuclear Cardiology (ASNC) guideline, clinical experience with cardiac stress testing has continued to expand and evolve necessitating updates to the previous guidelines. This guideline presents updated practice standards for cardiac stress testing intended to support safe and effective testing across a range of clinical environments, while allowing for individualized risk assessment and protocol adaptation based on patient characteristics, special populations, and site-specific logistics. The current guideline offers practical beginning-to-end guidance on the performance of cardiac stress testing, encompassing patient selection and preparation, stress modalities and protocols, safety considerations, and result interpretation and reporting. The utilization of single photon emission computed tomography (SPECT) and positron emission tomography (PET) in conjunction with stress testing are addressed for stress protocols for each available stressor. This revised guideline is intended for a broad, multidisciplinary audience involved in the performance, interpretation, and oversight of cardiac stress testing. ASNC has developed this updated guideline to recognize the evolution of diagnostic imaging that has taken place since the last iteration of the guideline. These updates are intended to support optimal test selection, standardized patient preparation, and individualized, patient-centric practice of nuclear stress testing in diverse clinical scenarios. Utilizing this guideline, clinicians will optimize diagnostic accuracy, maintain patient safety, and at the same time maximize clinical impact.Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Inc.

llm_summary: Stress testing, which involves monitoring the heart while a patient exercises or receives medication to increase heart rate, is one of the most common heart diagnostic procedures performed in hospitals and clinics today. The American Society of Nuclear Cardiology updated their official guidelines for stress testing in 2026 to reflect new clinical knowledge and experience that has developed since their last guideline in 2016, particularly regarding the use of imaging technologies like SPECT and PET scans that create detailed pictures of blood flow to the heart muscle. These new guidelines provide doctors with practical, step-by-step instructions for safely performing stress tests, including how to prepare patients, which methods to use for stressing the heart, how to keep patients safe during testing, and how to interpret and report the results. The guidelines are designed to help doctors choose the best testing approach for each individual patient based on their specific health situation, medical history, and the resources available at their particular medical facility. By following these updated standards, healthcare providers can improve the accuracy of heart disease diagnosis, protect patient safety, and ensure that stress testing delivers the greatest possible benefit to patients across different clinical settings.

title: Australian Pancreatic Cyst Registry: protocol for a prospective national clinical quality registry of intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasms.
abstract: Intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasms (IPMNs) are common pancreatic cystic neoplasms with malignant potential. Current evidence on IPMN management is derived largely from retrospective surgical cohorts that over-represent high-risk cases and provide limited insight into the long-term outcomes of conservatively managed lesions. Australia currently lacks a prospective national dataset to evaluate surveillance pathways, practice patterns, guideline adherence and long-term outcomes in individuals with IPMN. Variation between international guideline recommendations may also contribute to differences in surveillance intensity and thresholds for intervention. The Australian Pancreatic Cyst Registry (APCR) was established to address these evidence gaps.The APCR is a prospective, multicentre clinical quality registry that collects clinical, imaging, management and outcome data for individuals with IPMN across public and private healthcare settings in Australia. Historical information is extracted from existing clinical documentation where available, with prospective data collection continuing during routine follow-up. The registry operates under an opt-out model and aims to enrol up to 10 000 participants over a 5-year recruitment period. Participants are followed through routine clinical care until discharge from surveillance, diagnosis of pancreatic cancer, withdrawal or death. Standardised electronic case report forms capture clinical and imaging variables aligned with risk features described in the 2024 Kyoto guidelines. This analysis will describe participant characteristics, cyst features, management and clinical outcomes, with comparative, time-to-event and multivariable analyses undertaken where appropriate. Guideline adherence and the predictive performance of established risk stratification frameworks will also be evaluated.The study protocol was approved by the Monash Health Human Research Ethics Committee (Project ID: RES-24-0000-634A). llm_summary: Pancreatic cysts called intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasms, or IPMNs, are common growths that can sometimes develop into cancer, but most current medical knowledge comes from studying patients who had surgery rather than those who were simply monitored over time. Researchers in Australia created a national registry to collect information from up to ten thousand patients with IPMNs across both public and private hospitals, tracking their medical history, imaging scans, treatments, and long-term health outcomes through routine doctor visits. The registry uses standardized forms to record patient information aligned with international guidelines from 2024, allowing doctors to compare how well different hospitals follow recommended surveillance practices and when they decide surgery is necessary. This study will help doctors understand which patients with pancreatic cysts actually need surgery and which ones can be safely monitored with regular check-ups, potentially reducing unnecessary procedures and improving patient care across Australia. The findings will be shared with hospitals and published in medical journals to help guide how doctors manage pancreatic cysts in the future.

When standard treatments like pacemakers, which are devices that help regulate heart rhythm, fail to prevent these fainting episodes, doctors may consider more advanced procedures like cardioneural ablation, which involves using heat or cold to destroy specific nerve tissue that is causing the abnormal heart response.

title: ASTCT Consensus Grading for Toxicities after Immune Effector Cell Therapy.
abstract: In 2019, the American Society for Transplantation and Cellular Therapy (ASTCT) developed consensus definitions and grading criteria for the common immune effector cell (IEC)-associated toxicities of cytokine release syndrome (CRS) and IEC-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (ICANS). These grading scales were widely adopted by clinicians, investigators, and sponsors, allowing a clearer understanding of outcomes across clinical trials and a uniform basis to inform treatment algorithms. Since then, other IEC class effects, such as IEC-associated hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis-like syndrome (IEC-HS) and non-ICANS attributable neurotoxicity, have been recognized. ASTCT convened experts for 2 tasks. First, to consider updating the previously published ASTCT grading criteria for CRS, ICANS, and IEC-HS. Second, to consider existing definitions and grading criteria, and/or create consensus criteria for emerging toxicities, including immune effector cell-associated hematotoxicity; non-ICANS neurological toxicities such as parkinsonism, cranial nerve palsies, and polyneuropathies; IEC-associated enterocolitis; tumor inflammation-associated neurotoxicity; and on-target, off-tumor toxicities. These updated consensus toxicity definitions and grading criteria can facilitate comparisons of toxicities of IEC and T-cell engager therapy across clinical trials and in real-world settings, as well as aid clinicians in better characterizing the severity of toxicity that can ultimately be tied to management guidelines.Copyright © 2026 The Authors. llm_summary: The American Society for Transplantation and Cellular Therapy created a standardized system for measuring side effects from immune cell treatments, which are therapies where doctors use specially designed immune cells to fight cancer. Since the original guidelines were published in 2019, doctors and researchers have discovered new types of side effects from these treatments that needed to be added to the grading system. A group of medical experts met to update the existing guidelines for known side effects like cytokine release syndrome, which happens when the immune cells trigger a strong inflammatory response in the body, and to create new definitions for emerging side effects like blood cell problems, nerve damage, and digestive system inflammation. These updated guidelines will help doctors around the world use the same language when describing how severe a patient's side effects are, making it easier to compare results across different hospitals and clinical trials. Having clear, consistent definitions for these side effects will ultimately help doctors better manage patient care and develop safer treatment plans for people receiving immune cell therapy.

title: Colour Doppler ultrasound assessment of retrobulbar hemodynamics and static retinal vessel analysis in Sjögren's disease: the SICARD cohort.
abstract: To assess, for the first time, macrovascular, medium-calibre vessel, and microvascular damage in Sjögren's disease (SjD) using carotid greyscale ultrasound (GSUS), retrobulbar colour Doppler ophthalmic artery (OA) ultrasound (RCDUS), and static retinal vessel analysis (SRVA). Additionally, to evaluate associations of these markers with cardiovascular (CV) risk factors, patient- and disease-related characteristics.GSUS of the common carotid arteries was performed to measure carotid intima-media thickness (cIMT) and evaluate plaque burden. RCDUS assessed OA flow velocity integral (FVI), resistive, and pulsatility indices (RI, PI). SRVA quantified retinal microvasculature using central retinal arteriolar, venular equivalents (CRAE, CRVE), and the arteriovenous ratio (AVR). Imaging findings were compared between patients with SjD and healthy controls and analysed in relation to clinical parameters.130 SjD patients and 100 controls were included. SjD patients showed significantly higher cIMT (padj=0.003), OA-RI (padj=0.003) and -PI (padj<0.001), as well as lower OA-FVI (padj=0.012) and CRAE (padj=0.013) compared with controls. Higher OA-RI and -PI correlated with higher disease activity (ESSDAI: both; rho=0.324, p = 0.006), and impaired renal function (rho=-0.461, p < 0.001 and rho=-0.370, p = 0.002, respectively). OA-RI associated positively with age (rho=0.435, p < 0.001) and inversely with lung carbon monoxide diffusion (r=-0.342, p = 0.019). Lower CRAE correlated with higher mean arterial pressure (r =-0.378, p < 0.001), CRP (rho= -0.215, p = 0.046), ANA titre (rho=-0.268, p = 0.016), and disease activity (ESSDAI: rho=-0.273, p = 0.011).In this first comprehensive study of CV surrogate markers in SjD, patients exhibited vascular alterations across multiple vascular beds, indicating systemic vascular involvement and a possible link to increased cardiovascular and cerebrovascular risk.© The Author(s) 2026. llm_summary: Researchers examined whether people with Sjögren's disease, an autoimmune condition affecting moisture-producing glands, show signs of blood vessel damage that might increase their risk of heart and stroke problems. The study used ultrasound imaging to look at blood vessels of different sizes in 130 patients with Sjögren's disease and 100 healthy people, measuring things like vessel thickness, blood flow speed, and the width of tiny blood vessels in the eye. Patients with Sjögren's disease showed thicker artery walls, slower blood flow in vessels behind the eye, and narrower tiny blood vessels compared to healthy controls, with these problems getting worse in patients who had more active disease or kidney problems. These findings suggest that Sjögren's disease causes widespread damage to blood vessels throughout the body, which could explain why people with this condition face higher risks of heart attacks and strokes. The research represents the first comprehensive look at cardiovascular damage in Sjögren's disease patients and suggests doctors should pay closer attention to heart and blood vessel health in people diagnosed with this autoimmune condition.

title: Associations of Active and Passive Smoke Exposure and Hidradenitis Suppurativa in the Pediatric Population: A Case-Control Study.
abstract: Hidradenitis suppurativa (HS) is an inflammatory condition associated with cysts of the folliculopilosebaceous unit primarily affecting intertriginous areas. HS has been correlated with smoke exposure in the adult population, but there is a knowledge gap in understanding its effect in pediatric and adolescent patients. This study assesses correlations between active and passive smoke exposure and the development of HS in the pediatric and adolescent population.A retrospective case-control study was conducted at Mayo Clinic (2010-2023) of patients diagnosed with HS before the age of 18 years who were age-, sex-, and race-matched to healthy controls in a 1:3 ratio, analyzed using Fisher exact for categorical variables and Kruskal-Wallis for continuous.One hundred and seventy-four cases and 522 controls met inclusion criteria. The prevalence of active and passive smoke exposure was significantly higher in patients with HS compared to controls (p = 0.001), with passive smoke accounting for 64.6% (N = 31/48) of smoke exposure in patients with HS. Smoke exposure was associated with a significant increase in the odds of an HS diagnosis, with an odds ratio of 4.8 (95% CI: 3.06-7.61) for passive and/or active exposure, and 1.64 (95% CI: 1.01-2.61) for passive exposure alone. Smoke exposure was associated with a later age of diagnosis than those with no smoke exposure (p < 0.001).Prevalence of active and passive smoke exposure was higher in pediatric and adolescent patients with HS compared to age, sex, and race-matched healthy controls. Smoke exposure increased the odds of having HS and was associated with a later age at diagnosis.© 2025 Wiley Periodicals LLC.

llm_summary: Hidradenitis suppurativa is a painful inflammatory skin condition that causes cysts in areas where skin rubs together, and while previous research showed a link between smoke exposure and this disease in adults, doctors did not know if the same connection existed in children and teenagers. Researchers at Mayo Clinic conducted a study comparing 174 young patients with hidradenitis suppurativa to 522 healthy children and teenagers of similar age, sex, and race to see whether smoke exposure played a role in developing the condition. The results showed that children and teenagers with hidradenitis suppurativa were significantly more likely to have been exposed to smoke, either from smoking themselves or from secondhand smoke around them, with nearly two-thirds of the smoke exposure coming from secondhand sources. Young people exposed to any smoke had nearly five times higher odds of developing hidradenitis suppurativa compared to those with no smoke exposure, and interestingly, those exposed to smoke tended to develop the condition at a later age than those without smoke exposure. These findings suggest that reducing smoke exposure in children and teenagers could be an important way to help prevent or delay this painful skin disease, though more research is needed to fully understand how.

title: A Novel De Novo STAG1 Variant at the RAD21 Binding Interface Is Associated With Hypoglycemia, Recurrent Fever, Immunodeficiency and Features of Classical Cohesinopathies.
abstract: The cohesin complex, composed of SMC1, SMC3, RAD21, and STAG1/STAG2, is essential for chromosome cohesion, DNA repair, and transcriptional regulation. Pathogenic variants in cohesin components cause cohesinopathies. The classical characteristics of cohesinopathies include developmental delay (DD), intellectual disability (ID), feeding difficulties, hypotonia, short stature, hearing loss, and dysmorphic features. Here, we present a 5-year-old boy with classical cohesinopathy features, including DD/ID and feeding difficulties, along with non-classical features such as hypoglycemia, recurrent fever, and immunodeficiency. Trio exome sequencing identified a novel de novo missense variant of uncertain significance (NM_005862.3:c.643G>A(p.Val215Ile)) in the STAG1 gene. The variant localizes to the RAD21 interaction interface, and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations revealed conformational changes comparable to other STAG1 variants reported as likely pathogenic in patients, supporting a deleterious effect which may disrupt the STAG1-RAD21 interaction interface. This case expands the phenotypic and molecular spectrum of STAG1-related cohesinopathy and advances our understanding of the disease mechanism.© 2026 John Wiley & Sons A/S. llm_summary: The cohesin complex is a group of proteins that work together to hold chromosomes together, repair damaged DNA, and control which genes are turned on or off, and when these proteins are faulty, people develop serious health conditions called cohesinopathies. Researchers used genetic testing on a five-year-old boy and his parents to identify a new mutation in the STAG1 gene, which is one of the proteins that makes up the cohesin complex. The boy had typical cohesinopathy symptoms like developmental delays and feeding problems, but also unusual symptoms including low blood sugar, repeated fevers, and a weak immune system. Computer simulations showed that this new genetic mutation likely damages how the STAG1 protein connects to another cohesin protein called RAD21, which would prevent the cohesin complex from working properly. This case helps doctors and scientists understand that STAG1 mutations can cause a wider range of symptoms than previously known and provides clues about how these genetic changes harm the body at the molecular level.

title: Benchmarking four commercial antimicrobial susceptibility testing systems and disk diffusion to reference broth microdilution in the assessment of gram-negative bacterial isolates.
abstract: Commercial antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST) systems for gram-negative bacteria provide operational advantages over reference broth microdilution (BMD) testing, but the results produced by commercial AST systems might not be as accurate as the reference method. Assessing and comparing the performance of AST systems can be informative for clinical microbiology practice. In total, 280 clinical isolates and 100 isolates from the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention Antimicrobial Resistance Isolate Bank, including Enterobacterales and Pseudomonas aeruginosa, were intended to be tested using disk diffusion (DD) and automated commercial AST systems, such as Selux AST System (Selux Diagnostics), MicroScan (Beckman Coulter), Phoenix (Becton, Dickinson and Company), and Vitek 2 (bioMérieux). These results were compared to BMD as the reference standard. In total, 372 isolates were assessed. For Enterobacterales, the greatest frequency of very major errors was identified with cefepime by Vitek 2 (29.0%) and ertapenem by DD (9.1%); essential agreement less than 90% was identified with the following combinations: aztreonam by MicroScan (86.4%), aztreonam by Vitek 2 (88.9%), cefepime by Selux (86.3%), cefepime by Vitek 2 (76.8%), ceftazidime by Vitek 2 (89.9%), and levofloxacin by MicroScan (83.4%). For P. aeruginosa, essential agreement less than 90% was identified with the following combinations: gentamicin by Selux (87.2%), tobramycin by Selux (86.6%), and ciprofloxacin by Phoenix (88.4%). Overall, antimicrobials that had low demonstrable bias across all automated commercial AST systems included ampicillin, amoxicillin-clavulanate, ceftazidime-avibactam, ertapenem, and trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole. Comparing commercial testing systems head-to-head against a reference standard provides insight into the strengths and weaknesses of the performance of these test systems, and these insights can subsequently inform local decisions regarding further investigations and potential operational mitigation strategies.IMPORTANCEThis study assessed and compared the performance of multiple commercial antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST) systems and disk diffusion methods. The accuracy of determining minimum inhibitory concentrations or zone diameters of antimicrobials and the associated interpretive categories were studied for 372 isolates of Enterobacterales and Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Performance of the evaluated systems revealed that multiple antimicrobial-organism combinations were below the standards typically required by regulatory agencies and clinical laboratories. These deficiencies varied across the commercial platforms and disk diffusion methods, highlighting the importance of benchmarking studies that compare the performance using identical isolates. These identified performance weaknesses may warrant further study and/or the implementation of mitigation strategies in clinical laboratory operations to prevent the reporting of errant results.

llm_summary: Researchers examined how well four commercial testing systems and a traditional disk diffusion method could identify which antibiotics work against harmful bacteria, comparing their results to a gold-standard laboratory method. The study tested 372 samples of common gram-negative bacteria (rod-shaped bacteria that don't retain certain dyes) from hospitals and a disease control bank to see how accurately each testing system could determine if bacteria were resistant or susceptible to different antibiotics. The results showed that several antibiotic and bacteria combinations performed poorly, with some systems making serious errors up to 29 percent of the time, meaning they incorrectly reported that an antibiotic would work when it actually would not. The findings highlight that different commercial testing systems have different strengths and weaknesses, so hospitals need to carefully evaluate which system works best for their needs and may need to add extra checks for certain antibiotics. These results suggest that laboratories should regularly compare their testing systems against reliable standards and consider implementing safeguards to prevent incorrect results from being reported to doctors.

title: Neighborhood Contemporary Redlining and Racial Mortgage Lending Bias and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Women With Breast Cancer.
abstract: Studies have demonstrated neighborhood structural inequities are associated with cardiovascular outcomes among breast cancer survivors. We investigated the associations between bias in mortgage lending practices (contemporary redlining and racial lending bias) and cardiovascular outcomes in women with breast cancer.Using the SEER (Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results)-Medicare database, we identified 51 007 Black and White women diagnosed with breast cancer between 2010 and 2014 with follow-up through 2020. We used Home Mortgage Disclosure Act data to calculate census-tract contemporary redlining index and racial lending bias index, and assessed indices continuously and categorically (low, moderate, or high). We used Cox proportional hazards regression to estimate multivariable-adjusted, cause-specific hazard ratios (HRs) for major adverse cardiovascular events, ischemic heart disease, heart failure, stroke, and cardiovascular death.In the overall population, a 10%-unit increase in redlining was associated with increased risk of major adverse cardiovascular events (HR, 1.04 [95% CI, 1.02-1.06]). Among Black women, those in high redlining neighborhoods had an increased heart failure risk compared with those in low redlining neighborhoods (HR, 1.22 [95% CI, 1.05-1.41]). Similarly, White women in high redlining neighborhoods had an increased risk of ischemic heart disease (HR, 1.23 [95% CI, 1.15-1.30]) and stroke (HR, 1.09 [95% CI, 1.03-1.16]). Black women in high racial lending bias neighborhoods had reduced cardiovascular mortality risk compared with those in low racial lending bias neighborhoods (HR, 0.69 [95% CI, 0.54-0.90]).We identified associations between contemporary redlining and cardiovascular outcomes among breast cancer survivors. High racial lending bias was associated with reduced cardiovascular mortality risk among Black women. Bias in mortgage lending practices may serve as a structural driver of cardiovascular disparities.

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether unfair lending practices in neighborhoods, called contemporary redlining and racial lending bias, are connected to heart problems in women who have survived breast cancer. The study looked at information from over 51,000 Black and White women diagnosed with breast cancer between 2010 and 2014, tracking their health through 2020 and using mortgage lending data to measure the level of bias in their neighborhoods. Women living in neighborhoods with high levels of unfair lending practices had increased risks of heart-related problems, with Black women showing higher rates of heart failure and White women showing higher rates of heart disease and stroke. These findings suggest that the structural inequities embedded in lending practices may be an important factor driving differences in heart health outcomes among breast cancer survivors. Future research should continue exploring how discriminatory housing and lending policies affect the long-term health of cancer survivors and other vulnerable populations.

title: Tirzepatide and the Incidence of Atrial Fibrillation in Adults With Overweight or Obesity: An Updated Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
abstract: Tirzepatide is a dual agonist for glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptors, with proven efficacy in weight loss and improvement in cardiovascular outcomes. However, the effects of tirzepatide on the incidence of atrial fibrillation in patients with overweight or obesity remain unclear.PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Library were searched for randomized controlled trials comparing tirzepatide versus placebo for individuals with overweight or obesity. Odds ratios (ORs) with 95% credible intervals (CrIs) were pooled using a Bayesian binomial-normal hierarchical model, appropriate for rare-event outcomes.Our meta-analysis included 10 randomized controlled trials, including 6515 individuals, of whom 4491 (68.9%) were randomized to tirzepatide. The pooled OR was 2.20 (95% CrI, 0.81-6.75) for atrial fibrillation, 2.16 (95% CrI, 0.90-5.87) for atrial arrhythmia, and 1.84 (95% CrI, 1.04-3.90) for any arrhythmia.Tirzepatide was not associated with atrial fibrillation or atrial arrhythmia. Although higher odds of overall arrhythmias were observed, event rates were low and the findings should be interpreted cautiously.

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether tirzepatide, a medication that helps people lose weight by acting on two different hormone systems in the body, might increase the risk of atrial fibrillation, which is an irregular heartbeat condition. The team searched medical databases for ten randomized controlled trials, which are studies where some people receive the medication and others receive a fake treatment, involving a total of 6,515 people with overweight or obesity. The results showed that tirzepatide was not clearly linked to atrial fibrillation or general atrial arrhythmias, though there was a slightly higher odds of any type of irregular heartbeat overall. Since the number of people who actually experienced these heart rhythm problems was very small in the studies, doctors should be cautious about drawing firm conclusions from these findings. More research and longer-term monitoring of patients taking tirzepatide will be needed to fully understand whether this weight loss medication affects heart rhythm safety in people with overweight or obesity.

title: Contemporary management of differentiated thyroid cancer in Latin America: results from the CaTaLiNA prospective multicenter registry.
abstract: International guidelines increasingly endorse treatment de-escalation for selected patients with differentiated thyroid cancer (DTC), including thyroid lobectomy and selective use of radioactive iodine (RAI) therapy. How contemporary clinical practice in Latin America aligns with these recommendations remains unclear. We evaluated contemporary management patterns and early outcomes within a large prospective regional registry.The Cancer de Tiroides en Latinoamerica (CaTaLiNA) registry is an international, prospective cohort study including patients treated at 11 centers across Ecuador, Peru, Mexico, Brazil, and Uruguay. Adult patients with histologically confirmed DTC undergoing initial thyroid surgery between June 1, 2023, and October 31, 2025, were analyzed. American Thyroid Association (ATA) 2015 risk of structural recurrence and AJCC 8th edition staging were assigned retrospectively. Primary outcomes were the extent of initial surgery, RAI utilization across the ATA risk categories, and early postoperative complications. Multivariable mixed-effects logistic regression was performed to identify factors associated with RAI use and postoperative complications.A total of 901 patients were included (mean age 47.7 ± 13.3 years; 84.9% women). Papillary thyroid carcinoma accounted for 96.7% of cases. Most patients had early-stage disease (AJCC stage I, 81.5%). Total thyroidectomy was performed in 96.4% of patients. RAI was administered in 54.3% of patients, increasing across risk categories (40.7% low risk, 69.2% intermediate risk, and 59.6% high risk; p < 0.001). Tumor size, resection margin status, and a higher ATA 2015 risk category were independently associated with RAI use. Postoperative complications occurred in 15.4% of patients, predominantly transient hypocalcemia, and were more frequent in higher-risk groups; tumor size was the only independent predictor after adjustment.In this large Latin American cohort, management of DTC frequently exceeded the intensity recommended by ATA guidelines, with high rates of total thyroidectomy and RAI, including among low-risk patients. The ATA 2015 framework enables more refined risk stratification; however, its integration into clinical practice remains incomplete. These findings provide important region-specific data and highlight opportunities to optimize risk-adapted care and reduce overtreatment in DTC.© 2026. llm_summary: Researchers examined how doctors in Latin America are treating differentiated thyroid cancer, which is a slow-growing cancer of the thyroid gland, to see if their practices match international guidelines that recommend less aggressive treatment for certain patients. The study followed 901 patients across eleven hospitals in Ecuador, Peru, Mexico, Brazil, and Uruguay who had thyroid surgery between June 2023 and October 2025, tracking what type of surgery they received, whether they got radioactive iodine treatment (a therapy that destroys remaining thyroid tissue), and what complications they experienced. The results showed that doctors were performing more extensive surgery and giving radioactive iodine treatment more often than current guidelines recommend, even to patients with low-risk cancers that might not need such aggressive care. The findings suggest that while doctors have better tools to identify which patients truly need intensive treatment, many are still overtreating patients in ways that may cause unnecessary side effects like temporary low calcium levels without improving outcomes. These region-specific results highlight an opportunity for Latin American hospitals to adjust their practices to match international guidelines and provide more personalized, less intensive care based on each patient's actual risk level.

title: Nucleoporins in Cancer: Functional Roles and Therapeutic Opportunities.
abstract: The nuclear pore complex (NPC) and its building-block proteins, nucleoporins (NUP), play fundamental roles in maintaining cellular fitness by regulating nucleocytoplasmic transport, chromatin and transcriptional activity, and genome stability. These core biological processes are critical for cancer cells, and thus, tumor-driven co-option of NUP-regulated functions has emerged as an important mechanism contributing to the pathogenesis of multiple malignancies. This review discusses how NUP dysregulation mechanistically contributes to tumor initiation and progression and how these insights open opportunities for innovative anticancer therapies, including using clinical-grade molecular glues that induce selective NUP degradation and pharmacologically inhibiting NPC-regulated epigenomic/transcriptomic signaling and nucleocytoplasmic transport.Recent studies demonstrate that NUPs play fundamental roles in cancer pathogenesis by dysregulating key NPC functions and driving tumorigenesis and disease progression. NUPs and NPC-regulated mechanisms can be pharmacologically targeted, providing a strong rationale for developing much-needed innovative therapeutic strategies to combat cancer.©2026 American Association for Cancer Research.

llm_summary: Nucleoporins are proteins that make up the nuclear pore complex, which acts like a gatekeeper controlling what moves between a cell's nucleus and the rest of the cell, and these proteins are essential for keeping cells healthy by managing important processes like gene activity and protecting genetic material. Cancer cells have learned to hijack and misuse these nucleoporins in ways that help tumors grow and spread, making them an important target for understanding how cancer develops. Researchers reviewed how nucleoporins become faulty in cancer and identified that these proteins control several critical processes that cancer cells depend on to survive and progress. The study highlights that scientists can now develop new cancer treatments by using special molecules that force cancer cells to destroy their nucleoporins or by blocking the signals that nucleoporins send inside cancer cells. This research opens up promising opportunities for creating new anticancer drugs that could help patients by targeting a previously underexplored weakness in how cancer cells function.

title: Personalized Circulating Tumor DNA Analysis for Predicting Outcomes and Tracking Response to Radiotherapy and Pembrolizumab in Localized Sarcomas: Analysis of the SU2C-SARC032 Trial.
abstract: Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) holds promise for prognostication and disease monitoring in solid tumors. However, rare and heterogenous tumors with low mutational burden like soft tissue sarcomas (STS) present a technical challenge for ctDNA analysis. We investigated the ability of personalized ctDNA analysis to predict outcomes and track response to radiotherapy and pembrolizumab in patients with localized STS.We analyzed 313 plasma samples collected pretreatment, postradiotherapy/presurgery, and postsurgery from 106 patients treated with preoperative radiotherapy with or without perioperative pembrolizumab for high-risk, localized STS in the SU2C-SARC032 phase II randomized trial. Personalized ctDNA assays were designed to track a median of 46 somatic mutations per patient. Associations between ctDNA levels and outcomes were assessed using univariable and multivariable models adjusting for clinical risk factors.Personalized ctDNA profiling detected baseline ctDNA in 85% of patients. Baseline ctDNA levels correlated with tumor size, grade 3 disease, and expression of genes related to hypoxia and the cell cycle. ctDNA levels pretreatment, after radiotherapy with or without immunotherapy but before surgery, and postsurgery were strongly associated with disease-free and overall survival on univariable and multivariable analyses. Patients treated with pembrolizumab, who had significantly better disease-free survival, had a greater decrease in their ctDNA levels after neoadjuvant therapy. Finally, personalized ctDNA analysis enabled noninvasive subclone tracking and patients with multiple tumor clones detected by ctDNA analysis after surgery had inferior outcomes.Tumor-informed, personalized profiling enables sensitive ctDNA detection and quantitative monitoring in localized STS, providing independent prognostic information across the perioperative course. These findings support prospective ctDNA-guided interventional trials in STS.

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether a blood test that detects tiny pieces of tumor DNA could help predict outcomes and monitor treatment response in patients with soft tissue sarcomas, which are rare cancers that grow in muscles, fat, and connective tissue. The study analyzed blood samples from 106 patients who received radiation therapy with or without an immunotherapy drug called pembrolizumab before surgery, tracking genetic mutations specific to each patient's tumor. The researchers found that they could detect tumor DNA in the blood of 85 percent of patients before treatment, and the amount of this DNA was linked to tumor size, aggressive disease, and poor survival outcomes. Patients who received pembrolizumab showed a greater decrease in their tumor DNA levels after treatment and had better disease-free survival, and those with multiple tumor clones detected in their blood after surgery had worse outcomes. These findings suggest that personalized blood tests tracking tumor DNA could become a valuable tool for monitoring sarcoma patients throughout their treatment and recovery, though further research is needed to confirm these results in larger studies.

llm_summary: Cellular senescence, which is the process where cells stop dividing and age, is a well-known biological process that scientists continue to study and learn new things about. Researchers led by Durik and colleagues discovered that senescent cells, which are aging cells that have stopped dividing, release large fragments of their cytoplasm, which is the gel-like substance inside cells. These shed fragments appear to help the aging cells survive longer than they normally would. The fragments may also serve as a way for senescent cells to communicate with and influence neighboring healthy cells around them. This finding could help scientists better understand how aging cells affect the tissues around them and may lead to new ways to manage age-related diseases.

title: Repurposing a Dual-Head Programmable Power Injector for Controlled Intra-Arterial Vasodilator Delivery During Cerebral Vasospasm Treatment.
abstract: Cerebral vasospasm following aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality. Endovascular treatment with intra-arterial vasodilators is established for medically refractory vasospasm, yet medication delivery relies on manual hand-syringe injection with limited control over infusion rate and volume. In this proof-of-concept technical note, we describe a workflow innovation repurposing a dual-head programmable power injector (Nemoto PRESS DUO elite, Nemoto Kyorindo) for simultaneous contrast administration and controlled vasodilator infusion during endovascular vasospasm treatment. One chamber delivers contrast for angiographic runs, while the other contains a triple vasodilator cocktail of verapamil, nicardipine, and nitroglycerin, delivered via the injector's programmable Infusion Mode at operator-defined flow rates and volumes. This closed-system, dual-chamber architecture eliminates tableside syringe exchanges, reduces the risk of air entrainment, and enables precise, reproducible multi-agent delivery. In our experience with 9 patients (12 treatment sessions), the injector-based workflow facilitated routine use of the triple vasodilator cocktail with angiographic improvement observed in all sessions. Fluoroscopy time, radiation dose, contrast volume, and total procedural duration did not differ significantly from those of a historical manual-injection cohort, which served as a procedural workflow reference. Because the manual cohort received a different vasodilator regimen without nicardipine, the two cohorts are pharmacologically unmatched and angiographic outcomes were not compared between groups. No procedural complications related to the delivery method occurred. These preliminary findings suggest the dual-head programmable injector provides a feasible, ergonomic, and reproducible closed-system workflow for intra-arterial vasodilator delivery during cerebral vasospasm treatment, with broader applicability to other intra-arterial drug delivery settings.Copyright © 2026 The Author(s). llm_summary: Cerebral vasospasm, a dangerous narrowing of blood vessels in the brain that can occur after a ruptured aneurysm, remains a serious problem that causes disability and death in many patients. Researchers tested a new way to deliver blood vessel-relaxing medications directly into brain arteries by repurposing a medical device called a programmable power injector, which normally delivers contrast dye during imaging procedures. The device was modified to have two separate chambers, one for contrast dye to help doctors see the blood vessels and another for a mixture of three medications designed to relax the vessels, allowing doctors to control exactly how much medication was delivered and at what speed. In nine patients receiving twelve treatment sessions, the new method worked well, with all patients showing improvement in their blood vessel appearance on imaging, and the procedure took about the same amount of time and radiation exposure as the old hand-injection method. This innovation offers doctors a safer, more precise, and more reliable way to deliver these life-saving medications during brain vessel treatment, though more research is needed to confirm these benefits in larger groups of patients.

title: RECREA: Registry of Cardiac Rehabilitation Centers in Latin America of the Council of Cardiac Rehabilitation and Sports Cardiology of the Inter-American Society of Cardiology.
abstract: Despite economic and social disparities in Latin America (LA), a better understanding of cardiovascular disease (CVD) has driven regional growth in parallel with the evolution of therapeutic interventions. Cardiac rehabilitation (CR) is an interdisciplinary treatment that has expanded over the past 50 years. Consequently, several regional, continental, and global registries have emerged to understand its structure and operation worldwide. However, there is a lack of information on the evolution of these programs, their characteristics, and associated outcomes in Latin America. We aimed to characterize the geographical distribution of CR centers, their operational characteristics, their Phase II and III therapeutic offerings, and their main clinical results in Latin American countries.This was a multinational survey-based registry involving 31 countries invited to participate through cardiac rehabilitation specialists designated as "sentinels", national cardiology societies/associations, previous registries, professional networks, and an Inter-American Society of Cardiology (SIAC) campaign. The survey consisted of 66 variables divided into 4 domains: general characteristics, program structure, offerings, and outcomes.Eighteen of the 31 countries responded, with 256 of 320 programs participating, representing an 80.0% response rate; 71.5% of these were private centers. No formal CR was identified in 13 countries. There were 43,956 patients seen annually across the 256 centers, resulting in an estimated average of 172 patients per center/year. Due to their population density, Mexico, Brazil, Argentina, and Colombia are the countries that serve the largest number of patients and have the smallest coverage gap. CR delivery is heterogeneous in terms of monitoring, delivery, and referral pathways. Barriers to access are primarily financial and related to transportation, rather than a lack of access or patient comorbidities. Phase II programs are characterized by being mostly concurrent and short, but with a high volume of patients, and are heavily based on educational care strategies. Strengths include the emergency medical system, interdisciplinarity, inclusion of diverse heart conditions, back-referral systems, and center-reported favorable clinical results, especially in cardiorespiratory and physical fitness, the psycho-emotional sphere, and risk factor control. Adherence to Phase III was 57.3 ± 24.4%.CR capacity across LA remains heterogeneous, highlighting significant disparities in access and delivery across countries, with substantial gaps in referral and coverage. However, there is an expanded inclusion of various cardiovascular conditions, a comprehensive level of interdisciplinarity, professionalization, safety, and reported effectiveness in Phase II. These findings provide actionable data for health systems planning and the expansion of CR services in the region.Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Inc.

llm_summary: Researchers examined cardiac rehabilitation centers, which are medical facilities that help heart patients recover through exercise and education programs, across Latin America to understand how these services are distributed and how well they work. The study surveyed cardiac rehabilitation specialists across 31 countries in the region, and 256 centers from 18 countries responded, providing information about their operations, the types of programs they offered, and the results they achieved with patients. The researchers found that while cardiac rehabilitation services exist in most countries, they are unevenly distributed, with most centers being privately owned and serving an average of 172 patients per year, and that financial costs and transportation difficulties are the main barriers preventing people from accessing these programs. The study showed that these rehabilitation centers are effective at improving patients' heart and lung fitness, emotional well-being, and control of risk factors like high blood pressure and cholesterol, though only about 57 percent of patients continued with longer-term programs. The findings suggest that Latin American countries need to work on expanding and improving access to cardiac rehabilitation services, particularly in areas where coverage is limited, while building on the strengths that already exist in the region's medical systems.

title: Machine learning-assisted plasma PEA proteomics enables differential diagnosis of melancholic depression and bipolar disorder.
abstract: Differentiating bipolar disorder (BD) from major depressive disorder (MDD) remains a critical unmet need in psychiatry due to overlapping clinical presentations and the absence of reliable biological markers. In this study, we assessed the capacity of multivariate machine learning models to accurately differentiate BD from MDD with melancholic features using plasma proteomic profiles obtained via Proximity Extension Assay (PEA) technology. A total of 67 participants were included (23 BD, 20 MDD, and 24 HC), and plasma protein expression was assessed using the Olink Target 96 Neurology panel. Differential proteomic analysis revealed distinct disorder-specific expression patterns, identifying 21 differentially expressed proteins in BD versus MDD, 18 in BD versus healthy controls, and 7 in MDD versus healthy controls. Using a stepwise feature reduction strategy, machine learning models were trained on three feature sets comprising all proteins, the top 20 most informative proteins, and the top 5 most beneficial proteins, and evaluated across BD-MDD, BD-HC, and MDD-HC classification tasks using five algorithms. For BD-MDD discrimination, the Random Forest model achieved the highest performance when trained on the top 5 protein set (LXN, HAGH, MATN3, PLXNB1, and CTSC), yielding an AUC of 0.905, with similarly strong performance observed using the top 20 protein set. Feature importance analysis highlighted proteins involved in neurodevelopmental processes, immune regulation, and extracellular matrix organization. Overall, these findings demonstrate that integrating plasma proteomics with machine learning enables robust differentiation between BD and MDD with melancholic features, supporting the development of scalable and biologically informed diagnostic tools for precision psychiatry.Copyright © 2026. llm_summary: Doctors struggle to tell the difference between bipolar disorder, a condition with extreme mood swings, and major depressive disorder with melancholic features, a severe form of depression, because the two conditions look very similar even though they need different treatments. Researchers studied 67 people including those with bipolar disorder, those with severe depression, and healthy people by measuring 96 different proteins in their blood using a technology called Proximity Extension Assay, which detects tiny amounts of proteins in blood samples. The scientists found that people with bipolar disorder had distinctly different protein patterns compared to those with depression, and they used computer programs trained to recognize these patterns to sort people into the correct diagnosis group. When the computer models focused on just the five most important proteins, they could correctly identify whether someone had bipolar disorder or depression about 90 percent of the time, which is a very high level of accuracy. This research suggests that a simple blood test measuring specific proteins could one day help doctors quickly and accurately diagnose whether a patient has bipolar disorder or depression, leading to better and faster treatment decisions.

title: Endovascular treatment of an anterior condylar confluence cerebrospinal fluid-venous fistula.
abstract: Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF)-venous fistulas are an increasingly recognized source of spontaneous intracranial hypotension, for which endovascular embolization has emerged as an effective treatment option.1-3 Advances in diagnostic imaging have improved detection of CSF-venous fistulas throughout the cervical, thoracic, and lumbar spine; however, identification of lesions at the cranial and caudal extremes of the spine remains challenging.4 In video 1, we present the novel case of an anterior condylar confluence CSF-venous fistula arising from a hypoglossal canal nerve root sleeve diverticulum. We demonstrate the diagnostic evaluation, preprocedural planning, and transvenous embolization of the fistula using the pressure cooker technique, highlighting key technical considerations for navigating this uncommon venous anatomy. Finally, we review the patient's postprocedural course and imaging findings demonstrating radiographic resolution of spontaneous intracranial hypotension.neurintsurg;jnis-2026-026136v1/V1F1V1Video 1Endovascular embolization of a cerebrospinal fluid-venous fistula arising from a hypoglossal canal nerve root sleeve diverticulum using a transvenous pressure cooker technique.© Author(s) (or their employer(s)) 2026. llm_summary: Cerebrospinal fluid-venous fistulas, which are abnormal connections between the fluid surrounding the brain and spinal cord and blood vessels, are an increasingly recognized cause of spontaneous intracranial hypotension, a condition where pressure around the brain drops dangerously low. Doctors have improved their ability to find these fistulas in various parts of the spine using better imaging techniques, but fistulas located at the very top or bottom of the spine near the skull remain difficult to detect and treat. In this case report, researchers presented a novel example of a fistula at the anterior condylar confluence, a specific location at the base of the skull, which they successfully treated using an endovascular embolization procedure, a minimally invasive technique where doctors navigate catheters through blood vessels to seal off the abnormal connection. The doctors used a special technique called the pressure cooker method to carefully navigate the complex blood vessel anatomy in this rare location and successfully close the fistula. After the procedure, imaging scans showed that the patient's spontaneous intracranial hypotension had resolved, demonstrating that this endovascular approach can be an effective treatment option for this.

title: Transcatheter vs Surgical Replacement of Degenerated Bioprosthetic Aortic Valve: A Meta-Analysis of Propensity-Score-Matched Studies.
abstract: Degeneration of bioprosthetic aortic valves is a common late complication. While redo surgical aortic valve replacement (redo-SAVR) has traditionally been the standard of care, transcatheter valve-in-valve implantation (ViV-TAVR) has emerged as a less invasive alternative. This meta-analysis aimed to compare outcomes between ViV-TAVR and redo-SAVR using propensity-score-matched studies.A systematic search of Cochrane CENTRAL, Scopus, MEDLINE (via PubMed) Embase, and Scopus was conducted from inception through to 1 September 2024. Propensity-score matched cohort studies comparing ViV-TAVR and redo-SAVR were included. Risk ratios (RRs) and mean differences (MDs) or standardised mean differences (SMD), as appropriate, were pooled using a random-effects model.Thirteen propensity score-matched studies encompassing 16,223 patients (8,463 ViV-TAVR; 7,760 redo-SAVR) with a weighted mean follow-up of 16.6 months were included. Compared to redo-SAVR, ViV-TAVR was associated with significantly lower short-term all-cause mortality (RR: 0.47; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.34-0.66; p<0.0001), major bleeding (RR: 0.45; 95% CI: 0.33-0.59), acute kidney injury (RR: 0.56; 95% CI: 0.38-0.84), and shorter hospital stay (SMD: -0.79; 95% CI: -1.00 to -0.57). ViV-TAVR was also associated with a significantly lower incidence of new-onset atrial fibrillation (RR: 0.22; 95% CI: 0.13-0.37) but higher post-procedural mean transvalvular gradients (SMD: 0.45; 95% CI: 0.20-0.69). No significant differences were observed in 1- or ≥2-year mortality, stroke/transient ischaemic attack, myocardial infarction, permanent pacemaker implantation, or early readmission. Results remained consistent across sensitivity and subgroup analyses.ViV-TAVR offers significant short-term benefits over redo-SAVR, including lower early mortality and shorter hospitalisation. Long-term clinical outcomes remain comparable, while postprocedural mean gradients are higher after ViV-TAVR, underscoring the need for randomised trials and individualised patient selection to guide treatment decisions for degenerated bioprosthetic valves.Copyright © 2026 Australian and New Zealand Society of Cardiac and Thoracic Surgeons (ANZSCTS) and the Cardiac Society of Australia and New Zealand (CSANZ). llm_summary: When heart valve replacements made from animal tissue wear out over time, doctors traditionally perform another surgery to replace them, but a newer less invasive procedure using a catheter (a thin tube) to place a new valve inside the old one has become an alternative option. Researchers combined results from thirteen previous studies that carefully matched patients between the two treatment approaches to compare how well each method worked for people with worn-out biological heart valves. The catheter-based procedure resulted in significantly better short-term outcomes, including lower death rates, less bleeding, shorter hospital stays, and fewer cases of irregular heartbeat compared to repeat surgery. However, both approaches showed similar results over longer follow-up periods of one to two years or more, though the catheter procedure did leave slightly higher pressure gradients across the valve, meaning the blood flow through the new valve was not quite as smooth. These findings suggest that the catheter-based approach offers real advantages in the immediate recovery period, but doctors need more large-scale randomized trials to determine which patients benefit most from each treatment option.

title: Codon bias variation in Staphylococcus aureus.
abstract: Staphylococcus aureus causes a multiplicity of human diseases acquired in community and healthcare settings alike around the globe. While most studies focus on coding changes to assess genome evolution and study genetic adaptation, interrogation of silent mutations in the form of synonymous codon usage bias is less well-studied. As such, understanding of patterns in codon bias at the gene and genome levels, and how codon bias impacts protein expression in S. aureus remains incomplete.The codon bias of 2,565 protein encoding genes from NCTC 8325 was queried against all publicly available closed S. aureus genomes. Using public BioSample data, genomes were sorted by disease state, submitting institution, and collection site. Codon bias was assessed at the level of gene and genome using the codon adaptation index (CAI), calculated using 30S and 50S ribosomal genes. Gene set enrichment analysis was applied to determine associations between physiological functions, CAI gene scores, and interquartile ranges. CAI scores were also compared to an in vitro S. aureus proteomics database to correlate codon bias and protein expression.CAI scores varied within and between isolates at the gene and genome levels. Genes with ribosome-associated functions were most enriched among high CAI genes, and had low CAI interquartile ranges (IQR), suggesting selective pressure to maintain high expression of these genes across all S. aureus isolates. Genome sequences submitted by Aga Khan University Hospital, Nairobi, Kenya were most different from others. For the LAC USA 300 strain, CAI and protein expression were moderately positively correlated (cor = 0.534, p < 2.2e-16).Codon bias in S. aureus was shown to vary between gene, and to be a source of genetic variation between isolates; CAI and in vitro protein expression were positively correlated.Copyright: © 2026 O’Connor et al. llm_summary: Researchers examined how Staphylococcus aureus, a common bacteria that causes serious infections in hospitals and communities, uses different versions of genetic instructions to make proteins, which had not been thoroughly studied before. The team analyzed the genetic code from over 2,500 genes across many different strains of this bacteria to see how much variation existed in the way genes were written, even when they produced the same protein. They found that genes responsible for making ribosomes, which are the structures that build proteins inside cells, were written in a very consistent way across all bacterial strains, suggesting that nature strongly favors keeping these genes highly active. The researchers also discovered that the way genes were written correlated with how much protein was actually produced in laboratory tests, meaning that genetic code choices do influence protein levels in this bacteria. These findings suggest that codon bias, or the preference for certain genetic code variations, is an important source of genetic differences between bacterial strains and could help explain how different strains of Staphylococcus aureus adapt and survive in different environments.

title: Measuring Radiologist Workload After AI Triage in Breast Cancer Screening.
abstract: Artificial intelligence triage can sharply reduce the number of human readings in breast cancer screening. Reading count, however, does not show how much radiologist time is saved or whether work shifts to arbitration, consensus, or other tasks. We propose a session-level reporting standard based on total active human interpretation minutes per 1000 women screened, work shifted elsewhere in the pathway, and diagnostic outcomes, together with a matched-session design to measure these effects directly.Copyright © 2026 The Association of University Radiologists.
