llm_summary: Heart failure, a condition where the heart cannot pump blood effectively, affects many people and causes serious health problems, yet current medications do not completely solve the issue for all patients. Researchers designed a carefully controlled experiment to test a new medical device called the Edwards APTURE shunt system, which creates a small opening between the left upper heart chamber and a nearby vein to help reduce pressure buildup in the heart. The study enrolled about one hundred symptomatic heart failure patients who were randomly assigned to either receive the new shunt device or a fake procedure, with neither the patients nor the doctors evaluating them knowing which group they were in. The main goals were to measure whether the device was safe after thirty days and whether it reduced the pressure in the heart during exercise after six months, with additional measurements taken over five years to track long-term effects. This trial represents an important step toward finding new treatment options for heart failure patients whose symptoms persist despite taking current medications.

title: Circumscribed Meningeal Melanocytic Neoplasms: CNS WHO Grade, Molecular Profile, and Clinical Outcomes.
abstract: Circumscribed meningeal melanocytic neoplasms (CMMNs) represent a spectrum of rare central nervous system (CNS) tumors. Knowledge of their clinical behavior and molecular correlates remains limited. In this single-institution retrospective study, we analyzed 31 patients (14 male, 17 female; median age, 59 years) diagnosed with CMMN between 2004 and 2025. In this patient cohort, based on the current World Health Organization Central Nervous System Tumor Classification (WHO CNS5) criteria, the majority of cases (18, 58.1%) fell into the intermediate-grade melanocytic tumor (IMT) category based on histology, with either increased mitotic activity, CNS invasion, or both; 7 (22.6%) were melanocytomas, 5 (16.1%) melanomas, and 1 (3.2%) indeterminate case because of limited tissue. By next-generation sequencing, mutations were identified in GNAQ/GNA11 in 21/24 cases, BAP1 in 5/23 (2 IMT, 3 melanoma), EIF1AX in 9/21 (1 melanocytoma, 8 IMT), and SF3B1 in 3/23 (2 IMT, 1 melanoma). Primary sites were spinal (20), posterior fossa (6), and supratentorial (5). During follow-up, progression was observed in 5/6 melanocytomas, 9/13 IMTs, and 4/5 melanomas, suggesting a high frequency of progression across all groups. Two-year progression-free survival was 83.3% (95% confidence interval [CI], 53.5%-100.0%) for melanocytoma, 55.9% (95% CI, 26.7%-85.2%) for IMT, and 25.0% (95% CI, 0.0%-67.4%) for melanoma. Five-year overall survival (OS) was 80.0% (95% CI, 44.9%-100.0%) for melanocytoma, 65.3% (95% CI, 37.0%-93.6%) for IMT, and 0.0% for melanoma. OS was significantly worse in melanoma compared with melanocytoma (p = 0.002). BAP1 mutation correlated with worse OS (hazard ratio 8.73, p = 0.006). Upfront maximal safe resection appeared to be associated with improved outcomes in selected patients, whereas radiotherapy and systemic therapy did not demonstrate clear additional benefit in this cohort. In summary, our study shows that all CMMNs, irrespective of grade, have a high propensity to recur and melanoma histology and BAP1 mutation are associated with significantly worse OS.© 2026 The Author(s). llm_summary: Researchers examined a rare group of brain and spinal cord tumors called circumscribed meningeal melanocytic neoplasms, which are growths that develop in the protective membranes surrounding the nervous system and contain melanin-producing cells. In this study, doctors reviewed medical records and tissue samples from 31 patients treated between 2004 and 2025, classifying the tumors by grade and looking for genetic mutations that might explain why some tumors behave more aggressively than others. The results showed that most patients had intermediate-grade tumors, and genetic testing revealed that mutations in specific genes like GNAQ, GNA11, and BAP1 were common, with BAP1 mutations being linked to worse survival outcomes. All three tumor types showed a high tendency to come back after treatment, with melanoma patients having the poorest survival rates at five years, while patients who had surgery to remove as much of the tumor as safely possible had better outcomes than those who received radiation or drug therapy. These findings suggest that doctors should prioritize complete surgical removal when possible and that patients with BAP1 mutations may need closer monitoring and more aggressive treatment strategies.

title: Evidence for a tubular basement membrane-cilia connection in autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease pathogenesis.
abstract: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD), mainly driven by pathogenic variants in PKD1 and PKD2, is the most common inherited cause of kidney failure. Details of ADPKD pathogenesis are incompletely resolved, but primary cilia are an integral component. There is also evidence for changes to the tubular basement membrane (TBM) in early disease. In this issue of the JCI, Mazloum and colleagues link cilia-dependent, PKD1-mediated regulation of the TBM to ADPKD pathogenesis. Using in vivo, ex vivo, tubule-on-chip, and cellular models of ADPKD, they connect cilia-dependent tubule dilation and TBM thinning to early-stage cystogenesis. Moreover, they identify a cilia-dependent TBM remodeling expression signature in affected tubules and suggest that PC1 loss compromises TBM stiffness. By integrating roles for cilia at the apical membrane and extracellular matrix at the basolateral membrane in cystogenesis, this work highlights the TBM as an additional area for investigation of therapeutic and biomarker discovery in ADPKD.

llm_summary: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease, a common inherited condition that causes kidney failure, is mainly caused by mutations in two genes called PKD1 and PKD2, and scientists have long known that tiny hair-like structures on kidney cells called cilia play an important role in how the disease develops. Researchers led by Mazloum and colleagues used multiple laboratory approaches including living animal models, tissue samples, miniature kidney tubes grown in the lab, and individual cells to study how the loss of a protein called PC1 affects both the cilia and the basement membrane, which is a thin supportive layer surrounding kidney tubules. They discovered that when PC1 is missing, the cilia cannot properly control the basement membrane, leading to the membrane becoming thinner and weaker, which then causes the kidney tubules to expand and form cysts, the hallmark of this disease. This research suggests that the basement membrane is just as important as the cilia in understanding how polycystic kidney disease develops, opening up new possibilities for doctors to find better treatments and develop tests to detect the disease earlier. title: LSD1-mediated demethylation of the DNA damage response factor ATM promotes senescence and organ aging.
abstract: Aging occurs heterogeneously across organs, leading to progressive tissue dysfunction. Cellular senescence is a stress response triggered by age-associated insults, yet the mechanisms regulating senescence and organ aging remain incompletely understood. Here, we defined a role for lysine-specific demethylase 1 (LSD1) in DNA damage-mediated senescence and organ aging. LSD1 was upregulated in aged organs and senescent cells. In response to natural aging or ionizing radiation-induced DNA damage, LSD1 interacted with and demethylated ATM at lysine 3,016, as confirmed using a newly generated ATM-K3016me antibody. This modification sustained ATM phosphorylation, amplified DNA damage signaling, and delayed checkpoint recovery, promoting senescence and organ aging. Inhibition of LSD1 accelerated ATM dephosphorylation via WIP1, enhanced DNA repair, reduced senescence and DNA damage, and prevented irradiation-induced hair graying. Elimination of senescent cells with senolytics reduced LSD1 protein in aged organs, indicating a feedback loop between LSD1 and senescence. Mechanistically, LSD1 underwent autophagosome-lysosome degradation through interaction with LC3 and Beclin1, and autophagy impairment during DNA damage contributed to LSD1 accumulation in senescent cells. This study revealed LSD1 as a key regulator of DNA damage-induced senescence and organ aging and suggested that targeting LSD1 may attenuate senescence, delay organ aging, and prevent hair graying.

llm_summary: Researchers examined how organs age at different rates and how cells stop dividing and functioning properly as we get older, a process called senescence. They discovered that a protein called LSD1 becomes more active in aging organs and damaged cells, where it removes chemical tags from another protein called ATM that normally helps cells respond to DNA damage. When LSD1 removes these tags, it keeps ATM active longer than it should, which prevents cells from repairing their DNA and recovering from damage, ultimately pushing them into senescence and accelerating aging. By blocking LSD1 in experiments, the researchers were able to speed up DNA repair, reduce senescent cells, and even prevent hair graying caused by radiation exposure. These findings suggest that targeting LSD1 could be a potential strategy to slow down aging and reduce age-related diseases in the future.

title: Radiotherapy for the Treatment of Peyronie Disease (Induratio Penis Plastica): An American Radium Society (ARS) Appropriate Use Criteria (AUC).
abstract: To critically analyze the current evidence for the use of radiotherapy in the treatment of Peyronie Disease (PD).A systematic review of the literature was designed using the Population, Intervention, Comparator, Outcome, Timing and Study Design (PICOTS) framework and was assessed using Cochrane and PRISMA methodology. Eligible studies included prospective and retrospective studies published between January 1, 1970 and June 24, 2026. Clinical variant cases were developed as examples to illustrate practical applications of consensus recommendations. RAND-UCLA consensus methodology (modified Delphi) was used to rate the appropriateness of the treatment options.Evidence to support the use of radiotherapy treatment of PD is limited by poor quality evidence, which is based on older studies, heterogenous patient cohorts, inconsistent radiation dose fractionation schedules, and lack of objective measurable outcomes and long-term follow-up. Data suggests that radiotherapy may result in faster resolution of pain for patients with acute-phase PD; however, this observation does not take into account the possibility that any improvement may be due to the natural disease course as some patients experience spontaneous symptom resolution. Radiotherapy is not useful in the treatment of erectile dysfunction or penile deformity or in chronic-phase PD.Current literature contains insufficient evidence to recommend the routine use of RT for the treatment of PD. llm_summary: Peyronie Disease is a condition where scar tissue forms in the penis, causing pain and deformity, and doctors have explored whether radiation therapy might help treat it. Researchers reviewed all available studies published since 1970 using a systematic method to evaluate the quality of evidence and gather expert opinions through a consensus process called a modified Delphi technique. The evidence they found was weak and based on older studies with inconsistent methods, but it suggested that radiation therapy might help reduce pain in the early stages of the disease, though this improvement could simply be due to the disease naturally getting better on its own. Radiation therapy was found to be ineffective for treating erectile dysfunction, penile deformity, or the chronic long-term phase of Peyronie Disease. The researchers concluded that there is not enough reliable evidence to recommend radiation therapy as a standard treatment for Peyronie Disease and that it should only be used within controlled research studies to gather better information.

title: Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery and Change in the AI-ECG-Derived Biological-Age Gap: A Longitudinal Cohort Study.
abstract: Obesity is associated with accelerated aging, yet whether metabolic and bariatric surgery (MBS) can reverse or attenuate this process, as measured by the artificial intelligence-electrocardiogram (AI-ECG)-derived age gap, remains uncertain.We retrospectively studied 2,380 adults who underwent primary MBS from 2008 to 2023 and contributed 6,149 ECG observations. The outcome, δage, was AI-ECG-predicted age minus chronological age. Linear mixed-effects models used continuous time with a clinically prespecified 1-year knot and decomposed weight into between-person and within-person components. Secondary analyses evaluated alternative adiposity measures, observed ECG-age normalization, exploratory mediation, and mortality.Median preoperative δage was 3.86 years (IQR, - 1.30 to 9.03), and 69.6% had δage > 0. δage changed by + 0.275 years/year during the first postoperative year (95% CI, - 0.187 to 0.738; P=.244) and by - 0.192 years/year thereafter (95% CI, - 0.303 to - 0.081; P=.001). The piecewise model was not superior to a linear model (P=.093). Higher between-person mean weight was associated with higher δage (+ 0.548 years per 10 kg; P<.001), whereas within-person weight change was not (+ 0.117 years per 10 kg; P=.084). Baseline, observed postoperative nadir, and maximum BMI were positively associated with δage; %EWL and observed weight regain were not. The exploratory indirect effect through weight change was near zero (ACME, + 0.0008 years; P=.814). Among 1,657 patients with baseline δage > 0, 335 (20.2%) had an observed δage ≤ 0 during follow-up.MBS was associated with a modest late decline in AI-ECG-derived δage. llm_summary: Obesity causes people's bodies to age faster than their actual years, but doctors wanted to know if weight loss surgery could slow down or reverse this accelerated aging process. Researchers studied nearly 2,400 people who had metabolic and bariatric surgery (a procedure that reduces stomach size to help with weight loss) between 2008 and 2023, using heart rhythm recordings and artificial intelligence to measure biological age compared to actual age. The results showed that after the first year following surgery, patients experienced a modest slowing of biological aging, with their biological age gap decreasing by about 0. 2 years per year, though the overall improvement was small. The study found that how much someone weighed overall mattered more for biological aging than how much weight they actually lost after surgery, suggesting that maintaining a lower weight is more important than the weight loss process itself.

title: Hemodynamic-Guided Nutrition Support in Pediatric Congenital Heart Disease.
abstract: Children with congenital heart disease (CHD) are at high risk of malnutrition, feeding difficulties and altered body composition beyond infancy. Nutritional decisions are often based on cardiac anatomy. Although anatomy alone does not capture differences in metabolic demand, mesenteric perfusion and feeding intolerance. This review presents physiology-based framework to guide nutritional support in pediatric CHD care pathway.Recent evidence favors early enteral feeding when hemodynamically appropriate, prioritizing human milk in high-risk infants, standardizing perioperative feeding protocols, assessment beyond weight alone and early attention to oral feeding skills. Long term concern includes micronutrition deficiency, protein losing enteropathy, sarcopenia, obesity and feeding difficulties. Some evidence remains unclear in several areas including exact calorie and protein goal, hemodynamic feeding threshold, weight loss medications in pediatric CHD. Five hemodynamic categories (systemic hypoperfusion, global hypoxia, pulmonary over circulation, mixing lesions, and single-ventricle physiology) may providea practical way to guide nutrition decisions than anatomic diagnosis alone. Matching feeding strategy to mesenteric perfusion, metabolic demand, and complication risk may improve consistency of care but pediatric-specific prospective studies stratified by hemodynamic physiology with patient-centered endpoints are needed.© 2026. llm_summary: Children born with heart defects often struggle with proper nutrition and feeding, which can lead to poor growth and muscle loss even after infancy. Researchers reviewed current evidence and created a framework based on how well blood is flowing through the body rather than just looking at the type of heart defect a child has, since blood flow patterns better explain what a child's body actually needs. The review found that feeding babies early through the stomach or intestines when their heart is stable enough, using breast milk when possible, and paying attention to how well they can eat by mouth produces better results than following nutrition plans based only on heart anatomy. The researchers identified five different patterns of blood flow problems in children with heart defects and suggested that matching feeding plans to each child's specific blood flow pattern, metabolic needs, and risk of feeding problems could lead to more consistent and effective care. More research studies focused specifically on children with heart defects and involving families in treatment decisions are needed to determine the exact amounts of calories and protein these children need and to identify the best time to start feeding them.

title: Vancomycin-Loaded Mesh Reduces Staphylococcal Infection in a Murine Extensor Mechanism Reconstruction Model.
abstract: Infection following extensor mechanism reconstruction (EMR) with Marlex mesh (C.R. Bard) is devastating and limb-threatening. The purpose of this study was to evaluate whether vancomycin-loaded mesh reduces staphylococcal infection in a murine EMR model.Mouse-sized, 8-layer mesh constructs were fabricated to simulate clinical reconstruction and soaked in a vancomycin solution (50 mg/mL) for in vitro and in vivo testing. Three methicillin-resistant clinical isolates from human periprosthetic Staphylococcus aureus, Staphylococcus epidermidis, and Staphylococcus lugdunensis knee infections were evaluated. In vitro testing assessed vancomycin loading capacity, mechanical properties, antibacterial activity, and inhibition of biofilm formation. For in vivo experiments, plain or vancomycin-loaded mesh was implanted into C57BL/6 mouse extensor mechanisms, which were intraoperatively contaminated with 1 of the 3 study isolates (5 per group). Mesh and surrounding tissue were harvested for quantitative culture on postoperative day 9.For all 3 isolates, vancomycin-loaded mesh produced zones of inhibition and exhibited antibacterial activity through at least 3 days in vitro (p < 0.0001). Mechanical testing revealed that loading mesh with vancomycin did not negatively impact tensile strength, hysteresis, or suture pull-through properties. In vitro testing of inhibition of biofilm formation demonstrated reduced colony-forming units 6 hours after inoculation, which remained low throughout the 9-day experimental period (p < 0.05 for all isolates). In vivo, vancomycin-loaded mesh reduced bacterial burden on mesh and in surrounding tissue by >3 log10 compared with plain mesh for all 3 isolates (p < 0.01 for both mesh and tissue).Vancomycin-loaded mesh provided in vitro antibacterial activity without compromising mesh mechanical properties and reduced staphylococcal infection in a murine EMR model. Further work is needed to evaluate translational potential and safety before clinical application.Mesh-associated infection after EMR is devastating and difficult to treat. These preclinical findings suggest that local vancomycin delivery may serve as an adjunct to systemic prophylaxis, warranting further study before clinical use.Copyright © 2026 by The Journal of Bone and Joint Surgery, Incorporated.

llm_summary: Infections following surgery to repair the extensor mechanism, which is the system of tendons and muscles that straightens the knee, can be devastating and threaten limb function, making prevention critically important. Researchers tested whether mesh coated with vancomycin, an antibiotic, could reduce dangerous bacterial infections caused by common staph bacteria in a mouse model that mimicked human knee surgery. The vancomycin-coated mesh successfully killed bacteria and prevented biofilm formation, which is a protective layer that bacteria create to resist treatment, while maintaining the mesh's strength and ability to hold stitches. In the mouse surgeries, the antibiotic-coated mesh reduced bacterial growth by more than a thousand-fold compared to plain mesh, suggesting it could work as an additional protective measure alongside standard antibiotic treatments. Although these early results are promising, the researchers emphasized that more testing is needed to ensure the treatment is safe and effective before it can be used in actual patients.

title: Feasibility, Safety, and Efficacy of Pulsed Field Ablation for Ventricular Arrhythmias: Insights From a Large Health System Registry in the United States.
abstract: Pulsed field ablation (PFA) is an emerging non-thermal ablation modality with proven safety in atrial arrhythmia ablation. However, data on its performance for ventricular arrhythmias (VA) remain limited.To evaluate the feasibility, safety, and efficacy of PFA for complex VA in a multicenter real-world US registry.This retrospective study included consecutive patients undergoing PFA for ventricular tachycardia (VT) or premature ventricular contractions (PVCs) at three Mayo Clinic centers (April 2024 to July 2025). The primary feasibility outcome was the successful delivery of PFA lesions to the intended target substrate. Primary efficacy outcomes included acute procedural success; sustained VT recurrence requiring implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) shocks or multiple antitachycardia pacing therapies; and ≥ 80% reduction in PVC burden. Safety outcomes included procedural complications, valvular function, thromboembolic events, renal function, and conduction disturbances.Twenty-six patients were included (13 PVC, 13 VT). Acute success was achieved in all VT ablations (69.2% complete; 30.8% partial) and in 92.3% of PVC ablations. Complications occurred in 11.5% of patients (transient LBBB [n = 1] and vascular complications [n = 2]). No thromboembolic events, intracardiac thrombus, or acute kidney injury were observed. Lesions near the mitral valve apparatus did not worsen mitral regurgitation, including in patients with pre-existing valve disease. After a median follow-up of 365 days, one patient experienced VT recurrence requiring ICD shocks. Estimated recurrence-free survival after VT ablation was 61.5% at 12 months; 58.3% of PVC patients achieved ≥ 80% burden reduction.PFA for VA appears feasible and acutely effective, with a low rate of procedure-related complications. While acute success was high, long-term outcomes were acceptable for VT ablation and relatively modest for PVC ablation, highlighting the need for continued refinement of technology and energy-delivery strategies. title: Financial Payments From Drug Manufacturers to Oncologists and Use of Guideline-Preferred Cancer Treatments.
abstract: Payments from the drug industry influence physicians' prescribing decisions. Whether industry payments affect the likelihood that patients receive the guideline-preferred treatment for their cancer is unknown.We used fee-for-service Medicare claims to identify patients with an incident cancer diagnosis from 2014 to 2020. We used the National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN) guidelines to identify cancers with variation in clinical benefit among recommended treatment options and to identify the preferred treatment as of each patient's diagnosis date. The primary exposure was drug industry payments received by the patient's medical oncologist during the year before diagnosis, categorized as no payment, payment for preferred treatment only, payment for nonpreferred treatment only, or payment for both. The primary outcome was receipt of a preferred treatment.There were 14 cancer scenarios comprising 15,607 patients; 60.2% were managed by oncologists who received no payment, 21.9% by oncologists who received payment for guideline-preferred treatment, 30.6% by oncologists who received payment for nonpreferred treatment, and 12.7% by oncologists who received both payment types. Among patients whose oncologist received no payments, 41.6% received payments for preferred treatment versus 51.5% of those whose oncologist received payments for guideline-preferred treatment only, 34.7% of those whose oncologist received payments for nonpreferred treatment only, and 42.9% of those whose oncologist received payments for both payment types. After adjustment, payment for guideline-preferred treatment was associated with a greater likelihood of receiving preferred treatment (risk ratio [RR] = 1.06 [95% CI, 1.01 to 1.13]) and payment for nonpreferred treatment was associated with a lower likelihood (RR, 0.93 [95% CI, 0.89 to 0.98]). Association magnitude increased as payment dollar value increased.Industry payments were associated with increased use of the promoted cancer treatment, regardless of whether that treatment was guideline-preferred or nonpreferred for a given patient.

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether payments from drug companies to cancer doctors influence which treatments patients receive, since previous studies show that money can affect how doctors prescribe medications. The team looked at Medicare records from 2014 to 2020 for patients newly diagnosed with cancer and compared the treatments they received to the guidelines recommended by the National Comprehensive Cancer Network, which is an organization that sets standards for cancer care. They found that when doctors received money from drug companies promoting guideline-preferred treatments, patients were more likely to receive those recommended treatments, but when doctors received payments for non-preferred treatments, patients were less likely to get the best recommended option. The strength of this effect grew larger as the dollar amounts of the payments increased, suggesting that even modest financial relationships between doctors and drug makers can sway treatment decisions. These findings raise concerns about how industry payments might influence cancer care and suggest that closer monitoring of these financial relationships may be needed to protect patients.

title: Evolving Evidence-Driven Strategies in Cardiogenic Shock Management.
abstract: Although existing guidelines and expert consensus documents provide a general framework for management of cardiogenic shock (CS), a substantial body of evidence has yet emerged which has not been fully incorporated into current recommendations. This State-of-the Art review synthesizes both established and recent literature to provide an updated perspective on contemporary CS management. We review randomized controlled trials and key observational studies evaluating invasive hemodynamic monitoring, pharmacologic therapies, temporary mechanical circulatory support, and structural and valvular interventions. We critically appraise trial design, patient heterogeneity, and methodological limitations that influence interpretation and clinical applicability. Finally, we highlight persistent gaps and ongoing trials that aim to refine risk stratification and treatment strategies. This review provides a comprehensive, up-to-date synthesis of the CS literature and outlines key directions for future research and clinical practice.Copyright © 2026 The Authors. llm_summary: Cardiogenic shock, which occurs when the heart cannot pump enough blood to support the body's needs, is a serious condition that doctors treat using various methods, but current treatment guidelines have not kept up with all the newest research available. Researchers reviewed both established studies and recent findings about how to manage cardiogenic shock, examining different treatment approaches including monitoring blood flow with special catheters, using medications, using temporary mechanical devices to help the heart pump, and performing surgical procedures to fix heart valve problems. The review found that while many treatments show promise, the quality and design of different studies vary widely, and patients with cardiogenic shock are often very different from each other, which makes it harder to know which treatments work best for which people. This comprehensive summary of current evidence helps doctors understand what treatments are most supported by research and identifies areas where better information is still needed to improve patient outcomes. The authors point out that more research is underway to help doctors better predict which patients will do well with certain treatments and to refine which therapies should be used for different types of cardiogenic shock.

title: Spillover Effects of Medicaid Expansion on Insurance Coverage, Diagnosis, and Survival Among Low-Income Older Patients With Cancer.
abstract: Medicaid expansion under the Affordable Care Act primarily benefits adults aged <65 years but may also indirectly benefit individuals aged ≥65 years. This study examines the associations of Medicaid expansion with insurance coverage and cancer outcomes among older patients residing in low-income areas.Using the National Cancer Database, we identified patients aged ≥65 years, newly diagnosed with cancer 2010-2021, and residing in areas with median household income <200% of the federal poverty level. Using the quasi-experimental difference-in-differences design, multivariable models compared dual Medicare-Medicaid enrollment or Medicaid-only coverage, stage at diagnosis, treatment initiation, and 2-year overall survival before and after Medicaid expansion in expansion versus non-expansion states.Our sample included 1,461,540 patients. Dual Medicare-Medicaid or Medicaid-only coverage increased in Medicaid expansion states (10.3%-11.3%) and decreased in Medicaid non-expansion states (9.4%-8.1%), resulting in a net increase of 1.25 percentage points (ppt; 95% CI, 1.02-1.48). Early-stage cancer diagnoses decreased overall, driven by prostate cancer, but declined less in expansion states than in non-expansion states, with a net adjusted relative increase of 1.00 ppt (95% CI, 0.59-1.41). Such protective effects were stronger for lung/bronchus and head and neck cancers. Treatment initiation within 30 days also decreased less in expansion states than non-expansion states, with a net adjusted increase of 0.74 ppt (95% CI, 0.34-1.14). Two-year overall survival increased more in expansion states (58.8%-62.4%) than non-expansion states (59.2%-62.5%), leading to a net increase of 0.70 ppt (95% CI, 0.35-1.04). Such increase was most notable for stage IV, lung/bronchus, kidney, and bladder cancers.Medicaid expansion was associated with increased Medicaid coverage, attenuated declines in early-stage diagnosis and timely treatment initiation, and improved survival among low-income older patients with cancer, highlighting important spillover benefits beyond the target population.

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether Medicaid expansion under the Affordable Care Act, which was designed to help younger adults, also provided indirect benefits to older adults aged sixty-five and above living in low-income areas who were diagnosed with cancer. The study compared cancer outcomes in nearly one and a half million older patients across states that expanded Medicaid coverage with states that did not, looking at insurance enrollment, cancer stage at diagnosis, how quickly treatment started, and survival rates over two years. The results showed that Medicaid expansion led to more older adults having Medicaid coverage, helped catch more cancers at earlier stages, allowed patients to start treatment faster, and improved two-year survival rates compared to states without expansion. These findings suggest that expanding health insurance programs for younger adults can have positive spillover effects that also help older patients with cancer receive better care and live longer. Future research should explore how these insurance coverage improvements translate into better access to cancer treatments and whether similar spillover benefits occur for other age groups and health conditions.

title: Continence Durability for Male Sling Surgery and Subsequent Pelvic Radiation: A Multicenter Analysis.
abstract: To evaluate urinary continence outcomes in males who underwent pelvic radiation therapy (RT) before versus after urethral sling placement.We performed a retrospective study of males undergoing urethral sling placement for stress urinary incontinence at three tertiary centers from 2010 to 2025. Patients with history of pelvic radiation were stratified into two cohorts: sling placement before radiation (pre-RT) and sling placement after radiation (post-RT). The primary outcome was continence durability, assessed by pad use. Social continence was defined as the use of ≤1 pads per day (ppd). Secondary outcomes included International Prostate Symptom Score (IPSS), complications, and salvage surgery.Of 666 males undergoing sling placement, 28 (4.2%) had history of pelvic radiation: 15 (2.3%) pre-RT and 13 (2.0%) post-RT. In the pre-RT cohort, 100% experienced social continence post-sling; however, subsequent radiation resulted in marked deterioration, with social continence declining to 11% and median pad use increasing from 0 to 3 ppd. In the post-RT cohort, 50% of men achieved social continence post-sling. No mesh erosions were observed. Salvage artificial urinary sphincter (AUS) placement was performed in 21% (6/28) of the entire cohort, with no significant difference between the pre-RT and post-RT groups (13% vs. 31%; p = 0.37).In this retrospective cohort, pelvic radiation after sling placement was temporally associated with declining continence in some patients. Both a history of pelvic radiation and the potential future need for radiation should be considered during counseling and selection of surgical treatment for stress urinary incontinence.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Inc. llm_summary: Researchers examined how well a surgical procedure called a urethral sling works for treating urinary leakage in men, particularly when those men also receive radiation therapy to the pelvis area as cancer treatment. The study looked back at medical records from three hospitals between 2010 and 2025, comparing men who had the sling surgery before radiation to those who had it after radiation, tracking how many pads they needed to use daily to stay dry. Men who received the sling before radiation started out completely dry after surgery, but when they later underwent radiation therapy, most of them began leaking again and needed about three pads per day, while men who had radiation first and then received the sling surgery only achieved dryness about half the time. The findings suggest that radiation therapy can significantly damage the results of sling surgery in some patients, so doctors should discuss this risk with men who might need radiation in the future before deciding on this type of surgery. Doctors should consider whether a patient might need radiation therapy when choosing the best treatment option for urinary leakage, as this could affect how well the surgery works over time.

title: Ten-year outcomes of PET-directed salvage nodal radiotherapy and temporary ADT for N1 and M1a hormone-sensitive prostate cancer.
abstract: Evaluate long-term outcomes of PET-directed elective nodal radiotherapy (ENRT) with simultaneous integrated boost (SIB) plus fixed-duration androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) for pelvic and/or para-aortic oligorecurrent hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (HSPC).HSPC patients with PET-detected nodal-only recurrence after curative-intent primary therapy were treated with ENRT (45-50 Gy elective, SIB 50-62.5 Gy), plus ADT (median, 2 years). Outcomes included overall (OS), prostate cancer-specific (PCSS), biochemical relapse-free (BRFS), distant metastasis-free (DMFS), castration-resistant prostate cancer-free (CRPC-FS), and treatment-free survival (TFS), and CTCAE v6.0 toxicity. Multivariable Cox regression explored factors associated with BRFS and DMFS.Ninety-three patients had a median follow-up of 10.0 years. Median PSA at recurrence was 2.7 ng/mL, with two PET-positive nodes; 30% had pelvic-only and 70% common iliac and/or para-aortic involvement. OS at 5/10 years was 95%/77%, and PCSS was 96%/87%. Patients with pelvic-only versus common iliac/para-aortic disease had higher 10-year OS (93% vs 70%, P=0.01) and PCSS (96% vs 83%, P=0.04). At 5/10 years, BRFS was 46%/38%, DMFS 54%/31%, CRPC-FS 79%/55%, TFS 55%/35%. No acute G3 events attributable to ENRT occurred; 10-year G3 GU/GI rates were 4.3%/1.1%. Normal testosterone recovery (>240 ng/dL) reached 51.7% at 5 years. Cox models had c-indices of 0.69 for BRFS and 0.79 for DMFS.Among selected patients in this retrospective cohort, PET-directed ENRT with SIB and predominantly temporary ADT was followed by favorable long-term survival and low observed rates of grade 3 toxicity. These mature outcomes provide long-term benchmarks for patient counseling, while prospective evaluation is needed to establish the long-term benefit of this combined-modality approach in the context of treatment paradigms that have since evolved.Copyright © 2026 The Author(s). title: Timing and trajectory of acute kidney injury predict mortality in alcohol-associated hepatitis: A multinational cohort study.
abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is common in alcohol-associated hepatitis (AH) and associated with poor outcomes, yet the prognostic implications of AKI timing and early renal trajectory remain unclear.In this prospective multicenter cohort from the Global AlcHep Prospective Database, patients with AH were classified as no AKI, prevalent AKI at admission, or incident AKI during hospitalization. The primary outcome was 90-day mortality, using competing-risks regression with liver transplantation as the competing event. A 7-day landmark analysis assessed the prognostic impact of AKI trajectory among prevalent AKI patients.Among 581 patients, 37% had prevalent AKI, and 11% developed incident AKI. The 90-day mortality was 18.2% (11 transplantations, 1.9%). Prevalent AKI was predominantly functional (84%), while incident AKI had a higher proportion of structural injury (44%). Despite lower baseline severity [median mDF 59.8 vs. 69.3 and lower rates of ACLF grade 3 (23.4% vs. 45.3%)], incident AKI conferred mortality of similar magnitude to prevalent AKI (sHR 2.18, 95% CI 1.19-3.99 vs. sHR 1.80, 95% CI 1.02-3.16). Among 7-day survivors (N=457), prevalent AKI without progression had mortality similar to no AKI (sHR 1.27, p=0.52), while prevalent AKI with progression carried the worst prognosis (sHR 3.34, 95% CI 1.44-7.77).Both prevalent and incident AKI independently predict mortality in AH. Incident AKI confers equivalent risk despite lower disease severity and a distinct etiologic profile with higher rates of intrinsic renal injury. Early renal trajectory refines risk beyond baseline AKI status, where absence of progression approximates outcomes of those without AKI, while progressive AKI identifies the highest-risk subgroup.Copyright © 2026 The Author(s). llm_summary: Kidney injury is a common and serious problem in patients with alcohol-related liver disease, but doctors did not fully understand how the timing and progression of this kidney damage affected survival rates. Researchers from multiple hospitals around the world followed 581 patients with alcohol-associated hepatitis, a severe liver condition caused by heavy drinking, and tracked whether they developed kidney injury when admitted to the hospital or during their hospital stay. The study found that 37 percent of patients had kidney injury when they arrived at the hospital while 11 percent developed it later, and importantly, patients who developed kidney injury during hospitalization had similar death rates to those who arrived with kidney injury despite having less severe liver disease overall. Among patients who survived the first week, those whose kidney injury did not get worse had survival rates similar to patients without kidney injury, but those whose kidney injury worsened had the worst outcomes and highest death rates. These findings suggest that doctors should monitor how patients' kidney function changes during the first week of hospitalization, as this early progression pattern is more important for predicting survival than simply knowing whether kidney injury is present.

title: Warmth, Competence, Hope and Belonging at Mayo Clinic: Using Social Science to Improve Hospital Patients' Experience.
abstract: In the aftermath of patient experience challenges during the Covid-19 pandemic, Mayo Clinic surveyed more than 21,000 outpatient medical practice patients. The findings were that, although Mayo Clinic's typical patient experience scores remained high, warmth and competence measures, such as listening, respect, and clear communication, showed opportunities to deepen patient relationships and foster greater feelings of hope and belonging. As a result, Mayo Clinic adopted the social science of warmth and competence as a new framework for improving its relationships with patients. By applying this human social perception lens to the inpatient care environment at its flagship hospital complex in Rochester, MN, frontline staff were empowered to identify overlooked issues, renew collaboration, and implement targeted improvements. Warmth and competence have become an operational framework that guides multidisciplinary teams in identifying practical opportunities to improve the care environment in areas such as quietude, strengthen staff collaboration, and reinforce Mayo Clinic's commitment to patient-centered care. These have contributed to the hospital's increase from a four-star to a five-star rating for patient experience on the Hospital Consumer Assessment of Healthcare Providers and Systems survey in 2025 and 2026.

The survey revealed that while Mayo Clinic's overall patient satisfaction scores were already high, there were opportunities to strengthen how warmth and competence—qualities like listening carefully, showing respect, and communicating clearly—were being delivered to patients. Mayo Clinic then adopted a new framework based on social science research about warmth and competence, training frontline staff to identify overlooked problems and work together to make practical improvements in areas like reducing noise and strengthening teamwork. These targeted changes helped create a care environment where patients felt more hope and belonging, ultimately contributing to the hospital's improvement from a four-star to a five-star patient experience rating on a national healthcare quality survey. This approach demonstrates that hospitals can use insights from social science to transform how they interact with patients and significantly improve the overall experience of receiving care.

title: Therapeutic targeting of cancer-associated fibroblasts with oncolytic virus in preclinical models of intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma.
abstract: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (iCCA) is an aggressive malignancy with limited effective therapies. Treatment resistance is partly due to activated cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs), which induce pro-tumor signaling and formation of a highly fibrotic tumor microenvironment. CAFs exist on a functional spectrum of subtypes and are difficult to target in vivo. Oncolytic viruses (OVs) can destroy pro-tumor CAFs and reduce fibrosis. We hypothesized that OV infection both lyses CAFs and reprograms surviving CAFs toward a less tumorigenic phenotype. Using in vitro models with CAFs from patient-derived xenograft (PDX) and syngeneic tumors, we evaluated the effects of Vaccinia (VV) and vesicular stomatitis viruses (VSV) and found that OVs killed iCCA cells and CAFs, while also reducing pro-tumor CAF signaling. In vivo, subcutaneous PDX and syngeneic models evaluated OV efficacy, tumor architecture, and CAF function. OVs effectively killed iCCA cells and CAFs, alongside a significant reduction of pro-tumorigenic signaling from syngeneic CAFs. Tumor growth abrogation correlated with decreased inflammatory CAF signaling, namely, hepatocyte growth factor (HGF) production. Notably, HGF enhanced OV tropism, while OV infection reduced HGF expression, suggesting a CAF antiviral defense that also limits pro-tumor signaling. These findings suggest a dual cytotoxic and reprogramming role for OVs in the iCCA microenvironment.© 2026 The Author(s).

llm_summary: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma, a type of liver cancer, is difficult to treat because special cells called cancer-associated fibroblasts create an environment that helps tumors grow and resist therapy. Researchers tested whether oncolytic viruses, which are viruses designed to kill cancer cells, could also destroy these problematic fibroblasts and change them into less harmful versions. Using laboratory experiments and animal models with human tumor samples, the team found that two types of viruses successfully killed both the cancer cells and the fibroblasts while reducing the cancer-promoting signals these fibroblasts normally produce. The virus treatment worked especially well because it reduced a specific growth factor called hepatocyte growth factor that the fibroblasts normally make to help tumors survive, and interestingly, this same factor also helped the viruses infect cells more effectively. These results suggest that oncolytic viruses could be a promising new treatment approach for this aggressive cancer because they work in two ways at once: directly killing cancer cells and fibroblasts while also reprogramming the remaining fibroblasts to be less supportive of tumor growth.

title: Periodontitis, Tooth Loss, and Risk of Cognitive Impairment and Dementia: A Systematic Review With Meta-Analysis.
abstract: To systematically review and meta-analyze cohort studies evaluating associations of gingival inflammation, periodontitis, and tooth loss with cognitive decline and incident mild cognitive impairment or dementia.PROSPERO-registered searches of MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library identified cohort studies from inception through October 10, 2025, with a PubMed update on June 24, 2026. Random-effects meta-analyses pooled adjusted hazard ratios (HRs) for dementia/MCI; cognitive function outcomes were summarized qualitatively. Risk of bias (RoB) was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale.Fifty-nine studies met inclusion criteria; 28 contributed to dementia/MCI meta-analyses. Severe periodontitis (HR: 1.16; 95% CI: 1.06-1.27; I2 = 0%; Q-test p = 0.49), periodontitis of unspecified severity (HR: 1.45; 95% CI: 1.21-1.73; I2 = 98%; Q-test p < 0.001), edentulism (HR: 1.26; 95% CI: 1.19-1.33), and low tooth count (HR: 1.27; 95% CI: 1.14-1.42; I2 = 94%; Q-test p < 0.001) were associated with elevated dementia/MCI risk. RoB was low in 31 studies (53%), moderate in 25 (42%), and high in 3 (5%); inadequate confounder adjustment was common. Meta-regression showed stronger estimates for ICD-code periodontitis definitions (fold change (FC) = 1.44 95% CI: 1.04-2.01), older cohorts (FC per year = 1.02 95% CI: 1.00, 1.05), and weaker estimates with lower RoB (FC per NOS star = 0.81 95% CI: 0.73-0.92). Follow-up duration, cohort age, and RoB were not associated with tooth-count estimates.Periodontitis and tooth loss are associated with modestly higher dementia/MCI risk and poorer cognitive function, but heterogeneity, residual confounding, and bias temper causal interpretation. llm_summary: Researchers examined whether gum disease and tooth loss might be connected to memory problems and dementia, which is important because finding preventable risk factors could help protect brain health. The team searched medical databases for long-term studies that followed people over time and tracked whether those with gum disease or missing teeth developed cognitive decline, mild memory problems, or dementia. They found that people with severe gum disease had a sixteen percent higher risk of developing dementia or memory problems, while those who had lost all their teeth had a twenty-six percent higher risk compared to people with healthy teeth and gums. These findings suggest that dental health problems may play a modest role in brain health decline, though the researchers noted that the studies had some limitations and it remains unclear whether treating gum disease would actually prevent dementia. The authors concluded that more rigorous research is needed, including studies that carefully measure thinking ability at the start and test whether treating gum disease can reduce the risk of developing memory problems.

title: Senescent cell heterogeneity in brain aging and neurodegenerative disease.
abstract: Senescent cells in the aging and diseased brain are increasingly recognized as highly heterogeneous catalysts of dysfunction, originating from diverse cell types and characterized by wide-ranging molecular signatures and functional outcomes. Additionally, technological advances in single-cell transcriptomics and mouse modeling have helped reframe senescence from a static fate to a dynamic trajectory that is heavily influenced by evolving environmental cues. In this review, we identify key hubs of heterogeneity in brain cell senescence. We discuss how differences in senescence induction, cell-cycle arrest mechanisms, cell-type biology, and microenvironments contribute to the diverse senescence programs observed in the central nervous system. We also synthesize insights from the recent wave of single-cell transcriptomic studies and discuss how advances in spatial omics technologies could transform our ability to study senescent cells within intact neural circuits. Finally, we argue that integrating multimodal molecular profiling with functional studies in mice will be essential for advancing mechanistic understanding and therapeutic targeting of senescent cells in brain aging and disease.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Inc. llm_summary: Senescent cells, which are aging cells that stop dividing and accumulate in the brain, are now understood to be highly diverse and come from many different types of brain cells, each with unique characteristics and effects on brain function. Researchers reviewed recent advances in single-cell technology, which allows scientists to study individual cells rather than groups of cells, and found that senescence is not a fixed state but rather a dynamic process that changes based on the brain's environment and conditions. The study identified several key sources of variation in how brain cells become senescent, including differences in what triggers the aging process, how cells stop dividing, the specific type of cell involved, and the surrounding cellular environment. Understanding this diversity of senescent cells could help scientists develop better treatments for brain aging and neurodegenerative diseases like Alzheimer's by targeting the specific senescent cells causing damage. The researchers emphasize that combining advanced molecular analysis techniques with functional studies in mice will be necessary to fully understand how senescent cells contribute to brain disease and to create effective therapies.

title: Widespread Loss of Heterozygosity and Endoreduplication in Odontogenic Myxoma: Expanding the Clinicopathologic Spectrum of An Enigmatic Odontogenic Neoplasm.
abstract: Odontogenic myxoma (OM) is an uncommon, locally aggressive odontogenic neoplasm with characteristic histologic and clinico-radiographic features but with potential for histologic overlap with other odontogenic and non-odontogenic entities and a non-specific immunoprofile. Widespread loss of heterozygosity (LOH) has been recently described in rare cases of OM. The aim of this study was to determine whether widespread LOH represents a recurrent molecular signature that can be leveraged for clinical decision-making. Allele-specific copy number variation data from chromosomal microarray were generated from 7 OM, comprising a combined prospective and retrospective cohort. Four tumors arose in the mandible and 3 in the maxilla in patients ranging in age from 18 to 94 years (median: 44), with tumor size ranging from 2.2 to 13.0 cm. Variable amounts of fibrous stroma (odontogenic "fibromyxoma") were present in 4/7 OM, and hypercellularity not typically appreciated in conventional OM was present in 3/7 cases. All OM (7/7) demonstrated widespread LOH, with 5 cases showing a near-haploid/low hypodiploid genomes (multiple monosomies) and 2 cases showing evidence of pseudo-hyperdiploidy due to probable endoreduplication. Both pseudo-hyperdiploid cases were ≥10 cm in size; 1 represented local recurrence. Chromosomes 1 to 3, 6, 9, 11, 13, 15, and 22 demonstrated LOH in ≥75% of cases (chromosomes 1 to 3, 6, and 9 in 100% of cases), while chromosomes 5, 12, 19, and 20 universally retained heterozygosity. Altogether, widespread LOH is a recurrent event in OM and a novel finding in odontogenic pathology, and allele-specific copy number variation analysis can serve as a diagnostic adjunct in challenging cases.Copyright © 2026 Wolters Kluwer Health, LLC. llm_summary: Odontogenic myxoma is a rare tumor that grows in the jaw and is difficult to diagnose because it looks similar to other tumors under a microscope and does not have clear identifying markers. Researchers examined seven tumors from patients ranging in age from 18 to 94 years using a genetic test called chromosomal microarray, which detects missing or extra copies of DNA segments, to see if these tumors shared common genetic patterns. All seven tumors showed widespread loss of heterozygosity, meaning they had lost one copy of genetic material across many chromosomes, with some tumors showing unusual genetic changes like having mostly single copies of chromosomes or evidence of doubling. The two largest tumors, which were at least ten centimeters in size, showed evidence of genetic doubling, and one of these was a tumor that had come back after previous treatment. This discovery suggests that genetic testing for loss of heterozygosity could help doctors more confidently diagnose odontogenic myxoma in confusing cases and may provide insight into how these tumors behave and grow.

title: Association between age at Parkinson's disease onset and divorce: An exploratory analysis from the fox insight cohort.
abstract: BackgroundParkinson's disease (PD) typically presents after age 60; however, approximately 10% of individuals experience early-onset PD (EOPD), with symptoms beginning between ages 21 and 50. Beyond motor and non-motor symptoms, PD can impact personal relationships through stigma, social isolation, and emotional burden. This study aims to examine the influence of PD on relationship outcomes such as divorce or separation.MethodsThis exploratory study analyzed data from the Fox Insight cohort, an online longitudinal research initiative supported by The Michael J. Fox Foundation. We included 470 individuals with self-reported PD who had complete data on marital status ("married" or "divorced") and age at PD onset. Participants were categorized as having EOPD (<50 years) or late-onset PD (≥50 years). Chi-square tests assessed the association between PD onset group and marital status. A binary logistic regression model further evaluated gender and onset age as predictors of marital status in a subset of 330 participants.ResultsA significant association was found between PD onset group and marital status, with a higher divorce rate among the EOPD group (17.5%; 7/40) compared to late-onset PD (6.1%; 26/430) (p = 0.017). Logistic regression revealed no statistically significant predictors, though trends suggested lower odds of divorce in men and those with late-onset PD.ConclusionThis exploratory analysis identified a potential association between early PD onset and higher divorce rates; however, with only 7 events in 40 EOPD participants, this finding is inherently unstable and should be regarded as hypothesis-generating only. Confirmation in larger, longitudinal cohorts is required before any conclusions can be drawn.

llm_summary: Parkinson's disease, a neurological condition affecting movement and other body functions, can strain personal relationships through emotional stress and social challenges, making it important to understand how the disease impacts marriage and family life. Researchers analyzed data from 470 people with Parkinson's disease who participated in an online research study, comparing divorce rates between those who developed the disease before age 50 (early-onset) and those who developed it at age 50 or later (late-onset). The study found that people with early-onset Parkinson's disease had a notably higher divorce rate of 17. 5 percent compared to just 6. 1 percent for those with late-onset disease, suggesting that developing the condition at a younger age may put marriages at greater risk.

title: Periprocedural rescue antiemetic administration during radiologic procedures performed under conscious sedation.
abstract: This study aimed to determine the incidence and clinical predictors of periprocedural rescue antiemetic administration during radiologic procedures performed under conscious sedation.We performed a retrospective review of adult patients who underwent radiologic procedures under conscious sedation with midazolam and/or fentanyl between May 6, 2018, and December 31, 2024. Rescue antiemetics was defined as the use of an antiemetic during the procedure or recovery period. A modified Apfel score (excluding need for postprocedural opioids) was calculated. Logistic regression was used to assess the association of clinical characteristics with the need for rescue antiemetics.Among 21,343 unique patients, 990 (4.64%; 95% confidence interval [CI] 4.34-4.93) were administered a rescue antiemetic. Clinical factors associated with the need for rescue antiemetics included female sex (adjusted odds ratio [OR], 2.31; 95% CI, 1.99-2.67), history of postprocedural nausea and vomiting (OR, 1.99; 95% CI, 1.59-2.48), younger age (OR, 0.84 per decade of life; 95% CI, 0.81-0.88), procedural duration (OR, 1.78 per hour; 95% CI, 1.60-1.99), and fentanyl dose (OR, 1.12 per 25 mcg; 95% CI, 1.07-1.16). Risk increased with higher modified Apfel scores. Duration of recovery was longer among patients who were administered vs not administered a rescue antiemetic (median duration 116 [73, 165] vs 47 [27, 100] minutes, P < 0.001).Rescue antiemetic administration during radiologic procedures with conscious sedation complicates <5% of cases. Risk factors for rescue antiemetics are similar to those for postprocedural nausea and vomiting following general anesthesia.

llm_summary: Researchers examined when patients undergoing imaging procedures with sedation (a state of relaxation and reduced awareness) needed emergency nausea medication to understand what puts them at higher risk. The team reviewed medical records from over twenty-one thousand adult patients who received imaging procedures using sedation drugs between 2018 and 2024, tracking which ones required rescue antiemetic medication (drugs to stop nausea and vomiting) during or after their procedure. About four and a half percent of patients needed rescue nausea medication, and the researchers found that women, younger patients, those who had experienced nausea after procedures before, those undergoing longer procedures, and those receiving higher doses of pain medication were more likely to need it. Patients who received rescue antiemetic medication spent significantly longer in recovery, with a median time of nearly two hours compared to less than one hour for those who did not need the medication. These findings suggest that doctors can use similar risk factors to predict and potentially prevent nausea in patients undergoing imaging procedures with sedation, just as they do for patients receiving full anesthesia during surgery.

title: Japanese subgroup analysis of AQUILA trial: daratumumab vs active monitoring in high-risk smoldering multiple myeloma.
abstract: In the global phase 3 AQUILA trial, daratumumab monotherapy was associated with a significantly lower risk of progression to active multiple myeloma or death than active monitoring in patients with high-risk smoldering multiple myeloma without unexpected safety concerns (NCT03301220).Here, we report a subgroup analysis of Japanese patients from the trial. Among the 28 Japanese patients, 15 and 13 patients received daratumumab and active monitoring, respectively.At the median follow-up of 60.9 months, the median progression-free survival was 59.1 and 24.8 months, respectively, with a hazard ratio of 0.25 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.10-0.65] favoring daratumumab treatment. The overall response rate was 86.7% and 7.7%, with an odds ratio of 78.0 (95% CI: 6.24-974.71). Overall survival data were immature. Grade ≥3 adverse events were observed in five patients (33.3%) treated with daratumumab, which did not lead to treatment discontinuation, and no new safety concerns were noted.In this small-scale exploratory post hoc Japanese subgroup analysis, the efficacy of daratumumab monotherapy was generally comparable to that demonstrated in the global trial population, and no data suggesting new safety concerns were identified. These findings may provide useful information for determining treatment options in Japanese patients with high-risk smoldering multiple myeloma. llm_summary: Researchers examined whether a cancer-fighting drug called daratumumab could help Japanese patients with smoldering multiple myeloma, a blood cancer that has not yet become fully active, by comparing it to simply monitoring patients without treatment. In this study, 28 Japanese patients were divided into two groups, with 15 receiving daratumumab injections and 13 receiving active monitoring over a follow-up period of about five years. The patients who received daratumumab had much better results, with their cancer taking nearly twice as long to progress to active disease compared to those who were only monitored, and about 87 percent of daratumumab patients showed improvement in their condition compared to just 8 percent in the monitoring group. The side effects from daratumumab were manageable, with one-third of treated patients experiencing serious adverse events that did not require stopping treatment and no new safety problems were discovered. These findings suggest that daratumumab could be an effective treatment option for Japanese patients with high-risk smoldering multiple myeloma, though the results come from a small group and larger studies may be needed to confirm these benefits.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Detection of ARIA on MRI During Alzheimer Disease Therapy: Expert Opinion on Responsible Clinical Integration.
abstract: Amyloid-targeted monoclonal antibody therapies have introduced a new era in the treatment of early Alzheimer disease. However, their use has increased the importance of detecting and monitoring amyloid-related imaging abnormalities (ARIA) on MRI, as such findings may influence treatment continuation, dose modification, and patient safety assessment. As anti-amyloid therapies expand into routine practice, increasing surveillance MRI volumes, interreader variability, and the potential for missed subtle abnormalities have generated interest in artificial intelligence (AI)-based clinical decision support tools. A multidisciplinary panel of neuroradiologists and Alzheimer disease clinicians examined the extent of evidence supporting clinical implementation of AI-assisted ARIA detection tools, these tools' safe integration into practice, and remaining evidence gaps. The panel concluded that AI-assisted ARIA detection is likely to enhance patient safety when used as clinical decision support within a radiologist-in-the-loop framework. Panelists also noted substantial variation among commercially available tools in regulatory status, technical capabilities, and validation evidence. Moreover, they emphasized the need for further studies to assess the impact of improved detection on clinical outcomes. Overall, the panel supported conditional implementation with radiologist oversight, ongoing quality assurance, and prospective monitoring of clinical performance.

llm_summary: New treatments for early Alzheimer disease that target amyloid, a protein that builds up in the brains of people with this disease, have created a need to carefully monitor patients for side effects seen on brain scans called MRI images. A group of brain imaging doctors and Alzheimer disease specialists reviewed the available evidence to determine whether artificial intelligence computer programs could help detect these side effects more reliably and safely than doctors working alone. The experts found that artificial intelligence tools used as a second opinion alongside radiologists, rather than replacing them, could improve patient safety by catching subtle problems that might otherwise be missed. The panel recommended that hospitals and clinics could start using these artificial intelligence tools right away, but only with a radiologist reviewing the results, regular quality checks, and careful tracking of how well the tools actually work in real patients. The specialists also noted that more research is needed to understand whether finding these side effects earlier with artificial intelligence actually leads to better health outcomes for patients taking these new Alzheimer treatments.

title: Cost-Effectiveness of Early Empirical Antibiotic Cessation in Pediatric High-Risk Febrile Neutropenia.
abstract: Early discontinuation of empirical antibiotic therapy (EAT) is non-inferior to continuation of EAT until absolute neutrophil count (ANC) ≥500 cells/mm3 for children with high-risk febrile neutropenia (FN). In this prospective trial-based economic evaluation, we aimed to estimate the healthcare resource utilization and cost-effectiveness of early discontinuation of EAT versus continuation of EAT in children with high-risk FN in India.Clinically stable children aged 2-18 years with acute leukemia, high-risk FN, and afebrile status for ≥72 h were randomized to stop EAT or continue EAT until ANC recovery. Healthcare utilization data, including antibiotic exposure, antifungal use, hospitalization, laboratory investigations, and organ support, were prospectively collected. Individual patient data were used to estimate the direct medical costs, quality-adjusted life years (QALYs), and the incremental monetary benefit (iNMB).A total of 76 patients were included in the stop arm and 73 in the continuation arm. Early discontinuation reduced total antibiotic duration and antifungal use. The mean total cost per patient was ₹67,894 in the stop arm versus ₹77,291 in the continuation arm (difference: ₹9397). Antibiotic and antifungal expenditures were lower with early discontinuation of EAT. Mean QALYs were 0.0255 in the stop arm and 0.0236 in the continuation arm (difference: 0.0018). The iNMB favored early discontinuation (₹9785.6; 95% credible interval ₹6949.1-₹12,534.2). In probabilistic sensitivity analysis, early discontinuation was cost-effective in 100% of simulations.Early discontinuation of EAT in children with high-risk FN is cost-saving and the preferred strategy for children with acute leukemia and high-risk FN in India.© 2026 Wiley Periodicals LLC.

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether stopping antibiotics early in children with blood cancer and serious infections could save money without harming patient outcomes. The study followed 149 children with acute leukemia who had fevers and low white blood cell counts, randomly assigning them to either stop antibiotics after being fever-free for three days or continue antibiotics until their white blood cell counts recovered. Children who stopped antibiotics early had lower total costs (about 9,400 rupees less per patient), used fewer antifungal medications, and had slightly better quality of life measures compared to those who continued antibiotics. The results showed that early discontinuation of antibiotics was cost-effective in every computer simulation tested, making it the preferred treatment approach for this patient population in India. This finding suggests that doctors can safely stop giving antibiotics sooner to children with blood cancers and infections, which reduces healthcare expenses while maintaining or improving patient health outcomes.

title: High-grade astrocytoma with piloid features: a clinical and genomic analysis of prognostic factors using a large cohort.
abstract: High-grade astrocytoma with piloid features (HGAP) is a recently defined tumor type that is not well-understood. Prognostic factors of clinical outcomes are not well-established.Methylation profiling was performed on tumor samples, many at the National Cancer Institute (NCI) Laboratory of Pathology, and others from publicly available sources. Methylation classifier scores of ≥ 0.90 to the HGAP class on the NCI-Bethesda classifier version 3 were included. Clinical features were collected from the medical record. Survival analyses were performed using the Kaplan-Meier and Cox-proportional hazards methods.The cohort comprised 421 patients. There were high rates of ATRX alteration (62%), CDKN2A/B homozygous loss (78%) and MGMT promoter methylation (53%). MAPK alterations were identified in 74% of evaluable samples. The median age was 46 years, and posterior fossa location was predominant (52%). The median overall survival (OS) was 88 months. Older age (p = 0.01) and the presence of an ATRX alteration (p = 0.04) were found to be negative prognostic factors. The presence of cystic features on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) was found to be favorably prognostic (p = 0.01). Factors that were not significantly associated with prognosis included histologic high-grade features, CDKN2A/B homozygous deletion, MGMT promoter methylation, extent of resection, and presence of NF1 syndrome.This large cohort establishes relative frequencies of several important markers. Additionally, older age, the presence of an ATRX alteration, and cystic features on MRI were found to be prognostic. Our work may aid in optimizing treatment regimens for patients with this tumor type.Published by Oxford University Press on behalf of the Society for Neuro-Oncology 2026.

llm_summary: Researchers examined a large group of patients with a recently identified type of brain tumor called high-grade astrocytoma with piloid features to better understand which factors predict how well patients will do after treatment. The study involved analyzing tumor samples from over four hundred patients using a technique called methylation profiling, which looks at chemical markers in tumor cells, along with collecting information about each patient's age, tumor location, and medical history. The researchers found that older patients and those whose tumors had a specific genetic change called ATRX alteration had worse outcomes, while patients whose tumors showed cystic features (fluid-filled pockets) on brain imaging had better survival rates. Surprisingly, several factors that doctors might have expected to matter, such as the tumor's appearance under a microscope or certain genetic deletions, did not significantly affect how long patients survived. These findings could help doctors better predict which patients with this type of brain tumor are at higher risk and may guide decisions about how aggressively to treat individual patients.

title: Mammogram-Based Artificial Intelligence Risk Assessment in High-Risk Women Undergoing Supplemental Screening with MRI.
abstract: Current clinical risk models were developed for longer-term breast cancer risk stratification and therefore have limited utility for predicting short-term (1-year) breast cancer risk. This study evaluates the performance of a mammogram-based artificial intelligence (MB-AI) risk model for predicting breast cancer diagnosis within 1 year in high-risk women.This retrospective case-control study included 340 women who underwent supplemental MRI screening within 1 year following a negative mammogram, of whom 101 (29.7%) developed breast cancer and 239 (70.3%) remained cancer-free during the same interval. Artificial-intelligence-assigned absolute 1-year risk scores, Tyrer-Cuzick (TC) lifetime and 10-year scores, and Gail lifetime and 5-year scores were analyzed. Model discrimination was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves. Sensitivity, specificity, and predictive values were estimated at optimal cutoffs. Subgroup analyses examined model performance across genetic, menopausal, reproductive, and tumor-based strata.The MB-AI model demonstrated the highest overall discriminative ability (area under the curve [AUC] = 0.812), with strong performance in extremely dense breasts (AUC = 0.976). By comparison, TC lifetime (AUC = 0.625) and Gail lifetime (AUC = 0.668) models showed modest discrimination, while TC 10-year and Gail 5-year models did not discriminate (AUCs ≤0.49). Subgroup analyses showed consistent performance across clinical and pathological categories. The MB-AI model also showed an AUC comparable to that of previously developed AI models.A mammogram-based AI model demonstrated improved performance compared with traditional clinical risk models for predicting breast cancer diagnosis within 1 year in women undergoing supplemental screening. These findings support that AI-based approaches may reflect both short-term risk and early imaging features of occult disease and suggest further investigation of AI as a complement to existing risk stratification strategies.© Society of Breast Imaging 2026. llm_summary: Researchers examined a new artificial intelligence tool designed to predict which women might develop breast cancer within one year, since traditional risk prediction methods were created to estimate cancer risk over much longer time periods and don't work well for short-term predictions. The study looked back at information from 340 high-risk women who had additional MRI screening (a detailed imaging scan) within a year after a normal mammogram, comparing the artificial intelligence predictions to two traditional risk assessment methods used in clinical practice. The artificial intelligence model performed significantly better than the traditional methods, correctly identifying cancer risk with an accuracy score of 0. 812 out of a possible 1. 0, while the traditional methods scored much lower at 0.

title: Revascularization in Asymptomatic Carotid Artery Stenosis With Hemodynamic Impairment and Cognitive Outcomes: The CREST-H Substudy of the CREST-2 Randomized Clinical Trial.
abstract: Cerebral hemodynamic impairment in patients with asymptomatic internal carotid artery (ICA) stenosis is associated with reduced cognition. It is uncertain whether revascularization might be an effective treatment for cognitive impairment in these patients.To test whether any cognitive benefit from revascularization of high-grade, asymptomatic ICA stenosis varies based on the degree of baseline cerebral hemodynamic impairment.This substudy was conducted within a multicenter phase 3 randomized clinical trial. Adults (aged 35-86 years) without dementia with eighth-grade education or higher and unilateral asymptomatic ICA stenosis greater than or equal to 70% were enrolled from January 2018 to July 2024 at 61 sites in North America (last follow-up in July 2025). Of 607 participants screened from 2485 in CREST-2, 392 were enrolled. Magnetic resonance or computed tomographic perfusion imaging tested for baseline hemodynamic impairment defined by delayed time-to-peak (TTP) arrival of intravenous contrast in the hemisphere ipsilateral minus contralateral to the stenotic artery.Carotid revascularization (endarterectomy or stenting) plus intensive medical management (IMM) vs IMM alone.The primary outcome was the difference in composite cognitive z score over 1 year based on 5 cognitive tests. The primary analysis tested for an interaction between treatment group (revascularization vs IMM alone) and degree of baseline hemodynamic impairment among those with reduced baseline cognition (cognitive z score ≤-1.0 SD).Of 392 participants enrolled (mean age, 71 years; 125 [32%] females), 61 were excluded for missing baseline imaging and 40 for missing cognitive examinations or other covariates, leaving 291 with complete data. Fifty-one had reduced cognition at baseline (25 in the revascularization group and 26 in the IMM alone group). TTP ranged from no interhemispheric TTP delay to a more-than-2-second delay. Mean (SD) cognitive z scores were -1.36 (0.51) at baseline and -1.17 (0.47) at 1 year in the revascularization group and -1.34 (0.83) at baseline and -1.01 (0.97) at 1 year in the IMM alone group. The primary analysis showed no difference in cognition by treatment group over 1 year, adjusting for treatment group × hemodynamic status interaction and other covariates (adjusted difference in cognitive z score, -0.15 SD [95% CI, -0.54 to 0.24]). The interaction was not significant (β estimate = 0.018 [95% CI, -0.025 to 0.061]; P = .40).In this substudy of a randomized clinical trial, there was no differential effect of revascularization vs IMM alone on cognition over 1 year by cerebral hemodynamic status among those with baseline reduced cognition, suggesting that revascularization does not improve cognitive dysfunction by restoring flow to the brain in chronic asymptomatic carotid stenosis.ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT03121209.
