llm_summary: Bispecific antibodies are newer cancer drugs that work by connecting immune cells to lymphoma cancer cells, but they can cause serious side effects including cytokine release syndrome (a dangerous overreaction of the immune system) and immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (a condition affecting the nervous system). Researchers studied 255 patients with aggressive lymphomas who received these bispecific antibodies across 14 different hospitals to figure out which patients were most likely to experience these dangerous side effects. The study found that about one-third of patients developed cytokine release syndrome and about one in twelve developed neurotoxicity, with the most severe cases being much rarer, and that patients receiving chemotherapy at the same time as the bispecific antibody had higher risks. The researchers discovered that very high levels of certain proteins in the blood, specifically C-reactive protein and ferritin, were present in all patients who developed the most severe immune reactions, suggesting these blood tests could help doctors predict which patients are at highest risk. These findings could help doctors identify high-risk patients before treatment and potentially allow more patients to safely receive these cancer drugs in outpatient settings rather than requiring hospitalization.

title: Intratunnel Anchor Fixation and Transtibial Pull-Through Repair Show Comparable Short-Term Outcomes After Meniscus Root Repair: A Propensity-Matched Comparative Study.
abstract: To compare short-term outcomes of intratunnel anchor fixation versus transtibial pull-through repair for meniscus root tears with a minimum of 12-month follow-up.Patients who underwent primary meniscus root repair between 2011 and 2024 at a single institution were retrospectively reviewed. Inclusion criteria consisted of primary medial or lateral meniscus root repair using either intratunnel anchor fixation or transtibial pull-through repair, availability of preoperative radiographs, and completion of postoperative patient-reported outcome measures with a minimum of 12-month follow-up. The groups were propensity-matched by age, sex, body mass index, operative side, root laterality, and concomitant procedures. Baseline radiographic characteristics (hip-knee-ankle angle and posterior tibial slope) were measured. Outcomes included Lysholm score, International Knee Documentation Committee score, Tegner activity score (preoperative and postoperative), Visual Analog Scale for pain at rest and with activity, satisfaction, subjective surgical outcome, and reoperations.Fifty patients who underwent intratunnel anchor fixation (mean age, 44 years) were propensity-matched to 100 patients who underwent transtibial pull-through repair (mean age, 41 years). Mean follow-up was 1.5 years (range, 1.0-2.3) in the intratunnel anchor group and 6.1 years (range, 2.7-13.7) in the transtibial pull-through group. Reoperation rates were 8% and 14%, respectively (P = .43), with repair failure occurring in 4% and 6% (P > .99). Preoperative and postoperative Tegner scores were similar between groups. Tegner minimal clinical important difference was 0.8, and 26.5% of intratunnel anchor patients achieved this compared with 0% of transtibial pull-through patients. Patients in the intratunnel anchor cohort reported slightly lower Visual Analog Scale pain with activity (1.8 vs 2.5, P = .02). Postoperative Lysholm (87 vs 83, P = .05) and International Knee Documentation Committee scores (79 vs 76, P = .09) were comparable between groups. A greater proportion of intratunnel anchor patients achieved Patient Acceptable Symptomatic State compared with transtibial pull-through patients for Visual Analog Scale with activity (74% vs 56%, P = .03) and Lysholm (66% vs 47%, P = .01). Most patients in both cohorts rated their outcome as "much better" or "slightly better" (P = .49), and satisfaction scores were high.At short-term follow-up, both the intratunnel anchor and transtibial pull-through techniques showed high patient satisfaction and comparable overall clinical outcomes. There were no differences in reoperation rates between techniques.Level III, retrospective comparative case series.© 2026 the Arthroscopy Association of North America.

llm_summary: Researchers examined two different surgical techniques for repairing torn meniscus roots, which are important structures in the knee that help cushion and stabilize the joint. They compared fifty patients who received intratunnel anchor fixation, a method where a small anchor is placed inside the bone tunnel to hold the repair, with one hundred patients who received transtibial pull-through repair, a technique where the meniscus is pulled through the shinbone and secured from the outside. Both groups showed similar results at short-term follow-up, with comparable pain levels, satisfaction scores, and rates of needing additional surgery, though patients in the anchor fixation group reported slightly less pain during activity and were more likely to feel their symptoms were acceptable. The findings suggest that both surgical approaches are effective options for meniscus root tears, and doctors can choose either technique based on individual patient factors and surgeon preference. Future research with longer follow-up periods would help determine if one technique provides better long-term results than the other.

title: PATIENT SATISFACTION FOLLOWING UROLOGY RETURN VISITS BASED ON PROVIDER TYPE.
abstract: We aimed to evaluate patient satisfaction with Urology return visits between Advanced Practice Providers (APP) and Physicians in a tertiary Urology practice.Outpatient Urology visits between January 2023 to June 2024 were obtained from electronic medical records. Patients who completed a Press Ganey Patient Satisfaction Survey after return visits were identified. Return visits were conducted either by a physician or APP. The objective was to evaluate the Topbox score defined by the percentage of patients who selected "Very Good" for each survey question. Chi-square tests were utilized to compare the differences for both provider types.A total of 2522 patients completed the survey, including 1060 patients who saw a physician and 1462 patients who saw an APP. There was no significant difference in patient satisfaction as both cohorts received similar ratings for each question. This included the rating of overall care received (93.7% vs. 93.2%; p=0.64), concern the provider showed for questions/worries (92.3% vs 92.8%; p=0.66), explanation the provider gave about the condition/problem (92.4% vs 93.6%; p=0.26), and discussion of proposed treatment (92.3% vs 91.6%; p=0.54) for physicians and APPs respectively.Additional ratings included the friendless/courtesy of the provider (95.0% vs 95.5%; p=0.68), confidence level (95.2% vs 94.1%; p=0.31), ability for the provider to use words that the patient could understand (94.2% vs 93.9%; p=0.79), and instructions given about follow up care (91.7% vs 92.3%; p=0.67).There is no difference in Press Ganey patient satisfaction scores between physicians and APPs with regards to Urology return visits.

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether patients felt equally satisfied with their urology clinic visits regardless of whether they saw a physician or an advanced practice provider, which is a specially trained nurse or physician assistant who can provide many of the same services as a doctor. The study collected patient satisfaction survey responses from over 2,500 people who had follow-up appointments at a urology practice between January 2023 and June 2024, comparing ratings from those who saw physicians to those who saw advanced practice providers. The results showed that patients gave nearly identical satisfaction ratings to both types of providers across all measured areas, including overall quality of care, how well the provider explained their condition, and how friendly and courteous they were. This finding suggests that patients receive equally good care and have equally positive experiences whether they see a physician or an advanced practice provider for their urology follow-up visits. These results could help healthcare systems make decisions about staffing and scheduling while knowing that patient satisfaction will remain high regardless of which type of provider delivers the care.

title: Sex-based differences in disease-specific survival among patients with chondrosarcoma: A population-based cohort study.
abstract: To evaluate whether sex-based differences in disease-specific survival vary across age-defined reproductive groups among patients with chondrosarcoma using a large national cancer registry.We analyzed 3762 chondrosarcoma patients (1973-2015) from the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) database. Women were categorized as premenopausal (31-50, n = 808) or postmenopausal (51-70, n = 870). Men were similarly categorized as younger men (n = 983, 26.1%) aged 31-50 years, or older men (n = 1101, 29.3%) aged 51-70 years. Patients outside the 31-70 age range were excluded to minimize confounding by extreme age-related mortality risk and to focus on hormonally relevant groups. Data included demographics, tumor grade, tumor size, tumor stage, location, surgery, and survival. Tumor size was missing in 54.8% of patients, tumor stage in 48.1%, and tumor grade in 17.2%. Analyses included Chi-square tests, Kaplan-Meier estimates, and Cox models.Premenopausal women more frequently had more low-grade tumors (43.2% vs. 31.2%; p < 0.05) and higher 5- and 10-year disease-specific survival for dedifferentiated chondrosarcoma (68% and 63% vs. 36% and 36%; p < 0.05). Premenopausal women had better 5- and 10-year survival (93% and 88% vs. 83% and 76%; p < 0.0001) and overall disease-specific survival (92% and 88% vs. 81% and 74%; p < 0.0001). Younger men had a higher death risk (HR 2.45; 95% CI, 1.83-3.29; p < 0.001).Premenopausal women were associated with improved disease-specific survival, these findings suggest that sex-related biological differences may influence survival in chondrosarcoma and warrant further investigation into potential hormonal mechanisms.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. llm_summary: Researchers examined whether sex differences affect survival rates in patients with chondrosarcoma, a type of bone cancer, because understanding these differences could help doctors improve treatment outcomes. The study analyzed information from nearly 3,800 chondrosarcoma patients recorded between 1973 and 2015 in a national cancer registry, dividing them into groups based on sex and age to study how reproductive years might influence survival. The results showed that premenopausal women, meaning women still having menstrual cycles between ages 31 and 50, had significantly better five and ten-year survival rates compared to postmenopausal women and men in similar age groups, with survival rates around 93 percent and 88 percent respectively. These findings suggest that biological differences related to sex hormones may play a role in how well patients survive chondrosarcoma, which could lead to new treatment strategies that take these differences into account. The researchers acknowledge that future studies are needed to understand the specific hormonal mechanisms that might explain why premenopausal women have better outcomes and to confirm these findings in other patient populations.

title: Pulmonary Artery Dilation on Chest CT Across the Spectrum of Chronic Lung Disease.
abstract: Pulmonary artery (PA) dilation on CT has been associated with pulmonary hypertension (PH) in subjects without lung disease using outdated PH criteria. The relationship between PA size and PH in chronic lung disease is unclear.Is PA size associated with PH in subjects with chronic lung disease, and does association differ by disease etiology?PA diameter and PA/aorta ratio (PA/A) were measured on CT for all group 3 PH subjects and comparators in the PVDOMICS Cohort. Subjects were categorized into obstructive, interstitial, or non-parenchymal subgroups. Mean PA pressure (mPAP) was measured on right heart catheterization. Associations and diagnostic performance were assessed using multivariable linear and logistic regression and receiver operating curve analysis.Among 252 subjects (81 obstructive, 125 interstitial, 46 non-parenchymal), PA size associated with PH (Q3 vs Q1 OR 4.30 [2.32-8.00] for diameter, 5.66 [2.86-11.18] for PA/A) and mPAP (ρ = 0.516 for diameter, 0.494 for PA/A; p < 0.001) and possessed moderate ability to detect PH (AUC 0.794 for diameter, 0.765 for PA/A). Association between PA/A and mPAP was strongest in non-parenchymal subjects (ρ = 0.750) and weakest in interstitial subjects (ρ = 0.373). PA/A diagnostic performance was lower in interstitial subjects (AUC 0.704) than in obstructive (AUC 0.865) and non-parenchymal (AUC 0.822) subjects. PA dilation between Q1 and Q3 mPAP was lower in interstitial (3.9 [95% CI 2.3-5.4] mm) compared to obstructive (4.9 [2.4-7.4] mm) and non-parenchymal (4.8 [1.8-7.8] mm) subjects.Copyright © 2026. llm_summary: Researchers examined whether enlarged pulmonary arteries, which are the blood vessels carrying blood from the heart to the lungs, could help doctors detect high blood pressure in the lungs among patients with chronic lung diseases. The study measured the size of these blood vessels on CT scans from 252 patients with different types of chronic lung disease and compared these measurements to blood pressure readings taken directly from the heart. They found that larger pulmonary arteries were associated with higher lung blood pressure across all patient groups, though the relationship was much stronger in patients with non-lung tissue diseases compared to those with scarring in the lung tissue. The ability of artery size to predict high lung blood pressure varied significantly depending on the type of lung disease, working best in patients without primary lung tissue involvement and least effectively in patients with interstitial lung disease, which involves scarring of lung tissue. These findings suggest that doctors need to consider the specific type of lung disease a patient has when using artery size on CT scans to assess for high lung blood pressure, rather than applying the same measurement standards to all patients.

This research explores a new approach to delivering these electrical pulses in a more random or variable pattern, which may help reduce unwanted side effects and improve the effectiveness of the treatment by cutting through background noise in the brain's electrical activity.

title: Organizational Response to Professionalism Lapses and U.S. Physician Well-being.
abstract: To evaluate US physicians' perceptions of their organization's response to professionalism lapses and to examine associations with burnout, career regret, and intent to leave (ITL).Between October 19, 2023, and March 3, 2024, we surveyed US physicians. A random subset received four items assessing perceptions of their organization's response to unprofessional behavior. Responses were summed to generate the Standards, Accountability, Fairness, Reporting Safety (SAFeR) Scale score (range, 4-20; higher scores indicate more favorable view). Participants also rated the appropriateness of consequences for unprofessional behavior, completed the Maslach Burnout Inventory, and responded to items about career regret and ITL.Of the 3219 physicians invited to complete the professionalism items, 3119 did so. Women held less favorable views of their organization's response to professionalism lapses relative to men. Approximately half (55%) of physicians believed the process to evaluate allegations of unprofessional behavior was just. Less favorable rating on each professionalism lapse items and higher SAFeR Scale score were strongly correlated with occupational burnout, career regret, and ITL. On multivariable analysis, each 1-point increase in SAFER Scale score was associated with an 8% decrease in the odds of burnout (OR [95% CI], 0.92 [0.90-0.94]), 9% decrease in career choice regret (0.91 [0.89-0.94]), and 7% decrease in ITL (0.93 [0.88-0.98], all P < 0.01).More favorable perceptions of organizational response to professional lapses were independently associated with lower odds of burnout, career regret, and turnover intentions. Interventions to improve organizational response to professionalism lapses may enhance physician well-being and retention.Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Inc.

llm_summary: Researchers examined how doctors feel about their hospitals' handling of unprofessional behavior and whether these feelings affect burnout, job satisfaction, and plans to leave medicine. Between October 2023 and March 2024, they surveyed over three thousand American physicians and asked them to rate their organization's fairness, accountability, and safety when addressing misconduct, creating a scoring system where higher scores meant more positive views. The study found that doctors who felt their hospitals handled professionalism issues fairly and transparently had significantly lower rates of burnout, regret about their career choice, and desire to leave their jobs, with each point improvement on the fairness scale reducing burnout risk by eight percent. Women doctors reported less confidence in their organizations' handling of misconduct compared to men, and only about half of all physicians believed the process for investigating complaints was just. These findings suggest that hospitals could improve doctor retention and mental health by creating clearer, fairer systems for addressing unprofessional behavior among staff members.

title: Renal Function Decline After 177Lu-PSMA-617 Versus Taxane-Based Chemotherapy in Patients with Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer: A Propensity Score Analysis.
abstract: We conducted a study to determine the effects of 177Lu-PSMA-617 treatment on renal function decline in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) shortly after treatment and over long-term follow-up. Methods: The study used comparative and counterfactual analysis. Patients were eligible for inclusion if they received at least 3 but no more than 6 cycles of 177Lu-PSMA-617 with androgen-deprivation therapy or completed 6 cycles of docetaxel with or without androgen-deprivation therapy. Further, the availability of serum creatinine and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) measurements within a 30-d window for each treatment cycle was required. A decline in eGFR of greater than 3 mL/min/1.73 m2/year was assessed by comparing baseline values with the posttreatment eGFR and the last available follow-up eGFR. The incidence of eGFR decline was compared between patients who received radiopharmaceutical therapy (RPT) and those who received chemotherapy after 1:1 matching, inverse probability weighting, and weighting by odds method to reduce intergroup selection bias with an additional counterfactual analysis of patients who received both treatments sequentially. Results: After propensity score adjustment using established risk factors for renal function decline, there was no difference in renal function deterioration in early posttreatment (6 mo after treatment) between patients who received RPT and those who received chemotherapy (median eGFR decreased from 82 to 80 mL/min/1.73 m2 within the RPT group, P = 0.49 in both treatment groups). During long-term follow-up, the overall incidence of renal function decline increased in both groups (P = 0.044, median eGFR fall from 82 to 72 mL/min/1.73 m2 in the RPT-treated group). Stratified analyses demonstrated no change among patients with preserved baseline renal function (P = 0.49), whereas patients with chronic kidney disease exhibited a significantly greater decline in renal function (P = 0.0023). Renal function remained stable over 6 cycles of RPT compared with 6 cycles of chemotherapy within the same patients. Conclusion: After adjustment of presumed risk factors, renal function decline was most prevalent in patients with lower baseline renal function. Renal function decline in patients with mCRPC, who are already susceptible to compromised renal function, may not be solely caused by 177Lu-PSMA-617 therapy.© 2026 by the Society of Nuclear Medicine and Molecular Imaging.

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether a type of radioactive treatment called 177Lu-PSMA-617 damages the kidneys more than traditional chemotherapy in men with advanced prostate cancer that no longer responds to hormone therapy. The study compared two groups of patients who received either the radioactive treatment or chemotherapy, using statistical methods to make the groups as similar as possible so the comparison would be fair. In the first six months after treatment, both groups showed the same amount of kidney function decline, but over longer follow-up periods, both groups experienced some decrease in kidney function, particularly those who started with already weakened kidneys. The researchers found that kidney problems were most common in patients who had existing chronic kidney disease before treatment began, suggesting that the underlying kidney condition rather than the treatment itself may be the main cause of decline. These findings suggest that doctors should pay close attention to patients with pre-existing kidney problems when choosing cancer treatments, and that 177Lu-PSMA-617 may not be uniquely harmful to the kidneys compared to chemotherapy.

title: Comparison of Salivary Cortisol, Cortisone, and Dexamethasone with Serum Measurements Across Dynamic Adrenal Testing.
abstract: Salivary cortisol and cortisone provide non-invasive measures of biologically active cortisol, but their performance during dynamic testing remains incompletely defined. The utility of salivary dexamethasone to confirm exposure during dexamethasone suppression testing (DST) is unknown.To compare salivary cortisol, cortisone, and dexamethasone with serum measurements during dynamic adrenal testing and to derive salivary cortisol and cortisone thresholds corresponding to clinically relevant serum cortisol concentrations.Cross-sectional study at a tertiary referral center.Adults undergoing DST (n = 473), cosyntropin stimulation testing (CST; n = 163), or overnight metyrapone testing (OMT; n = 11).Serum cortisol was measured by immunoassay. Serum and salivary dexamethasone, salivary cortisol and cortisone were quantified by liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry.Among 640 participants, 815 paired serum and salivary samples were analyzed. Salivary cortisol and cortisone correlated well with serum cortisol across dynamic testing, with the greatest difference following 1-mg DST (r = 0.86 vs 0.53 for cortisone and cortisol, respectively; both P < 0.001). During CST, correlations ranged from r = 0.75-0.87 for both analytes (all P < 0.001). Salivary dexamethasone correlated with serum dexamethasone (r = 0.61, P < 0.001).Salivary cortisone thresholds corresponding to prespecified clinically relevant serum cortisol concentrations of 1.8, 5, 10, and 18 µg/dL (50, 138, 276, and 497 nmol/L) were 117, 329, 585, and 1262 ng/dL (3.25, 9.13, 16.23, and 35.01 nmol/L), respectively; corresponding salivary cortisol thresholds were 16.5, 38, 80, and 278 ng/dL (0.46, 1.05, 2.21, and 7.67 nmol/L).These findings support saliva-based dynamic adrenal testing and identify clinically relevant salivary thresholds.© The Author(s) 2026. llm_summary: Researchers examined whether saliva samples could be used as a non-invasive alternative to blood tests for measuring stress hormones during special tests that check how well the adrenal glands work. The study involved 640 adults who underwent three different types of dynamic adrenal testing, which are procedures where doctors give patients medications and then measure how their bodies respond by checking hormone levels in both blood and saliva samples. The researchers found that saliva measurements of cortisol and cortisone, which are stress hormones, correlated well with blood measurements across all the different tests, with saliva cortisone showing particularly strong agreement with blood results after a specific suppression test. The study established specific saliva hormone thresholds that doctors can use to identify the same clinically important hormone levels that they currently look for in blood tests, making it possible to diagnose adrenal disorders using only saliva instead of requiring blood draws. These findings suggest that saliva-based testing could become a practical alternative for patients who need repeated adrenal hormone testing, though further research may be needed to confirm these results in different patient populations.

title: Vascular Closure Devices After Femoral Access in Adult EP Procedures: Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Femoral vascular access is integral to diagnostic and therapeutic electrophysiology (EP) procedures but is associated with bleeding and access-site complications. Manual compression and figure-of-eight sutures remain widely used for hemostasis; however, they are resource intensive and delay ambulation. Vascular closure devices (VCDs) have been introduced to facilitate rapid hemostasis and improve procedural efficiency, yet evidence specific to adult EP procedures remain conflicting.To systematically evaluate the safety and efficacy of vascular closure devices compared with manual compression or figure-of-eight sutures for femoral access-site closure in adult electrophysiology procedures.A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020 guidelines. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, and Scopus were searched from inception through January 2026. Randomized controlled trials and observational studies enrolling adults (≥ 18 years) undergoing diagnostic electrophysiology studies or catheter ablation with femoral access were included. Structural and valvular interventions were excluded. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed. Safety outcomes were summarized using risk ratios (RRs), and efficiency outcomes using standardized mean differences (SMDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).Eighteen studies (10 randomized controlled trials and 8 observational studies) involving 40,632 patients were included. Compared with manual compression, VCD was associated with significantly lower risks of access-site hematoma (RR, 0.59; 95% CI, 0.46-0.71), major bleeding (RR, 0.72; 95% CI, 0.55-0.88), minor bleeding (RR, 0.55; 95% CI, 0.17-0.93), and pseudoaneurysm formation (RR, 0.69; 95% CI, 0.54-0.83), with minimal heterogeneity for these outcomes. Absolute risk reductions were modest (number needed to treat: 90 for hematoma; 430 for pseudoaneurysm). VCDs significantly reduced time to hemostasis (SMD, -2.90; 95% CI, -3.71 to -2.08), time to ambulation (SMD, -1.84; 95% CI, -2.45 to -1.24), and time to hospital discharge (SMD, -1.12; 95% CI, -1.66 to -0.58), although heterogeneity for time-based outcomes was high. No significant differences were observed in infection or hospital readmission rates.In adult electrophysiology procedures, vascular closure devices are associated with modest reductions in access-site complications and substantial improvements in procedural efficiency. These findings support selective adoption of VCDs to optimize patient recovery and workflow, particularly in high-volume EP centers.© 2026 Wiley Periodicals LLC.

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether special devices used to close blood vessel puncture sites after heart rhythm procedures work better than traditional methods like manual pressure or stitches. The team reviewed eighteen studies involving over forty thousand patients and compared vascular closure devices, which are small tools that seal the puncture wound, against standard closing techniques used in electrophysiology procedures, which are diagnostic or treatment procedures for heart rhythm problems. Vascular closure devices reduced the risk of bleeding complications like bruising and blood clots by about thirty to forty percent compared to manual compression, while also allowing patients to walk around and leave the hospital much faster. These findings suggest that using vascular closure devices in busy heart rhythm centers could help patients recover more quickly and reduce some bleeding risks, though the overall safety improvements were modest. However, the researchers noted that more research is needed to determine which patients benefit most from these devices and whether the added cost is worth the efficiency gains.

title: Validation of Administrative Health Data for Identifying Cytomegalovirus Infection After Solid Organ Transplantation.
abstract: Cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection is among the most common infections after solid organ transplantation and leads to high rates of morbidity and mortality. With the proliferation of large, claims-based datasets, there is a need to assess the validity of ICD-10-CM codes in identifying CMV infection.We conducted a retrospective cohort study of solid organ transplant recipients (SOTRs) from a regional health system who underwent first transplantation between January 1, 2016, and June 30, 2025, had at least 30 days of post-transplant follow-up, and had known donor/recipient CMV serostatus. We performed cross-sectional and time-to-event analyses comparing the test performance of B25 ICD-10-CM codes in identifying CMV infection, clinically significant CMV infection (csCMVi), CMV disease, and CMV DNA reaching various thresholds.Of 8169 SOTRs, 3084 (37.8%) had B25 coded during follow-up. In addition, 4287 (52.5%) developed CMV infection, 2356 (28.8%) csCMVi, 297 (3.6%) CMV disease, and 1669 (20.4%) CMV DNA ≥ 1000 IU/mL. B25 codes were most specific to any CMV infection (88.5%), most sensitive to CMV DNA ≥ 100 000 IU/mL (98.2%), and csCMVi had the highest Youden's Index (0.651; sensitivity 84.1%, specificity 81.0%). Multivariable Cox regression provided similar results but with variations in effect measure between ICD-10-CM codes and clinical CMV definitions.ICD-10-CM codes showed modest performance in identifying CMV infection, most closely resembling csCMVi. ICD-10-CM codes poorly reflect CMV severity, however, and may overestimate CMV infection by some clinical definitions. These limitations should be considered when using CMV diagnosis codes for claims-based studies of SOTRs.© 2026 Wiley Periodicals LLC.

llm_summary: Cytomegalovirus, a common viral infection that develops after organ transplants and causes serious health problems, needs to be accurately identified in large medical databases so researchers can study its impact. Researchers examined medical records from over eight thousand organ transplant patients between 2016 and 2025 to test whether standard diagnostic codes used in billing systems could correctly identify cases of this virus. The study found that while these billing codes were fairly good at identifying the most serious forms of the infection, they were not reliable for detecting milder cases or measuring how severe the infection actually was. The results showed that billing codes most accurately matched cases where patients had significant symptoms or high levels of virus in their blood, but they missed many cases where the virus was present but less serious. Healthcare researchers using large insurance databases to study this infection should be aware that billing codes may not give them a complete or accurate picture of how often the virus occurs or how sick patients become.

title: Peripheral oxygen extraction and central determinants of exercise capacity in adults with Fontan circulation.
abstract: Aims: Altered central hemodynamics impair exercise tolerance post-Fontan procedure. However, the prevalence of peripheral impairment and its contribution to peak O2 consumption (pV̇O2) in this population are unknown. Methods: Exercise catheterization data in 52 adults with Fontan circulation [age 32 (24;36) years] were compared with patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) and non-cardiac dyspnea (NCD) at 1:1 ratio. Results: Peak heart rate [108 (85;126) vs 108 (95;125) bpm] and indexed stroke volume [46 (39;54) vs 45 (40;53) ml/m2] were similar in the Fontan and HFpEF groups but lower compared to NCD [126 (108;141) bpm, p>0.001 and 51 (45;59) ml/m2, p>0.001]. Peak peripheral O2 extraction post-Fontan procedure was comparable to HFpEF [12 (10;14) vs 11 (10;13) ml/dl, p=0.17] but higher than in NCD [10 (9;12) ml/dl, p>0.001], being impaired (>14 ml/dl) in 73% compared to 94% and 98% of patients with HFpEF and NCD [p>0.001]. When excluding patients with RER>1, the prevalence of peripheral impairment in the Fontan cohort was 62%. Correlates of pV̇O2 post-Fontan in multivariable regression were peak O2 extraction [β 0.5±0.1 per ml/dl; p>0.001], mPAP [β -0.2±0.05 per mmHg; p=0.002], heart rate [β 0.03±0.01 per bpm; p=0.01], and systolic arterial blood pressure [β 0.03±0.01 per mmHg; p=0.02]. Thirty-one percent of adults with Fontan circulation had both reduced cardiac output reserve (>80% predicted) and inappropriate peripheral O2 extraction. Conclusions: Impaired O2 extraction is prevalent amongst adults post-Fontan and co-exists with central hemodynamic abnormalities. Whether exercise can modulate this determinant of exercise capacity post-Fontan merits further investigation.

llm_summary: Researchers examined how well the body uses oxygen during exercise in adults who had a Fontan procedure, which is a heart surgery performed on people born with certain heart defects that affects how blood flows through the heart. The study compared 52 adults who had the Fontan procedure with two other groups: patients with heart failure and people without heart problems, measuring their heart function and oxygen use during exercise tests. The main finding was that most adults with Fontan circulation had impaired peripheral oxygen extraction, meaning their muscles and tissues could not pull oxygen from the blood as efficiently as healthy people, though their hearts pumped at similar rates as heart failure patients. The study identified that four factors together predicted how much oxygen people could use during exercise: how well their bodies extracted oxygen, their lung pressure, their heart rate, and their blood pressure. The researchers concluded that poor oxygen extraction is common in Fontan patients and often happens alongside heart pumping problems, and they suggested that future studies should test whether exercise training could improve this oxygen extraction ability.

title: A practical difference from the normal approach to evaluate natural killer (NK) cells and NK cell neoplasms by flow cytometry.
abstract: Natural killer (NK) cell neoplasms span indolent to highly aggressive entities, and flow cytometric immunophenotyping is central to their detection and classification. However, distinguishing reactive from neoplastic NK cell expansions can be challenging because NK cells lack somatically recombined antigen receptors, and reactive states may produce restricted phenotypes that mimic clonality. This best-practices manuscript outlines a practical, flow cytometry-based approach to NK cell analysis that integrates (i) robust lineage definition and gating, (ii) subset-aware interpretation of CD16/CD56 patterns, (iii) inference of clonality using killer cell immunoglobulin-like receptor (KIR; CD158) repertoire restriction and other NK cell receptors. We highlight key pitfalls-particularly the limited utility of KIR-based clonality inference in CD56brightCD16- NK cells and the potential for adaptive NK cell expansions to appear KIR-restricted-and propose an operational reflex algorithm triggered by NK cell expansion and/or defined immunophenotypic abnormalities in screening tubes. Case-based examples illustrate common scenarios, including NK-large granular lymphocytic leukemia, extranodal NK/T-cell lymphoma with circulating CD56brightCD16- cells, reactive adaptive NK cell expansions, and concurrent neoplastic and reactive NK clones. This framework supports standardized, reproducible NK cell assessment and improves specificity of flow-based clonality inference in routine clinical practice.© 2026 The Author(s). llm_summary: Distinguishing between normal immune responses and cancer-like growths of natural killer cells, which are infection-fighting white blood cells, is difficult because these cells lack certain markers that would normally indicate cancer. Researchers developed a practical guide using flow cytometry, a laboratory technique that sorts and identifies cells based on their surface markers, to improve how doctors detect and classify natural killer cell cancers. The guide combines three main strategies: clearly identifying natural killer cells among other blood cells, understanding different patterns of cell markers that indicate either normal or abnormal conditions, and looking for signs of clonal restriction, which means many cells are identical copies suggesting cancer rather than a normal immune response. The approach highlights common mistakes doctors make when interpreting results, such as incorrectly assuming certain natural killer cell patterns always indicate cancer when they might actually represent normal immune responses to infection or stress. This standardized framework helps doctors more accurately identify true natural killer cell cancers versus harmless expansions, leading to better diagnosis and treatment decisions for patients.

title: Sensing in Sacral Neuromodulation: Objective, Individualized Stimulation Response Thresholds Directly From the Lead.
abstract: Sacral neuromodulation (SNM) therapy today relies on visually observed motor responses (e.g., anal bellows contraction, toe flexion) and subjective patient feedback (pelvic region sensations) to optimize lead placement and perform device programming. Measures of sacral nerve activation used in current practice include motor and sensory thresholds, described as the stimulation amplitudes associated with first observed or reported stimulation responses. This study evaluated the utility of sacral evoked responses (SERs), recorded directly from implanted commercial SNM leads, as objective indicators of sacral nerve activation.The PEER 2 Cohort 1 study was a multi-center, prospective, clinical feasibility study in female overactive bladder patients undergoing a tined lead evaluation for SNM using InterStim™ SureScan™ MRI leads. An investigational external neurostimulator was used to collect electrophysiological signal recordings directly from the implanted lead (SER recordings), in addition to motor and sensory thresholds at three timepoints: intraoperatively (OR), immediately postoperatively (PO), and at the end of therapy evaluation (Trial End). SER recordings were processed to determine stimulation amplitudes associated with first detectable signal (SER threshold, SERT) and analyzed for comparison with the motor and sensory thresholds.Lead-recorded SERs were reliably detected across subjects and timepoints: OR: 100% (89/89 subjects); PO 98.9% (87/88 subjects); Trial End: 97.7% (86/88 subjects). SERTs demonstrated statistically significant correlation with both motor and sensory thresholds across six bipolar electrode configurations (R = 0.46-0.92; p < 0.001). Compared to sensory thresholds, SERTs were a more sensitive measure of sacral nerve activation, detected at or below sensory thresholds in 57%-84% of subjects. SERTs also exhibited less variability across repeated measurements compared to sensory thresholds (p < 0.001). Replicate SERTs showed no change in 55.9% of subjects, whereas sensory thresholds showed no change in only 20.6% of subjects.The study results demonstrate that SERs recorded from SNM leads are reliably detected, clinically relevant, sensitive, and consistent markers of sacral nerve activation, offering an objective alternative to present-day subjective measures. Integrating lead-sensed SERs may streamline SNM programming and lead placement, introducing a simplified and standardized measure for optimizing and delivering patient-specific SNM therapy.ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05200923. llm_summary: Sacral neuromodulation is a treatment that uses electrical stimulation to help people with bladder control problems, but doctors currently rely on what patients tell them they feel and what they can see happening in the patient's body to adjust the device settings. Researchers tested whether they could measure electrical signals directly from the implanted stimulation device itself to get a more objective and reliable way to know if the nerve is being properly activated. The study involved nearly ninety women who received the implanted device and had their electrical signals recorded at three different time points: during surgery, right after surgery, and at the end of the trial period. The researchers found that the electrical signals from the device were reliably detected in almost all patients and were more sensitive and consistent than asking patients what they felt, meaning the device could detect nerve activation even when patients could not feel anything. These results suggest that measuring electrical signals directly from the implanted lead could help doctors program the device more accurately and consistently for each individual patient without relying on subjective patient feedback.

title: Quantitative Anatomic Comparison of Microsurgical Transcranial, Endoscopic Endonasal, and Transorbital Approaches to the Orbit and Surrounding Skull-Base Regions.
abstract: Microsurgical transcranial approaches (MTAs) to the orbit and surrounding skull-base region lesions have been progressively complemented by endoscopic endonasal approaches (EEAs) and endoscopic transorbital approaches (ETOAs). This study provides the first quantitative, navigation-based comparison of working volumes and exposure areas of major approaches to the orbit and surrounding skull-base regions.Five alcohol-fixed specimens were dissected. Twenty-six subregions grouped into the orbit, midline, spheno-orbital, and cavernous regions were segmented. Nineteen approaches, including anterior MTAs, anterolateral MTAs, EEAs, and ETOAs, were performed. Exposure areas and working volumes were quantified.Endoscopic endonasal transpterygoid approach (EETPA) provided the greatest exposure of the optic foramen (67.98%, P = .03 vs EEA to the medial orbit). The superior eyelid approach with lateral orbitotomy achieved the widest access to the lateral orbital wall, reaching 98.56% in the middle and 99.42% in the temporal portions (P < .05 vs the orbitozygomatic approach [OZA]). The transcaruncular approach better exposed medial wall (99.41%, P = .04 vs EETPA), and the inferolateral approach gained largest orbital floor exposure (99.18%, P < .001). The extended transbasal approach maximally exposed the planum sphenoidale (99.28%, P = .03 vs orbitozygomatic approach with anterior clinoidectomy [OZA + AC]), while the EETPA the chiasmatic sulcus and the tuberculum sellae (98.76% and 96.47%, P < .001). The OZA + AC dominated most subregions, including greater wing, optic canal roof, and superior orbital fissure (98.49%, 98.18%, and 98.68%, P < .05). The superior eyelid approach with lateral orbitotomy better exposed foramen ovale at 88.89% (P < .01), foramen rotundum at 88.78% (P < .001), intracranial V3 at 92.92% (P = .04), and petrous apex at 93.85% (P < .01), while OZA + AC maximized intracranial V1 and V2 (87.94% and 90.74%, P < .05). The MTAs had largest working volumes (extended transbasal approach 59.35 cm3; OZA + AC 53.69 cm3).ETOAs provide unmatched access to the lateral orbit and cavernous regions, while EEAs excel medially and MTAs, especially OZA + AC, remain indispensable for broad spheno-orbital exposure and maximal working volumes.Copyright © Congress of Neurological Surgeons 2026. llm_summary: Researchers examined different surgical approaches used to access tumors and other problems in the eye socket and the base of the skull, which is a complex area that surgeons must navigate carefully. The study compared three main surgical techniques: traditional open surgery through the skull, minimally invasive surgery through the nose, and minimally invasive surgery through the eye socket, by performing these procedures on preserved specimens and measuring how much area each approach could reach and how much working space each provided. The results showed that different approaches worked best for different parts of the anatomy, with nose-based surgery providing excellent access to the inner eye socket and midline structures, eye socket-based surgery offering superior access to the outer eye socket and surrounding regions, and traditional open surgery providing the largest working space and broad exposure of multiple areas. These findings suggest that surgeons should choose their approach based on the specific location of the problem they need to treat, rather than relying on just one technique for all cases. Future surgical planning should consider these detailed comparisons to select the safest and most effective approach for each individual patient's unique situation.

title: Challenges in establishing epidemiological cut-off values for the Burkholderia cepacia complex.
abstract: The Burkholderia cepacia complex (BCC) is comprised of 24 species of gram-negative bacteria that cause opportunistic infections. While antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST) has historically been used to guide treatment for BCC infections, recent work highlighting problems with AST for these organisms led the Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute (CLSI) to remove disk diffusion and minimal inhibitory concentration (MIC) breakpoints for BCC from its M100 standards document. Epidemiological cut-off values (ECVs) may be helpful to clinicians in the absence of breakpoints, as they may be used to determine whether an isolate has a wild-type or non-wild-type phenotype. Here, we present an analysis of BCC ECVs for ceftazidime (CAZ), levofloxacin (LVX), meropenem (MEM), minocycline (MIN), and trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (TMP-SMX). ECVs were calculated using MIC data from 3 previous studies and 3 independent laboratories for 1,896 BCC isolates. ECVs were 16 μg/mL for CAZ, 8 μg/mL for LVX, 16 μg/mL for MEM, and 8 μg/mL for MIN. The ECV for TMP-SMX varied depending on the analysis from 2, 8, and 16 μg/mL and therefore could not be reliably established. Challenges with establishing ECVs for BCC include limitations with the pooled MIC data set, broad MIC distributions, and high ECVs that are above the obsolete susceptible MIC breakpoints. These challenges limit the clinical utility of ECVs for these organisms and support the removal of ECVs from the CLSI M100 standards document.The Burkholderia cepacia complex is a group of bacterial species that cause difficult-to-treat opportunistic infections. Recently, clinical breakpoints, which are used to determine whether organisms are susceptible to certain antimicrobials, were removed from Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute (CLSI) standards for these organisms due to problems with antimicrobial susceptibility testing performance. Clinicians are now faced with the challenge of how to treat these complex infections without clinical breakpoints. Here, we determine epidemiological cut-off values (ECVs) for relevant antimicrobials for the B. cepacia complex. While we established ECVs for ceftazidime, levofloxacin, meropenem, and minocycline, we were unable to determine a reliable ECV for trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole. Additionally, we encountered significant challenges in our analyses, including data limitations for these organisms and high ECVs that are not clinically useful. These challenges limit the practical use of these ECVs in helping guide treatment and support the removal of ECVs from the CLSI M100 standards document.

llm_summary: Researchers examined a group of bacteria called Burkholderia cepacia complex that causes serious infections and is difficult to treat because standard testing methods do not work well for identifying which antibiotics will work against it. The team analyzed data from nearly 1,900 bacterial samples collected from previous studies and independent laboratories to establish epidemiological cut-off values, which are measurements that help doctors determine if a bacteria strain is normal or unusual in its response to antibiotics. They successfully established cut-off values for four antibiotics but could not reliably determine one for trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole because the data was too inconsistent and spread out across a wide range. The researchers found that the cut-off values they did establish were too high to be practically useful for doctors trying to decide which antibiotics to prescribe for patients with these infections. These findings support the decision to remove these cut-off values from official clinical standards because the challenges with the data and the impractical results mean they cannot reliably guide treatment decisions for patients.

title: A Global Perspective on Migraine Attack Triggers: Understanding Differences Across Lifestyles, Religions, and Regions.
abstract: This review aims to summarize migraine attack triggers and understand variance across lifestyles, religions, and regions.Experts from 11 countries collaborated to suggest a definition of migraine attack triggers. After investigating the geographical distribution of various triggers, referring to an earlier review written by the International Headache Academy (iHEAD) of the International Headache Society, we collected literature and summarized findings on both globally observed triggers and region- or culture-specific triggers. The most common triggers included stress, menstruation, and sleep disturbances. Several triggers were observed only in certain cultural contexts, such as fasting during Ramadan or Yom Kippur, or in specific regions, including barometric pressure in Eastern Asia, Lodos winds in Türkiye, midnight sun in the Arctic region, and watermelon consumption in Brazil. We summarized migraine attack triggers reported universally and specifically in different settings. In addition to using conventional methodology, future studies should address the mechanisms and causality of these triggers.© 2026. llm_summary: Migraine headaches affect millions of people worldwide, but the things that trigger these painful attacks can vary greatly depending on where someone lives and their cultural background. Experts from eleven different countries worked together to review scientific studies and create a clear definition of migraine triggers, which are the things that cause these headaches to start. The researchers found that stress, menstrual cycles, and poor sleep were the most common triggers reported by people everywhere, but they also discovered that certain triggers only happened in specific regions or cultures, such as fasting during religious holidays like Ramadan, changes in air pressure in Eastern Asia, or even eating watermelon in Brazil. These findings show that doctors and patients need to understand both the universal triggers that affect most people and the unique triggers that matter in different parts of the world. Future research should focus on understanding exactly how and why these triggers cause migraines rather than just listing what they are.

title: Communication Difficulties and Management: The Lived Experience of Individuals With Frontotemporal Lobar Degeneration Spectrum Disorders.
abstract: Frontotemporal lobar degeneration (FTLD) is the neuropathology that underlies a collection of progressive clinical syndromes typically classified by the initial/primary symptom. For example, individuals with loss of word meaning as a first manifestation are often diagnosed with the semantic variant of primary progressive aphasia. Growing evidence suggests that language and communication can be impacted in all clinical syndromes across the FTLD spectrum, but the functional relevance of these symptoms has yet to be explored.The Frontotemporal Degeneration (FTD) Insights Survey is the largest community survey of individuals affected by FTLD. It was administered online and included questions related to demographics, symptoms, life participation, quality of life, and experiences with and hopes for treatment. Self-reported diagnoses of respondents included the nonfluent/agrammatic, semantic, and unspecified variants of primary progressive aphasia, semantic dementia, corticobasal syndrome, progressive supranuclear palsy, and behavioral variant FTD. Here, we grouped respondents according to whether they had a language-predominant (n = 43), motor-predominant (n = 43), or behavior-predominant (n = 90) variant of FTLD and used descriptive statistics to explore how they perceive their own communication difficulties and gauge their motivation for management.Over 65% of respondents in each group identified changes to communication as a symptom; subsequent analyses focused on the responses of this cohort. Across groups, word finding and speaking were two of the most frequently endorsed difficulties. Over 50% of each group identified improved communication as a treatment priority, reflecting the impact that these symptoms have on their day-to-day life. Speech-language therapy is an important approach to manage these changes and minimize their impact. Whereas 76% of the language and motor groups had attended speech-language therapy, this was true for only 16% of the behavior group.Individuals across the FTLD spectrum experience changes to communication that impact their social engagement and quality of life. Management needs to be tailored to the needs of each individual, but recommendations are provided based on the insights and group-level preferences reported here. Future research is needed to identify current referral practices and how to increase engagement in skilled communication interventions, especially for individuals with the behavioral variant of FTD.https://doi.org/10.23641/asha.33940597.

llm_summary: Frontotemporal lobar degeneration is a progressive brain disease that affects different people in different ways, with some experiencing language problems first, others having movement difficulties, and still others showing behavior changes. Researchers surveyed over 175 people living with this disease through an online questionnaire to understand how communication problems affected their daily lives and what treatments they wanted most. More than sixty-five percent of people in all three groups reported experiencing changes in communication, with word-finding and speaking difficulties being the most common complaints, and over half of each group said improving communication was their top priority for treatment. The study revealed a significant gap in care, as seventy-six percent of people with language or movement problems had received speech therapy, but only sixteen percent of people with behavior-focused symptoms had received this help. Future research needs to explore why fewer people with behavioral variants receive speech therapy and how to better connect all patients with communication specialists who can help them maintain their quality of life and social connections.

title: Evaluation of Modern Hematology-Oncology Home-Call: Optimizing Patient Care, Physician Wellbeing, and Trainee Education.
abstract: Traditional home-call managing after-hours pager communications remains a common component of hematology-oncology fellowship and modern practice. Little is known about these patient-related interactions and implications. This project aimed to characterize after-hours pager volumes and evaluate perceived impacts on care, physician wellbeing, and trainee education. We performed a mixed-methods study at a tertiary academic center, analyzing after-hours pager activity from 2020-2024 across Hematology Consult (HCP), Hematology Outpatient (HOP), and Medical Oncology (MOP) pagers. A survey of hematology-oncology fellows evaluated perceptions and attitudes toward the home-call experience using free-text responses and a 5-point Likert scale. After-hours pager burden was substantial and sustained. The MOP received >3,000 pages annually, with medians of 5-6 per weekday and 15-15.5 per weekend day. The HOP volume nearly doubled over the study period (960 to 1,721 annually) with median pager volumes of 1-3 per weekday and 2-7 per weekend day. The HCP volume ranged from 594-768 pages annually. Survey response rate was 58% (19/33). Only 16% of fellows endorsed educational value from patient calls on MOP or HOP, and ≤5% agreed that call tasks required physician-level expertise. Respondents reported that the pager resulted in fatigue, anxiety, and social disruptions. Free text responses revealed themes of low educational value, high non-urgent call volume, and system inefficiencies. Contemporary home-call had substantial pager burdens with limited actionability, adverse effects on wellbeing, and low educational value. Systems engineering, including triage processes and augmented patient education, could help optimize patient care, physician wellbeing, and trainee education.Copyright © 2026 American Society of Hematology.

llm_summary: Doctors who work in blood disorders and cancer care often have to respond to patient calls and messages after regular work hours, but little research has examined how this affects their wellbeing or training. Researchers at a major medical center studied after-hours pager activity over four years and surveyed doctors-in-training about their experiences with these nighttime and weekend calls. They found that doctors received thousands of pages each year, with particularly high volumes on weekends, yet only a small percentage of fellows felt these calls taught them anything valuable or required a doctor's expertise. The survey also revealed that constant paging caused fatigue, anxiety, and disrupted doctors' personal lives, while many calls involved routine issues that could have been handled differently. The researchers suggest that hospitals could improve this situation by creating better systems to sort urgent from non-urgent calls and by educating patients more thoroughly, which would ultimately benefit patient care, reduce doctor burnout, and improve training for future physicians.

title: Real-world effects of a sepsis early detection model integrated into clinical workflow: a quasi-experimental study.
abstract: Sepsis is a life-threatening condition in which delayed recognition and treatment are associated with increased mortality. While predictive models such as Epic's Early Detection of Sepsis Model (ESM) were developed to support early intervention, their real-world effects after integration into clinical workflows remain difficult to evaluate.To evaluate the real-world effects of ESM integrated into clinical workflow on clinical outcomes, antibiotic use, and harm-benefit tradeoffs.We conducted a quasi-experimental study in a single healthcare system using encounter-level data from inpatient settings. Inpatient mortality, prolonged hospitalization, antibiotic use, and sepsis prevalence (defined by EHR) were compared between the pre-acquisition period (3 June 2023 to 24 June 2024) and the online period (21 August 2024 to 26 December 2024) when the model became visible to clinicians. We also applied a counterfactual framework using models trained on pre-acquisition data to estimate expected outcomes without ESM and to quantify harms related to overtreatment and delayed treatment.Among 89,469 encounters, 75,215 occurred during the pre-acquisition period and 14,254 during the online period. In unadjusted analyses, inpatient mortality, prolonged hospitalization, antibiotic use, and EHR-defined sepsis proportion all decreased during the online period (all p≤0.006). In the counterfactual analyses, observed outcomes were lower than expected without ESM for mortality (1.21% vs 1.94%; p<0.001), prolonged hospitalization (5.56% vs 8.14%; p<0.001), and antibiotic use (43.52% vs 47.74%; p<0.001). False positive harm (37.72% vs 42.31%; p<0.001) was also lower than expected.Integration of ESM into clinical workflow was associated with improved patient outcomes, reduced antibiotic use, and decreased harm from overtreatment, without evidence of increased harm from delayed treatment, supporting a positive net clinical benefit and the safety and effectiveness of ESM under Software as a Medical Device principles.Thieme. llm_summary: Sepsis is a serious blood infection that can be deadly if doctors do not recognize and treat it quickly, which is why researchers developed computer prediction tools to alert doctors when patients might be developing this condition. Researchers studied what happened when one of these prediction tools, called the Early Detection of Sepsis Model, was added to a hospital's electronic health records system so doctors could see the alerts while caring for patients. After the tool became available to doctors, the hospital saw improvements in several important measures, including lower death rates, fewer patients staying in the hospital longer than expected, and less unnecessary antibiotic use compared to what would have been expected without the tool. The results suggest that using this prediction tool in real clinical settings helped patients by catching sepsis earlier and reducing overtreatment, without causing harm from delayed treatment of actual infections. These findings support the safety and effectiveness of using computer prediction models like this one to help doctors make better decisions about sepsis care in hospitals.

title: Global burden of liver disease: 2026 update.
abstract: Chronic liver disease (CLD) remains a major global health challenge, affecting more than 1.5 billion people worldwide and contributing to morbidity, mortality, and healthcare costs. Cirrhosis is the 12th leading cause of death globally and together with primary liver cancer accounts for nearly 2.4 million deaths annually, disproportionately affecting low- and middle-income countries. The principal etiologies driving the burden of liver disease include alcohol-associated liver disease, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), and chronic viral hepatitis (HBV and HCV). Demographic changes, rising obesity, and increasing alcohol consumption are expected to escalate the burden of ALD and MASLD, while improved access to vaccination and antiviral therapy continues to reshape the epidemiology of viral hepatitis. Acute liver failure, though rare, results in significant clinical and economic consequences and highlights striking regional disparities in etiology and outcomes. Cirrhosis carries elevated risk of progression to hepatic decompensation, acute-on-chronic liver failure, and hepatocellular carcinoma. These complications are associated with limited access to advanced therapies in resource-restricted regions. Importantly, Africa now bears the highest age-standardized mortality rates from cirrhosis and liver cancer, driven largely by viral hepatitis, aflatoxin exposure, and constrained access to care. Liver transplantation remains lifesaving but is accessible to a minority of patients globally. The escalating burden of MASLD, the growing interplay of metabolic disease and alcohol use, and persistent gaps in viral hepatitis diagnosis and treatment underscore the urgent need for integrated prevention, early detection, and equitable access to evidence-based liver care. This review provides an updated global assessment of the burden of liver disease, highlighting widening regional disparities, and outlining priorities and strategies for reducing its worldwide impact.Copyright © 2026. llm_summary: Chronic liver disease, which means long-term damage to the liver, affects more than 1. 5 billion people worldwide and is responsible for nearly 2. 4 million deaths each year, making it a serious global health problem that hits poorer countries especially hard. The main causes of liver disease are alcohol use, obesity-related fatty liver disease, and viral infections like hepatitis B and C, with these problems expected to worsen as obesity increases and drinking habits change around the world. Africa currently has the highest death rates from cirrhosis, which is severe scarring of the liver, and liver cancer, largely because of viral hepatitis infections, food contamination with aflatoxins, and limited access to medical treatment.

title: Transcatheter Valve-in-Valve versus Surgical Aortic Valve Replacement for Failed Bioprostheses: AI-ECG Age as a Marker of Mortality.
abstract: To analyze outcomes of patients with failed stented bioprostheses undergoing redo surgical aortic valve replacement (redo SAVR) versus valve-in-valve transcatheter AVR (ViV TAVR) and evaluate the impact of preoperative artificial-intelligence electrocardiogram (AI-ECG) age on all-cause mortality.Between 2010 and 2025, 1558 patients underwent repeat AVR for a failed bioprosthesis. To obtain a more homogenous cohort, patients with concomitant procedures were excluded, leaving 244 redo SAVR and 369 ViV TAVR cases. Propensity score matching (1:1) was then applied, yielding 167 balanced pairs. Preoperative ECGs were analyzed using a convolutional neural network to estimate AI-ECG age. The age gap was defined as AI-ECG age minus chronological age, with positive values indicating a physiologically older age.The matched cohort had a mean chronological age of 72±11 years and AI-ECG age of 68±10 years. Mean age gap was -3.6 ± 9 years (range, -22 to +15). Compared to redo SAVR, ViV TAVR was associated with higher median predismissal gradients (13 [9-19] vs 9 [7-13] mm Hg, P<0.001), and more frequent severe prosthesis-patient mismatch (PPM) (25% vs 11%, P<0.001). Operative mortality was 2.4% for redo-SAVR and 0.6% for ViV (P=0.37). A positive age gap was an independent predictor of all-cause mortality (HR: 1.20; 95% CI: 1.16-1.24; P<0.001). No significant interaction between treatment modality and age gap was observed (HR: 1.02, 95% CI 0.96-1.07; P=0.571). An increasing age gap was associated with measures of postoperative outcomes, including atrial fibrillation, blood product transfusion, prolonged ICU stay, and prolonged hospitalization.AI-ECG age gap is independently associated with mortality following repeat aortic valve replacement and provides prognostic information beyond chronological age. Increasing age gap is also associated with several markers of postoperative outcomes, supporting its role as a noninvasive measure of physiologic reserve.Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Inc.

llm_summary: Researchers examined patients who needed a second aortic valve replacement, which is surgery to replace a heart valve that had previously been replaced with a biological valve made from animal tissue. The study compared two treatment approaches: traditional open-heart surgery versus a less invasive catheter-based procedure where doctors thread a new valve through blood vessels to replace the failed one. They used artificial intelligence to analyze heart electrical patterns from patient electrocardiograms and created an "age gap" score by comparing the AI-estimated biological age of the heart to each patient's actual age, with positive scores indicating a heart that appeared older than it should be. The key finding was that patients with a larger positive age gap, meaning their hearts appeared significantly older than their chronological age, had worse survival outcomes after either type of valve replacement procedure. This research suggests that measuring the physiological age of the heart through artificial intelligence provides valuable information about which patients are at higher risk for complications and death, going beyond what doctors can learn from a patient's actual age alone.

title: Grade 3 Lung Carcinoids/NETs: The IASLC Pathology Committee Study with Proposal of a New Diagnostic Category.
abstract: Lung carcinoids are well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumors (NETs), designated in the current thoracic WHO classification as typical carcinoids (grade 1) and atypical carcinoids (grade 2), whereas rare tumors with carcinoid/NET morphology and >10 mitoses/2mm2 are designated as large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma (LCNEC). This approach, however, has been a matter of growing debate.Lung resections of tumors with carcinoid/NET morphology and >10 mitoses/2 mm2 were contributed by the members of IASLC Pathology Committee. Digitized slides and detailed clinicopathologic, immunohistochemical, and molecular data were collected and analyzed.In total, 28 cases meeting the study criteria were collected from 9 institutions in 6 countries. Tumors exhibited mean mitotic counts of 15/2mm2 (range, 11-30/2mm2) and mean hot-spot Ki-67 rate of 32% (range 13-54%). In all cases, Ki-67 was heterogeneous, containing cold-spot zones with Ki-67 of <1%-15%. In all cases, Rb and p53 showed wild-type pattern by immunohistochemistry. Next-generation sequencing (n=9) revealed wild-type RB1 and TP53, low TMB (1.3-3.3 mutations/Mb), and genomic alterations characteristic of lung carcinoids. The study cohort exhibited significantly worse OS and RFS than control groups of 117 typical and 52 atypical carcinoids (P<0.0001 for all comparisons).In this international multi-institutional study, we address a major unresolved issue for WHO classification. By assembling the largest cohort to-date of the study cases, we propose that they should be classified as grade 3 carcinoids/NETs rather than LCNEC to enable clinical management more aligned with their biology. The concurrent IASLC proposal to include Ki-67 as additional criterion for grade 3 carcinoids should further enhance this approach.Copyright © 2026 International Association for the Study of Lung Cancer. llm_summary: Lung carcinoids are slow-growing tumors of the lung that doctors have traditionally divided into two grades based on how fast the cancer cells are dividing, but some rare tumors with carcinoid features that divide very quickly have created confusion about how to classify them. Researchers from nine institutions across six countries collected 28 cases of these confusing tumors and studied their characteristics, including how many dividing cells they contained, genetic information, and how well patients survived after treatment. The tumors showed high numbers of dividing cells and genetic patterns that were actually more similar to slow-growing carcinoids than to the aggressive large cell neuroendocrine carcinomas they were previously labeled as, and patients with these tumors had much worse outcomes than those with typical slow-growing carcinoids. The researchers propose that these tumors should be reclassified as a new grade three category of carcinoids rather than being called large cell neuroendocrine carcinomas, which would better match how the tumors actually behave and help doctors treat patients more appropriately. This new classification system, especially when combined with measuring a marker called Ki-67 to assess how many cells are actively dividing.

title: Contrast-Associated Acute Kidney Injury: Comprehensive Review of Risk Factors, Pathophysiology, Definition and Management.
abstract: Contrast-associated acute kidney injury (CA-AKI) remains an important clinical concern, especially as percutaneous coronary interventions (PCI) are being increasingly performed. This review provides a comprehensive, evidence-based synthesis of CA-AKI, acknowledging a shift in terminology from "contrast-induced" to "contrast-associated" to reflect the interplay of co-existing non-contrast factors and patient comorbidities. A comprehensive literature search was performed in PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Library from inception through June 2025 using terms related to contrast-associated acute kidney injury, risk factors, pathophysiology, prevention, and management; studies were selected based on relevance, methodological quality, and clinical applicability. While the exact causal relationship between contrast exposure and AKI is debated, CA-AKI is associated with adverse outcomes, including prolonged hospitalization, increased healthcare costs, and higher morbidity and mortality, as well as procedural variables such as contrast volume. Pathophysiological mechanisms include afferent arteriolar dilatation, medullary ischemia, direct tubular epithelial injury, and mitochondrial dysfunction, which can lead to maladaptive repair and progression to CKD. Management focuses on preventive strategies- maintaining hemodynamic stability, optimizing volume status, minimizing contrast dose, and implementing nephrotoxin stewardship. Despite the use of validated risk scores and emerging biomarkers for earlier detection, management remains largely supportive. llm_summary: Contrast-associated acute kidney injury, which is damage to the kidneys that can occur after patients receive contrast dye during heart procedures, remains a serious concern as more people undergo these medical interventions. Researchers conducted a comprehensive review of scientific literature to understand the risk factors, how this kidney damage happens in the body, how it is defined, and the best ways to manage it. The study found that while the exact relationship between contrast dye and kidney injury is still debated, this condition is linked to serious consequences including longer hospital stays, higher medical costs, and increased risk of death or long-term kidney disease. The researchers identified that kidney damage occurs through several mechanisms including reduced blood flow to kidney tissue, direct injury to kidney cells, and problems with how cells repair themselves, which can eventually lead to chronic kidney disease. Moving forward, doctors should focus on preventing kidney injury through personalized treatment decisions, using digital health tools to monitor patients, and developing new targeted treatments that could stop the progression from acute kidney injury to permanent kidney disease.

title: Effectiveness of Medical-Behavioral Therapy in Patients with Fecal Incontinence.
abstract: Guidelines recommend individualized medical and behavioral therapy (MBT) for fecal incontinence (FI), yet its effectiveness remains poorly defined. We assessed the response to MBT in FI.In this 5-center U.S. trial, adults with FI received individualized MBT (dietary modifications, medications, and pelvic floor exercises) for up to 3 months. The primary outcome was a ≥75% reduction in FI frequency after 4 weeks of MBT. Secondary outcomes included 3-month FI, bowel habits, FI-related quality of life (QoL) and changes exceeding minimal clinically important differences (MCIDs).Among 260 participants, FI occurred approximately once daily on average, more than one-third of bowel movements were incontinent, and nearly 25% had undergone anorectal procedures and/or colon resection. Sixty (23%) participants responded at 1 month but only 39 (15%) had a sustained response at 3 months; 200 (77%) were non-responders. At 3 months, FI-QoL also improved in sustained responders (P≤.006). Greater reductions in FI frequency were associated with a higher likelihood of exceeding MCIDs for FI frequency (P<.006) and FI-QoL lifestyle and coping subscores (P≤.04). In multivariable analysis, a greater response was independently associated with higher baseline FI frequency and no external anal sphincter defects (P=.0002). For a given reduction in Bristol stool score, FI frequency declined more among participants with more frequent baseline FI (P=.002).Among patients with moderate-to-severe FI, 23% and 15% responded to MBT at 1 and 3 months. Responses at 3-months were clinically meaningful, associated with improved QoL, and more likely in patients with higher baseline FI frequency, and no visible external sphincter defects.Copyright © 2026. llm_summary: Fecal incontinence, which is the inability to control bowel movements, affects many people and causes significant problems with quality of life, yet doctors have not clearly understood how well standard treatments actually work. Researchers at five medical centers across the United States studied 260 adults with moderate to severe fecal incontinence who received individualized treatment combining dietary changes, medications, and pelvic floor exercises (exercises that strengthen the muscles controlling bowel movements) for up to three months. Only 23 percent of patients showed significant improvement after one month, and this number dropped to just 15 percent by three months, though those who did improve experienced meaningful gains in their quality of life and bowel control. title: IMPROVED SEVERITY AND QUALITY-OF-LIFE MEASURES FOR FECAL INCONTINENCE: DEVELOPMENT OF THE MINNESOTA (MiNi)-FISI AND MiNi-FI-QOL.
abstract: Among patients with fecal incontinence (FI), the 29-item quality-of-life (FI-QoL) instrument is widely used but lengthy and only modestly correlated with symptom severity. We devised and evaluated revised symptom severity and FI-QoL instruments.Among 822 individuals with FI from a multicenter FI-QoL cohort (n=118), community (n=170), pelvic floor clinic (n=423), and clinical trials (n=111), FI severity was assessed using the Fecal Incontinence Severity Index (FISI), the Fecal Incontinence Symptom Severity scale, and a derived combined instrument, the Minnesota FISI (MiNi-FISI). FI specific-QoL was assessed with the 29-item FI-QoL, a new Minnesota FI-QoL (MiNi-FI-QoL) and SF-36 instruments. Associations between FI severity and QoL and the validity of the MiNi-FI-QoL were examined; findings were validated in a separate trial (n=260).Among 1082 patients, FI symptoms and QoL impact were worse in clinic and trial patients than community participants (P<.001). FISI scores explained 26% of FI-QoL variance, increasing to 60% when staying near a toilet to prevent FI was included (P<.001). For a given FISI score, FI-QoL declined as time spent near a toilet increased. Iterative reduction yielded a new 11-item Minnesota (MiNi) FI-QoL score, which captured 97% of the variance in the 29-item FI-QoL and correlated with SF36 scores. A revised 7-item Minnesota FISI (MiNi-FISI) explained 46% of FI-QoL variance vs 36% for the original FISI.The MiNi-FISI and MiNi-FI-QoL are concise, psychometrically derived short forms with strong performance across diverse cohorts. Further validation, including direct patient input to confirm content validity, is warranted.Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Inc.
