llm_summary: Researchers examined whether they could create shorter and simpler tools to measure how severe fecal incontinence (loss of bowel control) is and how much it affects a person's quality of life, since the existing 29-question quality-of-life test was long and didn't always match up well with symptom severity. The study involved over 1,000 people with fecal incontinence from different settings including clinics, community groups, and clinical trials, and researchers tested various measurement tools to see which ones worked best at capturing both symptom severity and quality-of-life impact. The researchers discovered that the original severity scores only explained about 26 percent of the variation in quality-of-life scores, but when they added information about how much time people spent staying near a toilet to prevent accidents, this jumped to 60 percent. Through careful analysis, they created two new shorter tools: a 7-item severity scale and an 11-item quality-of-life scale that captured nearly all the information from the longer original tests while being much quicker and easier to use. title: Multi-target blood test for hepatocellular carcinoma early detection: a cross-sectional analysis of the prospective ALTUS study.
abstract: Globally, 350 million people are at risk for HCC. Ultrasound screening is recommended but is limited by poor early-stage sensitivity and low adherence. This study evaluated whether the multi-target HCC blood test (mt-HBT) demonstrates non-inferior sensitivity for early-stage HCC compared with ultrasound and assessed its specificity.This prospective, multicenter study, conducted between July 2021 and June 2025 in the United States, evaluated the performance of the mt-HBT in a head-to-head comparison with standard-of-care ultrasound among adults with cirrhosis or chronic HBV infection who were eligible for routine HCC screening. All participants underwent computed tomography or magnetic resonance imaging as a reference standard. The co-primary outcomes were non-inferiority of mt-HBT to ultrasound for early-stage HCC sensitivity, with sequential testing of superiority, and mt-HBT specificity. A secondary outcome was overall (any-stage) mt-HBT sensitivity.Of 3089 participants, 2293 were evaluable with paired ultrasound and mt-HBT results. Thirty-seven HCCs were identified, with 27 classified as early stage by Milan criteria. Early-stage HCC sensitivities were 66.7% (95% CI, 47.8-81.4%) for mt-HBT and 22.2% (95% CI, 10.6-40.8%) for ultrasound, confirming mt-HBT non-inferiority within the prespecified 5% margin. The specificity for mt-HBT was 81.8% (95% CI, 80.1-83.4%), which did not meet the pre-specified co-primary outcome of 82%. Ultrasound specificity was 98.6% (95% CI, 98.0-99.0%). Any-stage HCC sensitivity was 73.0% (95% CI, 57.0-84.6%) for mt-HBT and 29.7% (95% CI, 17.5-45.8%) for ultrasound. No serious adverse events occurred during the blood collection process.The mt-HBT had higher observed sensitivity than ultrasound for early-stage HCC, with a paired absolute difference of 44.4% (95% CI, 20.2-63.8); however, specificity did not meet the prespecified target.The trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05064553) IMPACT AND IMPLICATIONS: HCC screening remains limited by the suboptimal sensitivity of ultrasound, particularly among patients with obesity and steatotic liver disease. In this prospective multicenter study, a multi-target HCC blood test demonstrated substantially higher sensitivity for early-stage HCC detection than ultrasound while maintaining favorable screening performance across diverse patient subgroups. These findings are important for clinicians, researchers, and patients because they support further evaluation of blood-based approaches to address known limitations of imaging-based screening.Copyright © 2026. llm_summary: Hundreds of millions of people worldwide are at risk for liver cancer, but current screening methods like ultrasound imaging miss many early cases and many patients skip these screenings altogether. Researchers tested a new blood test that looks for multiple markers of liver cancer against standard ultrasound screening in nearly 2,300 patients with cirrhosis or chronic hepatitis B infection, using CT or MRI scans as the gold standard to confirm which patients actually had cancer. The blood test detected early-stage liver cancer in about 67 percent of cases compared to only 22 percent for ultrasound, which is a major improvement, though the blood test's ability to correctly identify patients without cancer was slightly lower than hoped at 82 percent instead of the target of 82 percent or higher. These results suggest that blood-based screening could help catch liver cancer earlier than imaging alone, which is especially important for patients with obesity or fatty liver disease where ultrasound works poorly. The researchers say more work is needed to refine the blood test before it can replace ultrasound in routine screening, but the findings support developing blood tests as a better option for detecting early liver cancer.

title: Minimally Invasive Hemi-Hysterectomy for Symptomatic Uterine Didelphys: Surgical Technique and Fertility-Preserving Considerations.
abstract: To describe the step-by-step approach to hemi-hysterectomy in a patient with uterine didelphys to reduce pelvic pain while preserving fertility.Tertiary academic medical center.A 32-year-old G0 patient with uterine didelphys, Obstructed Hemivagina and Ipsilateral Renal Anomaly (OHVIRA) Syndrome, and chronic pelvic pain. She had previously undergone resection of an oblique vaginal septum for hematocolpos. She presented with persistent pelvic pain requiring multiple emergency room visits, copious white-yellow vaginal discharge and leukocytosis of unknown origin with white blood cell count of 14,000 µL. Exam revealed a hypoplastic left cervix which was thought to be obstructing menstrual flow resulting in chronic pelvic pain.Robotic-assisted laparoscopic left hemi-hysterectomy and salpingectomy were performed. The left vaginal cuff was closed with special consideration given to the contralateral right cervix, which remained in situ. A medial defect in the right uterus was closed in multiple layers with appropriate reapproximation. Final diagnostic hysteroscopy was performed and confirmed patency and integrity of the remaining uterine cavity. The surgery and postoperative course were uncomplicated. Her chronic pelvic pain, abnormal vaginal discharge, and leukocytosis of unknown origin resolved after treatment.Hemi-hysterectomy is not a standard treatment for uterine didelphys-associated pelvic pain but may be considered in highly selected patients with persistent symptoms attributable to one hemiuterus after treatment of associated obstructive anatomy and careful exclusion of alternative etiologies. When pursued, meticulous preoperative planning and surgical technique are essential to preserve the contralateral hemiuterus and its reproductive potential.Copyright © 2026. llm_summary: A 32-year-old woman with a rare condition called uterine didelphys, which means she had two separate uteruses instead of one, suffered from chronic pelvic pain that persisted even after previous surgery to remove a blockage in her vaginal canal. Doctors performed a minimally invasive robotic surgery to remove her left uterus and fallopian tube while carefully preserving her right uterus and its ability to become pregnant in the future. After the surgery, the woman's chronic pain, abnormal vaginal discharge, and elevated white blood cell count all resolved completely, and she recovered without complications. This case demonstrates that removing one half of a double uterus can be an effective treatment option for women with severe pain from this rare condition, but only when the pain clearly comes from one specific uterus and other possible causes have been ruled out. Doctors emphasize that this type of surgery requires very careful planning and precise surgical technique to protect the remaining uterus and preserve a woman's future ability to have children.

Some patients experience ongoing pain in the anorectal region (the area around the anus and rectum) after this procedure, which may be related to pelvic floor dysfunction (weakness or tension in the muscles that support pelvic organs) and central pelvic sensitization (a condition where the nervous system becomes overly sensitive to pain signals in the pelvic area).

title: Cardiac Remodeling, Prognostic markers, and Cardiovascular Outcomes Across Heart Failure Phenotypes in Adults with Congenital Heart Disease.
abstract: Data comparing cardiac remodeling, prognostic markers, and cardiovascular outcomes across heart failure (HF) phenotypes in adults with congenital heart disease (CHD) are limited.In this study, adults with CHD and HF were classified based on left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF): HF with reduced EF (HFrEF; LVEF <40%), HF with mildly reduced EF (HFmrEF; LVEF 41%-49%), and HF with preserved EF (HFpEF; LVEF ≥50% with pulmonary artery wedge pressure ≥15 mmHg). Cardiac function (strain imaging), prognostic markers (NT-proBNP and peak oxygen consumption), and cardiovascular outcomes (HF hospitalization and cardiovascular death/heart transplantation) were compared across groups.Among 1,303 patients, 304 (23%) had HFrEF, 551 (42%) had HFmrEF, and 448 (34%) had HFpEF. There was a graded worsening of biatrial and right ventricular function from HFpEF to HFmrEF to HFrEF (all p<0.001). Despite less severe chamber dysfunction, HFpEF was characterized by higher NT-proBNP levels and lower peak oxygen consumption compared with HFmrEF. HFrEF was associated with the highest adjusted risk of HF hospitalization (hazard ratio, 1.52; p=0.005) and cardiovascular death/heart transplantation (hazard ratio, 1.74; p=0.002), compared to HFmrEF and HFpEF. HF therapy was associated with lower event rates overall, with the strongest association in HFrEF, a more modest association in HFmrEF, and no significant association in HFpEF.In adults with CHD and HF, LVEF-defined HF phenotypes identified distinct patterns of cardiac remodeling and prognosis, with worse cardiac remodeling and adverse outcomes observed in the HFrEF phenotype. These findings support use of EF phenotype-based approach to HF management in CHD.Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Inc.

llm_summary: Researchers examined how heart failure develops differently in adults born with heart defects, since previous studies have not thoroughly compared these different patterns. The study looked at 1,303 patients with congenital heart disease and heart failure, dividing them into three groups based on how well their hearts pumped blood: those with severely weakened pumping (23 percent), those with mildly weakened pumping (42 percent), and those with normal pumping but fluid buildup (34 percent). The results showed that patients with the most severely weakened hearts had the worst overall heart function and the highest risk of needing hospitalization or experiencing death or heart transplant, while those with normal pumping had better heart structure but surprisingly high levels of stress markers in their blood. Heart failure medications worked best for patients with the most severely weakened hearts, worked somewhat for those with mildly weakened hearts, and did not significantly help those with normal pumping but fluid buildup. These findings suggest that doctors should tailor heart failure treatment based on how well a patient's heart pumps, rather than using a one-size-fits-all approach for all adults with congenital heart disease.

title: Reframing the Gut-Brain Axis: The Gut Wall as a Neural Immune Interface in Multiple Sclerosis and Autoimmune Neurological Diseases.
abstract: Gut wall physiology in multiple sclerosis (MS) and autoimmune neurologic diseases remains underexplored. This review examines gut wall dysfunctions' contribution to MS and autoimmune neurological disorder pathogenesis and progression. We discuss 3 inter-related aspects of gut physiology: intestinal barrier, enteric nervous system (ENS), and mucosal immunity. We highlight the ENS as a putative target of immune injury in selected antibody-mediated and T cell-associated neurologic diseases. Finally, we propose a unifying framework in which the gut functions as a site of immune priming and target of autoimmune injury, bridging microbiome-driven mechanisms in MS with ENS-directed autoimmunity across neurologic diseases. llm_summary: Researchers examined how the gut wall, which is the lining of the digestive system, may play an important role in multiple sclerosis and other autoimmune neurological diseases where the body's immune system attacks the nervous system. This review looked at three connected parts of how the gut works: the intestinal barrier that controls what enters the bloodstream, the enteric nervous system which is a network of nerves in the gut, and the immune system in the gut lining. The authors found that the enteric nervous system may be a target where the immune system causes damage in certain neurological diseases, particularly those involving antibodies or specific immune cells. The research proposes a new way of thinking about these diseases by suggesting the gut serves as both a place where immune responses start and a place where autoimmune damage occurs, connecting gut bacteria-related mechanisms in multiple sclerosis with immune attacks on the gut's nervous system across different neurological conditions. This framework could help scientists and doctors better understand how gut health influences neurological diseases and may lead to new treatment approaches targeting the gut-brain connection.

title: Anti-Fungal and Toxicology Assessment of ISFP10, an Inhibitor of Fungal Phosphoglucomutase (PGM).
abstract: The novel small molecule ISFP10 inhibits fungal phosphoglucomutase (PGM) activity in Aspergillus fumigatus and Pneumocystis spp. With 50-fold selectivity over the human isoform, conferred by a conserved cysteine residue present in several pathogenic fungi, ISFP10 may represent a promising broad-spectrum antifungal. We evaluated its activity against Candida albicans and Candida glabrata, followed by toxicology assessment in mice.Minimum inhibitory concentration susceptibilities were performed on three strains of C. albicans and C. glabrata and compared with fluconazole. Growth inhibition was further assessed in an 8-h, concentration-dependent growth assay. For toxicology, C57BL6 mice received once-daily intraperitoneal injections of vehicle control (dimethyl sulfoxide) or ISFP10 (10 mg/kg) for 7 days. Body weight, complete blood count (CBC), blood chemistry, histopathology of major organs, and lung extracellular matrix (ECM) and cytokine levels (ELISA, qPCR) were analyzed.ISFP10 inhibited all tested Candida strains with significantly greater potency than fluconazole. It also showed concentration-dependent inhibition of growth in liquid culture. In mice, no significant differences in daily or final body weight, ECM transcript levels, or interleukin (IL)-6 expression were observed between groups. Tumor necrosis factor-α (TNFα) levels in lung tissue were significantly reduced in ISFP10-treated animals, suggesting a potential anti-inflammatory effect. Blood chemistry and CBC revealed minor abnormalities (increased neutrophils, decreased potassium), but these were not clinically significant. Histopathologic evaluation showed no evidence of organ toxicity.ISFP10 demonstrates potent antifungal properties against C. albicans and C. glabrata and a favorable safety profile in vivo, supporting its further development as a potential broad-spectrum antifungal agent.© 2026. llm_summary: Researchers examined a new experimental drug called ISFP10 that targets a specific enzyme found in fungal infections, which are serious health problems that current treatments like fluconazole sometimes cannot effectively fight. The team tested how well ISFP10 worked against common fungal infections called Candida in laboratory samples and then gave the drug to mice for a week to check if it caused any harmful side effects. The drug proved to be much more powerful than fluconazole at stopping the growth of Candida fungi, and it worked in a dose-dependent way, meaning higher amounts killed more fungal cells. In the mice that received ISFP10, researchers found no serious organ damage or dangerous blood changes, though the drug did reduce inflammation markers in the lungs, which could be beneficial for patients. These promising results suggest that ISFP10 deserves further testing and development as a potential new treatment for fungal infections, though more research in larger animal studies and eventually human patients will be needed before it can be used in medical practice.

title: NCCN Risk Groups Do Not Predict Adverse Pathology or Oncologic Outcomes Among Patients With Grade Group 1 Prostate Cancer in the MRI Era.
abstract: Prior studies in the pre-MRI era suggest that patients with NCCN Intermediate and High Risk Grade Group 1 prostate cancer (GG1 PCa) on biopsy have increased risk for adverse oncologic outcomes. However, prostate MRI has altered patient selection for biopsy and improved prostate sampling. Herein, we examined factors associated with adverse pathologic features (APF) at radical prostatectomy (RP) and biochemical recurrence (BCR) among patients with GG1 in the MRI era.A prospectively maintained institutional prostate cancer registry identified patients with GG1 PCa on biopsy who underwent RP from 2000 to 2023, stratified by MRI use. Multivariable logistic regression and Cox regression identified factors associated with APF at RP (GG3-5, ≥ pT3a, or pN1) and BCR free survival (two consecutive PSA ≥ 0.2 ng/mL), respectively.Among patients without MRI (n = 6732), NCCN risk group was associated with APF, BCR, and distant metastasis. Among 302 patients with GG1 and pre-operative MRI, NCCN risk group was associated with neither APF nor BCR. Age (OR 1.07, 95% CI 1.01-1.14, p = 0.01), PIRADS (p = 0.01), and % core positivity (OR 1.02, 95% CI 1.00-1.03, p = 0.04) were associated with APF. Age (HR 1.07, 95% CI 1.01-1.13, p = 0.03), APF (HR 4.36, 95% CI 2.14-8.86, p < 0.001), and positive margins (HR 4.88, 95% CI 2.39-9.98, p < 0.001) were associated with BCR.Prior to prostate MRI, NCCN risk groups offered meaningful prognostication among patients with GG1 PCa. However, the utility of NCCN risk groups for GG1 in the MRI era appears limited. Contemporary risk stratification for GG1 should focus on biopsy and MRI characteristics rather than NCCN criteria.© 2026 Wiley Periodicals LLC.

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether a standard risk classification system called NCCN risk groups could predict which patients with early-stage prostate cancer would have worse outcomes after surgery. They compared patients who had prostate MRI scans (a detailed imaging test) before surgery to older patients who did not have MRI scans, tracking whether cancer returned or spread in both groups. Among patients without MRI scans, the NCCN risk groups did help predict worse outcomes, but surprisingly, among patients who had MRI scans before surgery, the NCCN risk groups were not useful for predicting problems. Instead, factors like patient age, MRI findings, and how much of the biopsy samples contained cancer cells were better at predicting which patients would have worse outcomes. The study suggests that doctors should stop relying on the traditional NCCN risk groups for early-stage prostate cancer patients and instead focus on newer information from MRI scans and biopsy characteristics to better predict which patients need more aggressive treatment.

title: Impella purge solutions in patients receiving extracorporeal membrane oxygenation.
abstract: The optimal Impella purge solution in patients receiving concomitant ECMO and Impella (ECPELLA) support remains to be elucidated. We aimed to assess Impella device function in patients supported by ECPELLA receiving heparin-containing or anticoagulant-free (5% dextrose or sodium bicarbonate) purge solutions. Of 25 included patients, 14 received anticoagulant-free and 11 received heparin-containing purge solutions, with a median of five days of ECPELLA support. The only episode of Impella device malfunction occurred in the heparin-containing group. Given the low event rate and apparent maintenance of acceptable device longevity, use of anticoagulant-free purge solutions alongside systemic anticoagulation in ECPELLA patients may be reasonable but requires validation in an appropriately powered study.© 2026. llm_summary: Researchers examined the best way to keep a heart-pumping device called an Impella working properly when patients also receive a machine that does the work of both the heart and lungs, a combination treatment known as ECPELLA support. The study included 25 patients who received ECPELLA treatment for about five days on average, with some patients getting a purge solution containing blood thinner and others getting a purge solution without blood thinner. The results showed that only one device problem occurred, and it happened in the group that received the blood thinner purge solution, while the group without blood thinner in the purge solution had no device problems. These findings suggest that using a purge solution without blood thinner may be safe and effective for ECPELLA patients since the heart-pumping device continued to work well in both groups. However, the researchers noted that because so few problems occurred, larger and more carefully designed studies are needed to confirm whether anticoagulant-free purge solutions are truly the better choice for these critically ill patients.

title: Geographic Variation in Diagnostic Codes Associated With Mild Cognitive Impairment, Alzheimer Disease, and Related Dementias.
abstract: Mild cognitive impairment (MCI), Alzheimer disease (AD), and AD-related dementias (ADRD) are growing public health concerns. Regional, demographic, and clinical differences in these diagnoses and associated comorbid conditions may inform strategies to improve prevention, care, and outcomes. To assess the demographic and geographic distribution of patients in the United States with coded MCI or AD/ADRD, the prevalence of common comorbidities, and the frequency and timing of progression to complicated MCI or AD/ADRD within 180 days, using data from the American Academy of Neurology's former Axon Registry.This observational study included adults aged 50-89 years with at least 1 outpatient encounter between 2017 and 2023 in 201 participating US neurology practices. Registry data were linked to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention's 2019 Social Determinants of Health data set to assign patients to geographic regions. ICD-10 codes were used to identify MCI and AD/ADRD diagnoses, define comorbid conditions, and classify "complicated" MCI or AD/ADRD (e.g., with behavioral disturbances). The primary outcomes were odds of coded MCI/AD/ADRD, prevalence of top comorbidities, and proportion of patients progressing to complicated MCI/AD/ADRD within 180 days of initial diagnosis, stratified by region.Of 1,144,081 individuals with at least 1 documented outpatient encounter, 146,273 (12.8%) had MCI or AD/ADRD ICD codes. Of those, 65,088 (44.5%) were in the South, 35,027 (23.9%) in the Midwest, 30,008 (20.5%) in the Northeast, and 16,134 (11.0%) in the West. Unadjusted odds of MCI/AD/ADRD codes were 0.170 (Northeast), 0.155 (South), 0.134 (West), and 0.125 (Midwest). Among those with uncomplicated MCI or AD/ADRD at first encounter, the highest proportion of progression to complicated codes within 180 days was in the Northeast (2.04%), followed by the West (1.91%), South (1.24%), and Midwest (1.06%). Common comorbidities included hypertension, depression or mood disorders, and gait abnormalities.These findings highlight geographic and demographic variations in coded MCI/AD/ADRD prevalence and progression. Future studies should address underlying factors and the impact of comorbidities on outcomes, ultimately guiding more targeted approaches to dementia prevention and management. Future studies that phenotype AD/ADRD beyond the use of ICD codes can further validate the results.

title: From Hippocrates to Biologics, The Evolving History of Pericarditis: A Review.
abstract: Pericarditis remains a common and clinically relevant cardiovascular condition whose diagnosis and management have evolved substantially over time. Understanding this historical progression provides important context for contemporary practice and emerging therapeutic strategies. Early descriptions, dating back to Hippocrates, framed pericarditis as a clinical observation, with more precise diagnostic characterization emerging in the 19th century through the work of Laennec and later refined by clinicians such as Spodick and Hatle. Initial treatment approaches were largely symptomatic or surgical, including pericardiectomy for advanced constrictive disease. The mid-twentieth century marked a shift toward medical therapy with the introduction of nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs and corticosteroids, which improved symptom control but were limited by high recurrence rates. The advent of echocardiography transformed pericardial disease evaluation by enabling noninvasive diagnosis, hemodynamic assessment, and safer pericardiocentesis. More recently, cardiac magnetic resonance imaging has further advanced care by allowing detailed tissue characterization and improved risk stratification. Randomized trials established colchicine as a cornerstone therapy for both acute and recurrent pericarditis. A major paradigm shift has occurred with the recognition of autoinflammatory mechanisms underlying recurrent disease and the introduction of targeted interleukin-1 inhibition, including anakinra and rilonacept, particularly for refractory cases. Together, these advances reflect a transition from empirical management toward mechanism-based, personalized care. Ongoing progress in imaging, biomarker integration, and targeted immunomodulation is expected to further refine diagnosis, treatment, and long-term outcomes for patients with pericardial disease.

title: Genetic and cellular architecture of breast cancer risk across ancestries.
abstract: Breast cancer genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified more than 200 susceptibility loci, but most studies are dominated by European and East Asian populations.We analyzed breast cancer GWAS summary statistics from African (AFR), East Asian (EAS), European (EUR), and Hispanic/Latina (H/L) samples (159,297 cases and 212,102 controls). We estimated logit-scale SNP-based heritability, polygenicity, and cross-ancestry genetic correlation, partitioned heritability across functional annotations, and integrated GWAS results with the Tabula Sapiens single-cell atlas using scDRS+.The logit-scale heritability of breast cancer ranged from h2=0.47 (SE = 0.07) in EAS to AFR h2=0.61 (SE = 0.10), with no significant differences across ancestries (p = 0.63). The model-implied number of non-null susceptibility SNPs in the sparse normal-mixture effect-size model also varied from 4,446 (SE = 3,100) in EAS to 8,308 (SE = 2,751) in AFR, but differences were not significant across ancestries (p = 0.55). Cross-sample genetic correlations varied, with the strongest correlation between EUR and EAS (ρ=0.79, SE = 0.08) and weakest between AFR and H/L (ρ=0.26, SE = 0.24). Regulatory annotations were enriched for breast cancer heritability across samples. Integration with single-cell expression profiles implicated ancestry-shared associations with innate immune, secretory epithelial, and stromal cell types.These results indicate substantial cross-ancestry sharing of breast cancer polygenic architecture, highlight a consistent contribution of regulatory variation, and identify convergent cellular contexts that motivate functional follow-up and inform expectations for the transferability and attainable performance of common-variant risk prediction across populations.Published by Oxford University Press 2026.

title: Association of Postoperative Complication with Subsequent Mental Health Disorders: A Population-Based Study.
abstract: Postoperative complication is associated with lower health-related quality of life, but its association with subsequent mental health disorders is less well understood. We examined whether 30-day postoperative complication was associated with new or worsening mental health disorders.This population-based retrospective study included adults ≥18 years of age undergoing 1 of 25 common operations in Ontario, Canada, from January 2007 through December 2019. The primary outcome was new or worsening mental health disorders within 1 year, stratified by 30-day postoperative complication. Multivariable regression using generalized estimating equations adjusted for patient, provider, and procedural factors.Among 1,165,711 patients (median age 60 years; 61.9% female), 5.0% developed new or worsening mental health disorders within 1 year. The rate was higher among patients with a complication (6.2% vs 4.9%; p < 0.001). Complication was associated with higher adjusted odds (aOR) of mental health disorders at 1 year (aOR 1.28; 95% CI 1.24 to 1.32), with the strongest association at 30 days (1.77; 1.65 to 1.90). At 1 year, the association was present among patients without prior mental health history (1.31; 1.17-1.46), but not among those with pre-existing history. Patients with complication also had more new psychiatrist consultations (3.2% vs 1.5%; 2.02; 1.69 to 2.42) and a higher rate of new psychotropic prescriptions. Findings were generally consistent across other time points.Postoperative complication was associated with subsequent mental health disorders, specifically among patients without prior mental health history. llm_summary: Researchers examined whether surgical complications occurring within 30 days of operation were associated with new or worsening mental health disorders in a population-based study of 1,165,711 adults undergoing 25 common surgical procedures in Ontario, Canada between 2007 and 2019. title: Progressive motor impairment from intracerebral critical demyelinating lesions.
abstract: Focal critical demyelinating lesions anatomically associated with progressive motor impairment are described in multiple sclerosis (MS) and restricted demyelinating diseases, typically within the spinal cord lateral column and ventral cervicomedullary junction (CMJ). This study describes such lesions within the intracerebral corticospinal tracts.We retrospectively reviewed people seen at Mayo MS Clinic (2002-2025) with progressive central nervous system demyelinating disease and progressive (≥ 1 year) upper motor neuron weakness anatomically associated with a presumed demyelinating lesion of the cerebral white matter, internal capsule, or upper brainstem, excluding alternative spinal cord or CMJ lesions. Demographics, disease course, Expanded Disability Status Scale (EDSS), MS disease-modifying therapy use, brain and spinal cord magnetic resonance imaging, cerebrospinal fluid studies and neuropathology findings were reviewed.Seventeen people had an intracerebral critical demyelinating lesion: cerebral white matter in 12 (70%), internal capsule in 3 (18%) and upper brainstem in 2 (12%). Ten were female, and all were white. Progression from onset course was 13 (76%) and from relapse onset was 4 (24%). Median, interquartile range (IQR) for age at progressive motor impairment onset was 46 (IQR 38-52) years, and EDSS at last evaluation was 5.5 (IQR 4.0-5.5). Sixteen (94%) had progressive spastic hemiparesis and 1 (6%) monoparesis. Cognitive impairment occurred in 6/12 (50%) and seizures in 3/12 (25%) with cerebral white matter critical lesions. Abnormal intrathecal production of immunoglobulin G markers was consistent with MS in 10/15 (66%). Neuropathology confirmed demyelination in 4/6 biopsies.Intracerebral critical demyelinating lesions associated with progressive motor impairment can rarely occur along the corticospinal tracts of the brain.© 2026. title: MRI Characteristics of Myelin Oligodendrocyte Glycoprotein Antibody-Associated Disease: A Review.
abstract: Myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease (MOGAD) is a demyelinating disease distinct from multiple sclerosis (MS) and aquaporin-4 antibody-positive neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (AQP4+NMOSD). Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is central to confirming attacks, defining lesion distribution, and excluding alternative diagnoses and is a key component of the 2023 MOGAD diagnostic criteria. However, its imaging spectrum and lesion evolution remain underrecognized in practice, and variability in imaging parameters can contribute to delayed diagnosis and suboptimal treatment.This article summarizes the hallmark MRI features of optic nerve, brain, and spinal cord involvement in MOGAD, including key findings from the 2023 diagnostic criteria, supported by illustrative figures and detailed tables. The characteristic evolution of MRI abnormalities in MOGAD is highlighted, including radiologic lag, lesion dynamics during acute attacks, and frequent T2-lesion resolution, contrasting with the persistent lesions typical of MS. A recommended MRI protocol for acute attacks is proposed, and the timing and utility of rebaselining MRI (ie, repeating the MRI to establish a new baseline) after onset are reviewed. The clinical course of MOGAD is of attack-related neuroinflammation evident clinically and radiologically, and asymptomatic radiological activity is rare, suggesting that surveillance MRI has less clinical utility than in MS and less value as a surrogate biomarker in clinical trials. MRI features that differentiate MOGAD from MS and AQP4+NMOSD are summarized and imaging red flags suggestive of alternative diagnoses are highlighted. Finally, emerging advanced imaging, artificial intelligence in MOGAD imaging, and the link between imaging and immunopathogenesis are reviewed.MRI is central to MOGAD evaluation, and recognition of the characteristic imaging features and lesion dynamics outlined in this review can aid diagnosis. Application of the standardized MRI protocol summarized here can optimize use in clinical practice and promote harmonization across research studies. Future imaging and artificial intelligence applications may improve diagnosis, disease monitoring, and understanding of MOGAD pathogenesis.

title: Evaluating a shared decision engagement system in the NCI community oncology research program: a multi-level RCT.
abstract: Improving patient-centered care and communication in breast cancer remains challenging in the complex and evolving landscape of breast cancer care delivery.The SharES (Alliance A231901CD) trial was carried out in collaboration with the NCI Community Oncology Research Program Alliance Research Base to evaluate a multi-level intervention in a crossed design: 1) a patient-level randomized intervention of the evidence-based iCanDecide online tool with added emotional support enhancements (iCanDecide-ESE), intended to promote better information uptake by supporting management of distress associated with a new diagnosis vs. the standard version (iCanDecide-S); and 2) a clinic-level stepped-wedge randomized Clinician Dashboard intervention. Patient-reported outcomes assessed 5-weeks after registration were knowledge about breast cancer locoregional treatment (primary outcome), cancer worry and breast cancer self-efficacy (key secondary outcomes). We evaluated outcomes using linear mixed models considering the nesting of individuals within clinic across time periods.We enrolled 542 (403 evaluable) patients and 54 clinicians across 25 surgical clinics. The confidence intervals for all outcomes included zero but excluded pre-specified clinically important differences in the knowledge score. We found good fidelity to the intervention components and considerable variation in the primary outcome across sites.The addition of emotional support components to a patient support tool previously found effective is unlikely to result in clinically important improvements in knowledge, cancer worry, or breast cancer self-efficacy. The strong engagement of NCORP sites, clinicians and patients with the study and intervention components suggests future cancer care delivery studies could leverage implementation strategies to promote multi-level patient-centered communication interventions.ClinicalTrials.gov NCT04549571. title: FDG PET characteristics of intraneural perineurioma: patient series.
abstract: Intraneural perineuriomas (INPs) are rare benign peripheral nerve sheath tumors with characteristic clinical and MRI features. Their 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) positron emission tomography (PET) appearance has not been characterized in a patient series. The authors evaluated FDG uptake patterns in INP.The authors retrospectively reviewed that data of patients with confirmed INP who had MRI and FDG PET studies that included the affected nerve. Eight patients were included (5 male and 3 female; mean age 30.8 years, range 16-61 years). All lesions showed mildly increased FDG uptake relative to the contralateral nerve (lesion maximum standardized uptake value [SUVmax]: mean 1.5, median 1.2, range 1.1-3.5; contralateral nerve SUVmax: mean 0.9, median 0.9, range 0.8-1.0) and skeletal muscle background (SUVmean: mean 0.8, range 0.5-0.9). Six patients had denervation edema and/or fatty atrophy, without appreciably increased FDG uptake in the affected musculature. No additional abnormal hypermetabolic foci were identified.INPs generally demonstrate low-level FDG uptake. PET is best regarded as a complementary test when already available or when metabolic characterization may refine the differential diagnosis; unexpectedly high uptake should prompt reconsideration of the diagnosis or additional evaluation. https://thejns.org/doi/10.3171/CASE26698.

Researchers retrospectively reviewed imaging data from eight patients (mean age 30.8 years) with confirmed intraneural perineuriomas who had undergone both MRI and FDG PET scans of the affected nerve. All eight lesions demonstrated mildly increased FDG uptake relative to the contralateral nerve, with a mean maximum standardized uptake value of 1.5 compared to 0.9 in the unaffected nerve, and six patients showed denervation edema or fatty atrophy without appreciable increased uptake in affected muscles. These findings indicate that intraneural perineuriomas generally exhibit low-level FDG uptake, suggesting that PET imaging is best used as a complementary test when already available or when metabolic characterization may help refine the differential diagnosis. Unexpectedly high FDG uptake in a suspected intraneural perineurioma should prompt reconsideration of the diagnosis or additional evaluation.

All lesions demonstrated mildly increased FDG uptake relative to the contralateral nerve, with lesion maximum standardized uptake values (SUVmax) ranging from 1.1 to 3.5 (mean 1.5, median 1.2) compared to contralateral nerve SUVmax of 0.8 to 1.0 (mean 0.9, median 0.9). Six patients exhibited denervation edema and/or fatty atrophy without appreciably increased FDG uptake in affected musculature, and no additional abnormal hypermetabolic foci were identified. Intraneural perineuriomas generally demonstrate low-level FDG uptake, making PET best regarded as a complementary test when metabolic characterization may refine differential diagnosis. Unexpect.

title: From 5 to 15: The Impact of Increased Program Signals in the 2024 to 2025 General Surgery Application Cycle.

Candidates were more likely to get an interview invitation and be placed on a program's ROL at a program they signaled when compared to a program they did not signal. llm_summary: The 2024 to 2025 General Surgery residency application cycle introduced an increase in program signals from 5 to 15, prompting researchers to evaluate how this change affected the matching process between applicants and programs. Using data from the AAMC ERAS application system, Thalamus interview platform, and NRMP ranking and matching records, the study analyzed whether signaling a program—a mechanism allowing applicants to indicate interest—influenced interview invitations, placement on rank order lists, and final match outcomes. Applicants who signaled interest at a program were significantly more likely to receive an interview invitation and be placed on that program's rank order list compared to programs they did not signal, and signaling was associated with improved median match rates for candidates. The findings suggest that both applicants and programs are using the expanded signaling system as intended to facilitate better matching, and the increase in available signals appeared to reduce the average number of applications per applicant without harming interview or match outcomes. The authors note that continued research is necessary to fully understand the long-term impacts of program signaling on residency selection and to identify any potential unintended negative consequences of this policy change.

title: Potently neutralizing and protective human monoclonal antibodies against the measles fusion protein trimer.
abstract: Measles remains a significant source of morbidity and mortality globally. There are currently no licensed treatments for patients at high risk of severe disease. There is limited knowledge about the human antibody response to a measles infection or vaccination or the structural determinants of antibody-mediated neutralization on the measles virus surface hemagglutinin (H) and fusion (F) glycoproteins. Here, we describe a panel of human monoclonal antibodies isolated from individuals who had been naturally infected with the measles virus. Several antibodies that recognized a prefusion-stabilized F protein potently neutralized the virus in vitro. We determined the structural basis of molecular recognition and virus neutralization using cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) for two antibodies that recognize distinct sites of the F protein, MeV-15 and MeV-104. These antibodies also strongly inhibited viral replication in vivo when administered prophylactically in a murine transgenic model and when administered therapeutically in a cotton rat model of established infection.Copyright © 2026 The Author(s). llm_summary: Measles continues to cause significant illness and death worldwide, yet no approved treatments exist for patients at high risk of severe disease. Researchers isolated human monoclonal antibodies from individuals naturally infected with measles virus and identified several antibodies that bound to the prefusion form of the viral fusion protein and potently neutralized the virus in laboratory tests. Using cryo-electron microscopy, the team determined the three-dimensional structures showing how two antibodies, MeV-15 and MeV-104, recognized different sites on the fusion protein and achieved virus neutralization. When given before infection in mice or after infection was established in cotton rats, both antibodies strongly reduced viral replication in living animals. These results suggest that monoclonal antibodies targeting the measles fusion protein may represent a potential therapeutic approach for high-risk patients, though further development and clinical testing would be needed to establish safety and efficacy in humans.

title: Monoallelic variants in BRSK1 are associated with a neurodevelopmental disorder with or without epilepsy.
abstract: Brain-specific serine/threonine kinase (BRSK1; synapses of amphids defective [SAD]-B) encodes an AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK)-related serine/threonine kinase required for neuronal polarization and synaptic function. An individual with a variant in BRSK1 was identified in the Texome Project, which provides genomic diagnosis to financially disadvantaged individuals in Texas, using AI-MARRVEL. We subsequently found nine individuals harboring rare heterozygous BRSK1 variants through GeneMatcher. Affected individuals present with developmental delay and variable phenotypes including anxiety, attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), autism, and seizures. All variants (missense and nonsense) are predicted to be deleterious by pathogenicity prediction tools. We utilized Drosophila to model three missense variants to assess the impact of the variants in vivo. We show that Drosophila sff (sugar-free frosting; ortholog of BRSK1) is expressed in neurons of the larval central nervous system (CNS) and adult brain. Loss of sff leads to viable flies with severe locomotor impairment, bang and heat sensitivity, and a short lifespan. In addition, the third-instar neuromuscular junctions (NMJs) in sff null mutants display a significant overgrowth, associated with elevated levels of Futsch (MAP1B), a microtubule-associated protein. Expression of the human reference BRSK1 cDNA in the sff null mutant rescues the behavioral, NMJ morphology, and Futsch phenotypes, showing that the human gene is functional in flies. In contrast, the three individual-derived alleles (BRSK1p.Ile202Val, BRSK1p.Arg237Cys, and BRSK1p.Thr406Ile) provide only a partial rescue and fail to normalize NMJ morphology and Futsch levels, suggesting that they are partial loss-of-function alleles. llm_summary: Researchers identified ten individuals with rare variants in BRSK1, a gene encoding a protein essential for neuronal development and function, who presented with developmental delay and variable symptoms including anxiety, ADHD, autism, and seizures. Using fruit flies as a model organism, the team demonstrated that the BRSK1 ortholog is expressed in the nervous system and that loss of this gene causes severe locomotor impairment, abnormal heat sensitivity, and structural overgrowth at neuromuscular junctions. The three patient-derived variants tested in flies provided only partial restoration of normal function compared to the wild-type human gene, indicating they represent partial loss-of-function mutations rather than complete loss. These findings support a model in which heterozygous loss of BRSK1 function leads to a neurodevelopmental syndrome with variable clinical manifestations across affected individuals. The study establishes BRSK1 as a disease-associated gene but would benefit from functional studies of additional variants and larger patient cohorts to fully characterize the phenotypic spectrum.

title: Clinical Realities of Multimodal Imaging in Papillary Fibroelastoma in 385 Pathology-Proven Cases.
abstract: To evaluate the diagnostic utility of computed tomography (CT) and cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging compared to transesophageal echo (TEE) in detecting cardiac papillary fibroelastomas (PFE), using the largest dataset of pathologically-confirmed cases to date, and characterize imaging findings across modalities.We retrospectively reviewed 385 patients with pathologically proven PFEs identified during cardiac surgery from January 1, 1998, through December 31, 2024. We assessed TEE, CT and CMR for lesion detection and imaging characteristics. The study was approved by the Mayo Clinic Institutional Review Board (IRB 23-009539).Of 384 patients who underwent TEE, PFEs were detected in 310 (80.7%; 95% CI, 76.5%-84.4%). CMR detected PFEs in 11 of 48 patients (22.9%; 95% CI, 13.0%-36.1%), whereas CT detected PFEs in 39 of 91 patients (42.9%; 95% CI, 33%-53%), predominantly left-sided, especially on the aortic valve. Detection was higher when CT or CMR was performed specifically for cardiac mass evaluation (80.0% and 88.9%, respectively) than for other indications. All CT and CMR-detected PFEs were also seen on TEE. TEE demonstrated the ability to detect very small lesions, including PFEs measuring less than 1 mm.TEE remains the primary imaging modality for suspected PFEs. CT and CMR provide complementary information when TEE is contraindicated or inconclusive, but detection varies with study indication, protocol, lesion characteristics, and prior knowledge of lesion location. A targeted multimodality approach may improve diagnostic confidence in selected cases.Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Inc.

title: mRNA-Engineered Stem Cells Produce Nerve Growth Factor and Induce Neurite Outgrowth in Recipient Cells.
abstract: Innervation is essential for tissue healing, yet strategies to enhance nerve growth during repair remain limited. Here, we show that chemically modified messenger RNA (cmRNA) encoding nerve growth factor (NGF) can stimulate neurogenic responses in vitro. NGF cmRNA was delivered to human bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells using lipid carriers, leading to efficient NGF production. In co-culture, NGF-secreting stem cells induced differentiation of neural crest-derived PC-12 cells, as evidenced by increased neurite outgrowth and branching. Proteomic analyses revealed activation of neurogenesis-related pathways in both cell types. Notably, NGF cmRNA-transfected stem cells produced lower NGF levels than recombinant protein yet achieved comparable neurite-outgrowth response, demonstrating the efficiency of the transcript-based approach. These findings demonstrate that NGF cmRNA can induce NGF production by hMSCs and promote neurite outgrowth in NGF-responsive PC12 cells in vitro. This approach may provide the neurotrophic component of future regenerative strategies combining NGF cmRNA with osteogenic signals; however, its effects on functional tissue innervation and bone healing remain to be established in vivo.Copyright © 2026. title: Trends in Abortion Utilization in West Virginia During a Period of Increased Abortion Restrictions, 2013-2020.
abstract: To analyze changes in method, gestational duration, and out-of-state travel for abortion care in West Virginia and for West Virginians during a timeframe with increasingly restrictive abortion legislation and decreasing abortion availability.We used publicly available data from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and data obtained from the Guttmacher Institute to calculate abortion rates by state of occurrence and state of residence and describe trends in abortion by gestational duration and method from 2013 to 2020. We constructed a timeline of abortion restrictions and clinic closures in West Virginia using news reports and legislation from Nexis Uni and the WV Legislature website.From 2013 to 2020, West Virginia enacted six abortion restrictions and one of two clinics in the state closed. During this time, the abortion rates both in West Virginia and for West Virginians experienced greater decreases compared to abortion rates in the South and United States (US). Patients in West Virginia had a lower percentage of abortions before 7 weeks (22%) compared to 41% in the region and 38% nationally. Patients in West Virginia had proportionally more aspiration abortions (79% compared to 70% in the South and US) until 2019, when state trends began to resemble regional and national trends. By 2020, a majority (52%) of all abortions for West Virginia residents occurred out of state, compared to 14% in the South and 9% in the US.Abortion restrictions and a clinic closure coincided with decreased abortions at earlier gestational durations, increased use of medication abortion, and more out-of-state travel to a wider variety of states.© 2026 University of Ottawa.

title: Prolonged survival after systemic immune reactivation by aglatimagene besadenovec plus valacyclovir in immune checkpoint inhibitor-refractory non-small cell lung cancer.
abstract: Patients with advanced non-small cell lung cancer who progress on immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) face limited options and poor survival. Aglatimagene besadenovec (CAN-2409), a replication-defective adenoviral vector encoding herpes simplex virus-thymidine kinase, plus valacyclovir, has been shown to induce immunogenic cell death and systemic immune activation.In this open-label, phase 2a clinical trial, 76 patients were enrolled (intention-to-treat population) and 73 received at least one dose of aglatimagene besadenovec (safety population); 46 patients who received two intratumoral aglatimagene besadenovec injections, completed protocol-defined valacyclovir exposure, and underwent a 12-week imaging comprised the evaluable (per-protocol) population. Endpoints included clinical and immunological outcomes.In the 73 patients included in the safety analysis (including patients who did not receive a second injection due to apparent pseudoprogression), median OS was 14.3 months. In the evaluable (per-protocol) population of 46 patients who completed protocol-defined treatment and week-12 imaging, median OS was 24.5 months (95% CI 16.0 to 33.8). Among the 41 evaluable patients in cohort 2, 15 (37%) were alive at ≥24 months and 5 (12%) at ≥40 months. In the 46-patient evaluable population, the objective response rate was 10.9% (5/46; 95% CI 4.7% to 23.0%) and the disease control rate was 71.7% (33/46; 95% CI 57.5% to 82.7%). In the 73 patients included in the safety analysis (including patients who did not receive a second injection due to apparent pseudoprogression) median overall survival was 14.3 months. Exploratory biomarkers demonstrated systemic immune reactivation, including cytotoxic T-cell expansion and regression of uninjected lesions, with stronger signals in non-squamous histology. No grade 4 treatment-related adverse events or treatment-related deaths were reported. Most treatment-related adverse events were grade 1-2; 10/73 patients (13.7%) experienced grade 3 treatment-related adverse events. Six patients discontinued because of adverse events, including two with events considered possibly related to treatment (including ongoing ICI).In this single-arm phase 2a study, aglatimagene besadenovec plus valacyclovir with ongoing ICI was associated with systemic immune remodeling and encouraging survival. llm_summary: Patients with advanced lung cancer that no longer responds to immune checkpoint inhibitor drugs face poor survival outcomes and limited treatment options. In this phase 2a trial, 73 patients received aglatimagene besadenovec, a modified virus carrying a gene that triggers cell death when combined with the antiviral drug valacyclovir, alongside continued immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy. Among the 46 patients who completed the full treatment protocol and imaging assessments, median overall survival was 24.5 months, with 37% alive at 24 months or longer, and the treatment induced systemic immune reactivation including expansion of cancer-fighting T cells. The treatment was generally well tolerated, with no grade 4 treatment-related adverse events or treatment-related deaths, though 13.7% of patients experienced grade 3 side effects. Because this was a single-arm study without a comparison group, the researchers note that efficacy requires confirmation through a randomized controlled trial, which is currently underway.
llm_summary_expert: In this open-label phase 2a trial, 73 patients with immune checkpoint inhibitor-refractory non-small cell lung cancer received intratumoral aglatimagene besadenovec (an adenoviral vector encoding herpes simplex virus-thymidine kinase) plus valacyclovir, with primary endpoints including overall survival and immunological outcomes. Among 46 evaluable patients who completed protocol-defined treatment and 12-week imaging, median overall survival was 24.5 months (95% CI 16.0 to 33.8), with objective response rate of 10.9% (5/46) and disease control rate of 71.7% (33/46). Exploratory biomarkers demonstrated systemic immune reactivation including cytotoxic T-cell expansion and regression of uninjected lesions, with stronger signals in non-squamous histology. Treatment-related adverse events were predominantly grade 1-2, with no grade 4 events or treatment-related deaths reported. Because this single-arm study lacks a randomized control group, efficacy requires confirmation in an ongoing randomized controlled trial.

title: Headache Outcomes After Flow Diversion or Coiling of Unruptured Intracranial Aneurysms: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
abstract: Headache often prompts the imaging that reveals an unruptured intracranial aneurysm (UIA), but how endovascular treatment affects headache burden remains poorly defined. We pooled the incidence of de-novo and post-procedural headache and the rates of improvement and worsening, with treatment modality analyzed as an exploratory, across-study subgroup.PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched for studies reporting post-treatment headache outcomes after flow diversion or coiling of UIAs; studies that could not separate the endovascular arm from clipping, or unruptured from ruptured aneurysms, were excluded. Proportions were pooled with random-effects generalized linear mixed models on the logit scale, with 95% confidence intervals (CIs), 95% prediction intervals (PIs), I2, and modality subgroup tests. Post hoc subgroup, meta-regression, and sensitivity analyses examined ascertainment window, ascertainment method, design, and influential cohorts.Nineteen studies (2142 patients; eight flow-diverter and 14 coiling cohorts) were included. Among baseline headache-free patients, de-novo headache occurred in 30.2% (95% CI 19.4-43.6; I2=80%; k=9). New or post-procedural headache across the entire treated cohort was 14.4% (95% CI, 8.0-24.6; k=14). Among patients with pre-existing headache, 71.4% improved (95% CI, 58.8-81.4; k=11), and 5.6% worsened (95% CI, 2.2-13.9; k=6). No statistically significant between-subgroup differences were detected (de-novo p=0.42; post-procedural p=0.43; improvement p=0.29); however, this comparison was limited by few flow-diverter cohorts and predominantly indirect comparisons. De-novo headache was more frequent when ascertained within six weeks than when persistence beyond three months was required (36.7% versus 22.6%; meta-regression on follow-up duration p=0.025).About one in three previously headache-free patients develops a new headache after endovascular treatment of a UIA, whereas roughly seven in ten with pre-existing headache improve, and worsening is uncommon. llm_summary: Researchers examined headache outcomes following endovascular treatment of unruptured brain aneurysms because headaches often lead to the imaging that discovers these aneurysms, yet the effects of treatment on headache burden remain unclear. A systematic review and meta-analysis of 19 studies involving 2,142 patients compared headache outcomes after flow diversion or coiling procedures, pooling data on new headaches, symptom improvement, and worsening across treatment groups. Among patients without baseline headaches, approximately 30.2% developed new headaches after treatment (95% CI 19.4-43.6), while among those with pre-existing headaches, roughly 71.4% experienced improvement (95% CI 58.8-81.4) and only 5.6% worsened (95% CI 2.2-13.9). The analysis found no statistically significant differences between flow diversion and coiling approaches, though this comparison was limited by fewer flow-diverter studies and predominantly indirect comparisons. The researchers noted that estimates of new headache incidence varied substantially depending on when headaches were assessed, with higher rates detected within six weeks.

Among baseline headache-free patients, de novo headache occurred in 30.2% (95% CI 19.4–43.6%), while new or post-procedural headache across the entire treated cohort was 14.4% (95% CI 8.0–24.6%). Among patients with pre-existing headache, 71.4% improved (95% CI 58.8–81.4%) and 5.6% worsened (95% CI 2.2–13.9%). De novo headache was more frequent when ascertained within six weeks than when persistence beyond three months was required (36.7% versus 22.6%; p=0.025). No statistically significant differences were detected between flow diverters and coils, though this comparison was limited by few flow-diverter cohorts and predominantly indirect comparisons.

title: Real-World Outcomes of Dedicated Leaflet Modification for Bioprosthetic Valve-In-Valve TAVR: A 150-Patient Commercial Experience.
abstract: Coronary obstruction during valve-in-valve (ViV) transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is infrequent but catastrophic. Mechanical splitting of bioprosthetic leaflets may mitigate this risk, but real-world experience remains limited.This study sought to evaluate procedural performance and in-hospital outcomes of a dedicated mechanical leaflet-splitting device in ViV TAVR.Consecutive postapproval cases were performed at 28 centers from February to November 2025. Patients were selected for elevated risk based on preprocedural computed tomography criteria, including virtual valve-to-coronary distance ≤4 mm and/or virtual valve-to-sinotubular junction distance ≤3 mm. Procedural outcomes were assessed among patients in whom splitting was attempted; safety outcomes were assessed among all patients in whom the device was introduced. Events were adjudicated using Valve Academic Research Consortium-3 definitions.Among 150 patients (age 78.9 ± 8.5 years; 60.0% female), 95 of 150 (63.3%) underwent ViV TAVR for failed surgical and 55 of 150 (36.7%) for failed transcatheter valves. Computed tomography analysis showed predicted acute coronary obstruction risk in 131 of 150 (87.3%) patients, including combined sinus sequestration and direct ostial obstruction in 76 of 150 (50.7%). Leaflet splitting was attempted in 145 patients and was successful in 144 of 145 (99.3%); dual-leaflet splitting was performed in 83 of 145 (57.2%). Coronary obstruction occurred in 3 of 150 (2.0%; 95% CI: 0.7-5.7). All-cause mortality occurred in 3 of 150 (2.0%; 95% CI: 0.7-5.7), including 2 deaths from left ventricular perforation and 1 after stroke. Conversion to surgery occurred in 2 of 150 (1.3%; 95% CI: 0.4-4.7).In this early U.S. commercial experience, mechanical leaflet splitting demonstrated high procedural success in an anatomically high-risk ViV TAVR cohort. Serious complications occurred, and longer-term systematic follow-up remains important.Copyright © 2026 The Authors. Published by Elsevier Inc. All rights reserved.

title: Scuba-related injuries presenting to United States emergency departments: paediatric and adult patterns.
abstract: Scuba diving is a popular sport that carries risks unique to the underwater environment. Paediatric emergency department presentations for scuba diving injuries are incompletely characterised, particularly in comparison with adults.We retrospectively analysed scuba-related injuries recorded in the National Electronic Injury Surveillance System (NEISS) from 2005-2024. We estimated national paediatric emergency department presentations using NEISS weights and compared injury categories and hospitalisation rates between paediatric and adult patients.We identified 68 paediatric cases, corresponding to an estimated 122 paediatric scuba-related emergency department presentations annually. Trauma was the most common injury category (41.2%), followed by otitis (17.6%) and ear, sinus, ocular, or dental barotrauma (16.2%). Hospitalisation was most common among patients with possible decompression sickness or arterial gas embolism (DCS/AGE) (42.9%) and drowning/aspiration (25.0%). Compared with adults, paediatric patients were less often hospitalised (10.3% vs 21.4%, P = 0.038), more likely to present with traumatic injuries (41.2% vs 26.1%, P = 0.010), and less likely to present with possible DCS/AGE (10.3% vs 25.0%, P = 0.006).Among patients presenting to United States emergency departments with scuba-related injuries, paediatric patients most commonly had trauma, otitis, or ear, sinus, ocular, or dental barotrauma. Paediatric divers were also less likely than adults to experience DCS/AGE injuries and were less likely than adults to require hospitalisation. Our data describes emergency department presentation patterns rather than overall injury risk among paediatric scuba divers.Copyright: This article is the copyright of the authors who grant Diving and Hyperbaric Medicine a non-exclusive licence to publish the article in electronic and other forms.

llm_summary: Researchers examined scuba diving injuries in children and adults presenting to United States emergency departments using the National Electronic Injury Surveillance System database from 2005-2024 to characterize injury patterns that had been incompletely described in pediatric populations. The study identified 68 pediatric cases representing an estimated 122 annual pediatric scuba-related emergency department presentations, with trauma being the most common injury type (41.2%), followed by ear infections and pressure-related injuries to the ear, sinuses, eyes, or teeth (17.6% and 16.2% respectively). Compared with adults, pediatric patients were less frequently hospitalized (10.3% versus 21.4%, P = 0.038), more likely to present with traumatic injuries (41.2% versus 26.1%, P = 0.010), and less likely to present with decompression sickness or arterial gas embolism (10.3% versus 25.0%, P = 0.006). These differences in injury patterns and hospitalization rates between pediatric and adult divers suggest that children may experience different types of scuba-related complications or have different exposure.

title: Decoding the complexity of tricuspid regurgitation prognostic drivers using explainable artificial intelligence.
abstract: Prognosis in tricuspid regurgitation (TR) is shaped by complex clinical and haemodynamic interactions, complicating risk stratification. We aimed to use explainable artificial intelligence (EAI) to model these relationships and identify key predictors of outcomes.We analysed long-term all-cause mortality in a large prospective registry of patients with native TR across the full severity spectrum. Patients underwent detailed clinical evaluation and quantitative Doppler-echocardiography. Supervised EAI models were applied to identify and rank predictors of mortality under medical therapy, capturing non-linear associations and interactions among baseline characteristics.Among 9761 patients [mean age 73 ± 15 years; 56.9% women; effective regurgitant orifice area (EROA) 40 (30-56) mm2; regurgitant volume 39 (29-53) mL/beat; 42% severe TR], 2676 deaths occurred during 3.8 ± 4.6 years of follow-up. EAI identified and ranked 20 prognostic determinants of survival. Haemodynamic measures, led by elevated pulmonary-artery systolic and right-atrial pressures, were strongest, followed by age and comorbidity. TR-related variables ranked next, led by right ventricular dysfunction and EROA, which outperformed integrative TR grade and TRIScore. Left-ventricular parameters were less influential. Non-linear effects, including those involving ejection fraction, and interactions such as higher EROA-related risk with elevated pulmonary pressures or lower TRIScore (both P < 0.03) were observed. Proportional hazards models confirmed EROA as the strongest TR severity marker (P < 0.0001), with excess mortality beginning at 40 mm2 and increasing further at 60 mm2.EAI ranked mortality predictors in TR, highlighting patient factors, haemodynamics, TR-specific measures, and left-ventricular function. Among TR-specific measures, EROA and TRIScore were most prognostic. llm_summary: Researchers examined mortality predictors in tricuspid regurgitation (TR), a heart valve condition where blood leaks backward, using explainable artificial intelligence to model complex relationships among clinical and heart function measurements. Among 9,761 patients followed for an average of 3.8 years, 2,676 deaths occurred, and the analysis identified elevated pulmonary artery and right atrial pressures as the strongest predictors of mortality, followed by patient age and comorbidities. TR-specific measurements, particularly effective regurgitant orifice area (EROA) and a scoring system called TRIScore, ranked as important predictors, with EROA showing excess mortality beginning at 40 mm² and increasing further at 60 mm². The analysis revealed non-linear effects and interactions, such as higher risk from larger EROA when pulmonary pressures were elevated or TRIScore was lower (P < 0.03), suggesting that TR severity measures interact with hemodynamic factors in determining outcomes. These findings may help clinicians better stratify risk and time interventions in TR patients, though further research is needed to validate whether targeting these specific measurements.

title: Spine MRI in Spontaneous Intracranial Hypotension: A Survey of Current State of Practice.
abstract: Spine MRI plays a central role in the diagnostic evaluation of spontaneous intracranial hypotension (SIH) by helping identify extradural fluid and guide subsequent myelographic technique. Despite its widespread use, the technical details of spine MRI protocols for SIH are often incompletely reported, and the extent of practice variation across specialized centers remains poorly characterized. In addition, ambiguous and inconsistent terminology, including variable use of terms such as "MR myelography" and "heavily T2-weighted MRI," may obscure important differences between non-contrast MRI techniques and examinations performed after intrathecal contrast administration.This State of Practice was developed by neuroradiologists from 9 United States centers with expertise in SIH. Participating centers reviewed and reported their institutional whole-spine MRI protocols for SIH evaluation, including use of 2D and 3D T2-weighted imaging, fat suppression, and echo time.Current spine MRI protocols for SIH show substantial heterogeneity, particularly in fat-suppression technique and echo time, despite universal use of 3D T2-weighted imaging among surveyed centers. Ambiguous terminology further limits comparison across studies and may contribute to confusion regarding whether "MR myelography" refers to non-contrast heavily T2-weighted MRI or intrathecal contrast-enhanced MR myelography. Standardized terminology and more complete reporting of technical parameters are needed to improve interpretation of the literature and guide future protocol refinement.© 2027 by American Journal of Neuroradiology.

llm_summary: Spine MRI is essential for diagnosing spontaneous intracranial hypotension, a condition involving low cerebrospinal fluid pressure, by identifying fluid collections and guiding further imaging procedures. Neuroradiologists from nine specialized U. title: Ultrasound reference equations for diaphragm thickness and thickening fraction in healthy adults: protocol for an individual participant data meta-analysis.
abstract: Sonographic assessment of diaphragm thickness at end-expiration (DTe) and diaphragm thickening fraction (DTF) is increasingly recognised as a readily available bedside method for evaluating diaphragm structure and function. However, currently available reference values for DTe and DTF vary substantially across populations and between sexes, limiting their clinical interpretability. We hypothesise that an individual participant data meta-analysis (IPD-MA) incorporating readily available anthropometric variables can be used to derive robust population-adjusted ultrasound reference values for DTe and DTF.We will conduct a systematic review and IPD-MA of studies that measured right-sided diaphragm thickness in adult subjects using ultrasound. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL, Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection and LILACS/BVS will be searched from inception without language or publication-status restrictions. Anonymised individual participant data will be requested from study authors and harmonised according to a prespecified statistical analysis plan. The primary study aim is to develop prediction equations for DTF and DTe in quietly breathing healthy subjects using linear mixed-effects regression models and derive corresponding 95% reference limits. Model performance and generalisability will be evaluated using internal-external cross-validation. The study is currently at the planning stage-no definitive searches or other formal steps have been performed.Ethical approval is not required for this study as it is based on secondary analysis of anonymised data from previously conducted studies. title: Clinical Implications of the Type and Genomic Location of Pathogenic BRCA1 and BRCA2 Variants in Hereditary Breast and Ovarian Cancer.
abstract: Germline pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants (P/LPVs) in BRCA1 and BRCA2 are major determinants of hereditary breast and ovarian cancer susceptibility. Although clinical management has traditionally relied on the presence of a BRCA1/BRCA2 alteration regardless of its specific characteristics, growing evidence suggests that not all BRCA P/LPVs are biologically and clinically equivalent. Variant location within BRCA1 and BRCA2 influences the relative distribution of breast and ovarian cancer risk. Breast cancer cluster regions (BCCRs) are associated with a higher relative risk of breast versus ovarian cancer, whereas ovarian cancer cluster regions (OCCRs), largely encompassing exon 11, are associated with a relative shift toward ovarian cancer risk. Variant type may also be clinically relevant. Protein-truncating P/LPVs have been associated with higher cancer risks than selected missense variants with residual protein function and lower penetrance. Some studies have also reported poorer outcomes for carriers of protein-truncating P/LPVs and more favorable outcomes for those with missense variants. In this narrative review, we summarize current evidence on the clinical implications of BRCA1/BRCA2 P/LPV type and genomic location. While associations between variant location and breast or ovarian cancer risk are supported by large international consortia, prognostic and predictive associations remain largely exploratory. A better understanding of variant-specific genotype-phenotype correlations may ultimately refine risk prediction, preventive strategies, and treatment selection in hereditary breast and ovarian cancer.Copyright © 2026 The Author(s). title: Microbiome signatures linked to cancer and treatment adverse events in a real-world cohort.
abstract: The gut microbiome has emerged as a key contributor to cancer biology. Prior studies have focused on individual cancers and often overlook comorbidities, obscuring whether reported associations are specific to a cancer type. Here, we present findings from a real-world mixed-cancer cohort (Mayo Clinic Cancer Microbiome), comprising 1,364 cancer patients and 287 healthy controls. By applying a framework to account for non-specific microbiome associations with cancer, comorbidities, and demographic and clinical variables, we identified 341 cancer-associated species across five cancer classes that represent the most plausible contributors to cancer pathogenesis. Within cancer classes, we found lower levels of fecal bile acids and C. scindens in early-onset breast cancer and elevated lactate and Veillonella parvula in early-onset colorectal cancer. Additionally, Anaerostipes hadrus encoding dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase was protective against 5-fluorouracil-induced diarrhea. These findings demonstrate the strength of our cohort and provide a foundational resource for the discovery of cancer-specific microbiome signatures and predictive biomarkers.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Inc. title: Lessons Learned: Teaching Smarter, Not Harder Through Artificial Intelligence in Instruction.
abstract: Discussions surrounding the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in higher education remain highly prevalent, with most attention focused on how students using AI both within and external to the classroom. title: Accelerated Biological Aging in Cholestatic Liver Disease: Telomere Attrition and Association With Disease Severity.
abstract: Primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) and primary biliary cholangitis (PBC) are rare, chronic cholestatic liver diseases with heterogeneous progression and limited biomarkers of disease biology. Epigenetic age acceleration has been demonstrated in PSC and PBC, suggesting accelerated biological aging. DNA methylation-derived telomere length (DNAmTL) reflects replicative aging and cellular turnover, but its role in PSC and PBC remains unclear. We aimed to evaluate DNAmTL in PSC and PBC and its association with disease severity.We analysed and compared DNAmTL and age-adjusted DNAmTL among patients with PSC (n = 474) versus PSC controls (n = 484) and patients with PBC (n = 291) versus PBC controls (n = 291). Associations with clinical outcomes were assessed using nonparametric tests and multivariable logistic regression models. Correlations with primary sclerosing cholangitis Risk Estimate Tool (PREsTO) score and epigenetic age acceleration (AgeAccelGrim) were evaluated using linear regression.Patients with PSC demonstrated significantly shorter age-adjusted DNAmTL compared with controls (median -0.036 vs. 0.016, p < 0.001). Patients with PBC also exhibited reduced DNAmTL relative to controls (median 6.814 vs. 6.885, p < 0.001). Within PSC, shorter DNAmTL was associated with cirrhosis (OR 0.21, 95% CI 0.06-0.69, p = 0.013) and advanced disease (OR 0.20, 95% CI 0.06-0.67, p = 0.009). Shorter DNAmTL was also observed in hepatic decompensation and hepatobiliary malignancy, including cholangiocarcinoma. DNAmTL inversely correlated with PReSTO score (p < 0.001). DNAmTL was strongly inversely correlated with AgeAccelGrim in both PSC and PBC (p < 0.001).Cholestatic liver diseases are associated with shortened DNAmTL, which independently correlates with disease severity in PSC.
