title: Beyond biological risk: socioeconomic vulnerability and adverse pediatric kidney transplant outcomes.
abstract: Adverse social determinants are known contributors to poorer long-term allograft outcomes. Yet optimal measures of social determinants are lacking. We sought to evaluate the association between socioeconomic status (SES) and graft loss in children using several different metrics of social determinants of health (SDOH).Our study included 137 pediatric kidney transplant recipients (< 18 years at kidney failure onset) transplanted between 2010 and 2020. The association between SES measures (individual- and area-level) and graft survival was examined using Cox regression models. Measures were dichotomized: HOUSES Index [low SES(Q1) vs. high (Q2-Q4)], Area Deprivation Index (ADI) [high deprivation (76-100 percentile) vs. low (1-75 percentile)], and Childhood Opportunity Index (COI) [low opportunity (1s-25 percentile) vs. high (26-100)]. All models were adjusted for transplant age, sex, donor type, pretransplant dialysis, insurance, kidney failure cause, and body mass index z-score.After adjusting for covariates, we observed a significantly increased risk of graft loss in HOUSES Q1 vs. Q2-4 recipients (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR]: 3.25; 95% CI: 1.38, 7.64; p = 0.007) and nationally standardized low-opportunity COI vs. high-opportunity COI recipients (aHR: 5.01; 95% CI: 2.01, 12.5; p = 0.001). In contrast, we observed no significant association between ADI and graft loss.Using the HOUSES Index and COI, we identified a 3-fold to fivefold higher risk of pediatric graft loss among recipients with lower SDOH. These tools provide robust non-biological predictors for transplant outcomes; however, larger studies are required to compare their relative impact.© 2026. The Author(s).

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether socioeconomic factors predict kidney transplant failure in children, since social determinants of health are known to influence long-term transplant outcomes but optimal measurement tools remain unclear. The study followed 137 pediatric kidney transplant recipients from 2010 to 2020 and evaluated associations between three different socioeconomic measures—the HOUSES Index, Area Deprivation Index, and Childhood Opportunity Index—and graft loss using statistical models adjusted for biological and clinical factors. Children in the lowest socioeconomic category by HOUSES Index showed a 3.25-fold increased risk of graft loss compared to higher categories, and those with low childhood opportunity showed a 5.01-fold increased risk, while the Area Deprivation Index showed no significant association with graft loss. These findings suggest that certain socioeconomic measures, particularly the HOUSES Index and Childhood Opportunity Index, identify children at substantially higher risk for transplant failure independent of biological factors. Larger studies are needed to determine which socioeconomic measures most reliably predict transplant outcomes and to understand the mechanisms linking social disadvantage to graft loss.

title: A Call for Investment in Sponsorship, Apprenticeship, and Mentorship: Ensuring the Future of Congenital Heart Surgery.
abstract: Becoming a successful congenital cardiac surgeon requires the investment of senior surgeons in sponsorship, apprenticeship, and mentorship. The recent survey of The Society of Thoracic Surgeons Workforce on Congenital Surgery revealed distinct concerns from early-career surgeons related to these functions. This Invited Perspective reviews the concerning findings of the survey regarding the future of the specialty, describes key barriers to senior surgeon investment, and provides potential solutions to the concerns.Copyright © 2026 The Society of Thoracic Surgeons. llm_summary: Developing competent congenital cardiac surgeons depends critically on senior surgeons providing sponsorship, apprenticeship, and mentorship to the next generation of practitioners. The Society of Thoracic Surgeons Workforce on Congenital Surgery conducted a survey that identified significant concerns among early-career surgeons regarding the availability and quality of these developmental functions. The survey revealed distinct barriers that prevent senior surgeons from adequately investing time and resources in training and supporting junior colleagues in the field. The authors of this perspective piece review these concerning findings and discuss how they threaten the future sustainability of congenital heart surgery as a specialty. The paper proposes potential solutions to address the identified gaps and encourage greater senior surgeon engagement in sponsoring and mentoring the next generation of congenital cardiac surgeons.

title: Contractility patterns on functional lumen imaging probe prior to peroral endoscopic myotomy predict outcomes in achalasia.
abstract: Functional lumen imaging probe (FLIP) assessment of esophagogastric junction (EGJ) opening confirms suspected achalasia. However, the importance of the contractile response (CR) in the esophageal body to volumetric distension in established achalasia is unclear. This study evaluated the value of CR on FLIP before peroral endoscopic myotomy (POEM) to predict post-POEM esophageal emptying on timed barium esophagram (TBE).Patients with types 1 and 2 achalasia who underwent FLIP at a tertiary center from March 2020 to June 2024 were identified. FLIP was interpreted using published criteria, with reduced EGJ opening (REO) defined by distensibility index (DI) <2 mm2/mm Hg and maximum diameter <12 mm at 60 and 70 mL balloon volume, respectively, and CR categorized as normal, spastic, disordered/diminished, or absent. Outcome measures included significant barium retention on TBE, defined by column height greater than 5 cm at 5 minutes or 13-mm barium tablet retention.Among 141 patients (48.2% female; median age, 60.0; IQR, 44.0-73.0 years; 123 (74.1%) type II achalasia), all had reduced EGJ opening on FLIP pre-POEM, with absent CR in 111 (78.7%). Significant barium retention on TBE was observed in 29.1% post-POEM, with absent CR on pre-POEM FLIP associated with barium retention on TBE (RR, 3.0; 95% CI, 1.1-9.1; P = .033) and greater mean column height at 5 minutes (1.8 cm vs 0.4 cm; P = .042).Absent CR on FLIP prior to POEM predicts significant barium retention on TBE after POEM, supporting an additive diagnostic role for FLIP in achalasia therapeutic outcome predictions.Copyright © 2026 American Society for Gastrointestinal Endoscopy. title: Outcomes of cardiac resynchronization therapy in adults with congenital heart disease and heart failure with reduced ejection fraction.
abstract: There are limited data about the role of cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT) in adults with congenital heart disease (CHD) and heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF).The objectives of this study were (1) to assess the relationship between CRT and clinical outcomes (all-cause mortality and cardiovascular events) and (2) to assess temporal changes in clinical indices of disease severity (New York Heart Association [NYHA] functional class, peak oxygen consumption, N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide, and left ventricular ejection fraction) post-CRT.This is a retrospective study of adults with CHD, biventricular circulation, systemic left ventricle, and HFrEF who received CRT at Mayo Clinic (2003-2023). Clinical indices of disease severity were assessed pre-CRT and 1-year post-CRT. We defined a CRT responder as a patient with an absolute increase in left ventricular ejection fraction ≥10% and an improvement in NYHA functional class by ≥1 unit post-CRT. Intensity of heart failure therapy was assessed using the guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) score.Of the 327 patients with CHD and HFrEF, 105 (32%) received CRT (mean age 51 ± 15 years; 72 (68% men). CRT was associated with a 24% decrease in mortality (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 0.76; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.51-0.97) and a 21% decrease in cardiovascular events (adjusted HR 0.79; 95% CI 0.63-0.94). Of the 105 patients, 71 (68%) were CRT responders. Higher GDMT score was associated with greater odds of CRT response (adjusted odds ratio 1.28; 95% CI 1.04-1.47). CRT responders had a greater temporal improvement in NYHA functional class, peak oxygen consumption, N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide level, and a lower risk of cardiovascular events (unadjusted HR 0.73; 95% CI 0.47-0.99).These data highlight the clinical benefits of CRT and GDMT for the management of HFrEF in CHD and support the use of these therapies in this population.Copyright © 2026 Heart Rhythm Society. llm_summary: Limited evidence exists regarding the effectiveness of cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT), a device-based treatment that coordinates heart contractions, in adults with congenital heart disease who have weakened heart function. Researchers conducted a retrospective analysis of 105 adults with congenital heart disease and reduced ejection fraction who received CRT between 2003 and 2023, comparing their outcomes to a broader cohort of 327 eligible patients and measuring changes in heart function, exercise capacity, and biomarkers one year after device implantation. CRT was associated with a 24% reduction in mortality risk and a 21% reduction in cardiovascular events, with 68% of treated patients classified as responders showing improvements in functional class, oxygen consumption, and heart function markers. Patients who responded well to CRT and received intensive medical therapy showed greater clinical improvements and lower cardiovascular event rates than non-responders. These findings suggest that CRT combined with guideline-directed medical therapy may benefit adults with congenital heart disease and reduced ejection fraction, though the observational design limits conclusions about causation and generalizability to other patient populations.

title: A framework for inclusion: fostering representation in physical medicine and rehabilitation and beyond through dedicated mentorships and workshops.
abstract: The Association of American Medical Colleges has urged actions to promote inclusivity in medical education for historically underrepresented groups. Studies suggest that underrepresentation may be addressed through structured mentorship and workshops at the premedical level and generate interest in less familiar specialties including physical medicine and rehabilitation (PM&R).The authors implemented a novel half-day multi-institutional workshop in spring 2024 featuring physicians and medical students from New York City medical centers. The workshop included structured mentorship and pertinent PM&R-related topics, including disability health and adaptive sports, to which premedical students often have limited exposure. Participants were invited to complete pre- and postworkshop surveys to evaluate the workshop's impact. The authors collaborated with prehealth chapters of organizations such as the American Medical Women's Association and the Minority Association of Pre-Medical Students to distribute surveys.The preworkshop survey was completed by 147 premedical students, and 81 registered for the workshop. Ultimately, 55 attended the workshop, with 71% completing the postworkshop survey. Most participants had no previous exposure to PM&R (n = 77, 53.5%) and to adaptive sports (n = 116, 80.6%). Furthermore, although 76 (52.8%) had shadowed a physician, only 6 (4.2%) had experience shadowing a PM&R physician. The authors gathered a diverse representation of responses, including those identifying as female (n = 119, 81.0%) and underrepresented in medicine (n = 84, 57.1%). Pre-post comparative analysis showed a statistically significant rise in students' motivation to apply to medical school (P = .018), along with a statistically significant increase in the interest and understanding of PM&R and adaptive sports (P < .001).Future work will focus on developing longitudinal mentorship, improving accessibility through hybrid formats, and expanding the curriculum through interspecialty collaborations to support broader implementation and evaluation.© The Author(s) 2026. title: Does stigma reduce hazardous health behaviors contributing to steatotic liver disease?
abstract: Hazardous health behaviors increasingly contribute to end-stage liver diseases. To address surges in alcohol-associated liver disease and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, clinicians in hepatology and liver transplantation must increasingly understand factors that influence eating and alcohol behaviors and consider ways to therapeutically influence patients' health choices. Stigma is a prominent influence on patient behavior, but is overused as a sweeping explanatory factor as to why difficulties arise, behavior change does not occur, or when outcomes are suboptimal. With more awareness of behavioral influences, clinicians may wonder if, for all its adverse effects, stigma exerts some therapeutic effects on patients considering altering habits. While stigma is less likely to yield desired outcomes, other co-occurring systemic, social, and interpersonal influences can favorably affect health choices (ie, structural nudging, social norms and consequences, and motivational interviewing, respectively). In this article, we analyze these related yet distinct constructs in ways pertinent to liver disease and transplantation, indicating where they might be applied and further studied.Copyright © 2026 American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases.

llm_summary: Hazardous health behaviors such as excessive alcohol consumption and poor eating habits are increasingly driving end-stage liver disease, prompting hepatologists to better understand what influences patient behavior change. This article analyzes whether stigma—the social disapproval patients experience—might paradoxically serve as a therapeutic tool to motivate healthier choices, while also examining alternative behavioral influences like structural nudging, social norms, and motivational interviewing. The authors conclude that while stigma is unlikely to reliably produce desired health outcomes, other co-occurring systemic, social, and interpersonal factors show greater promise for favorably affecting patient decisions about eating and alcohol use. The analysis suggests that clinicians should move beyond viewing stigma as a sweeping explanation for treatment failures and instead consider applying evidence-based behavioral strategies tailored to individual patients with alcohol-associated liver disease and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease. Further research is needed to determine how these distinct behavioral constructs can be most effectively applied and studied in the context of liver disease and transplantation.
llm_summary_expert: The authors analyze the relationship between stigma and hazardous health behaviors contributing to steatotic liver disease and alcohol-associated liver disease in the context of hepatology and liver transplantation. Rather than treating stigma as a monolithic explanatory factor for poor outcomes or failed behavior change, the paper examines whether stigma might exert any therapeutic effects on patients considering lifestyle modifications. The authors distinguish stigma from related but distinct constructs including structural nudging, social norms and consequences, and motivational interviewing, each of which may favorably influence health choices. The analysis indicates potential applications and areas for further study of these constructs in liver disease and transplantation populations. This conceptual review does not present empirical quantitative results but instead provides a framework for clinicians to understand multiple behavioral influences beyond stigma alone.

title: Development of A Screening Tool to Predict Post Intensive Care Syndrome (PICS) in Critically Ill Adults in a Prospective Cohort.
abstract: PurposeSurvivors of critical illness often acquire significant physical, cognitive, and psychological burdens following their intensive care unit (ICU) stay, termed "post-intensive care syndrome" (PICS). Screening for PICS is generally not performed outside of research settings largely due to lack of a simple assessment tool and time constraints.MethodsThis was a prospective cohort study at a single academic medical center in the USA. We included adults (18 years or older) who spent greater than 48 h in any ICU within the medical center. Following transfer out of the ICU and at 3 months, psychological, cognitive, and physical functioning were assessed using the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale, Impact of Event Scale-Revised, Montreal Cognitive Assessment-blind, and Barthel Index. We compared these validated questionnaires to a brief, 15-item PICS screening tool (5 questions/domain) that was developed by our multidisciplinary study team and administered to study participants after ICU discharge to general care. The primary objectives of this study were to assess the ability of validated screening tools administered at ICU discharge to predict PICS at 3 months and develop a novel screening tool for identifying patients at risk of PICS.Major Findings191 participants completed the initial questionnaire, and 109 (56%) completed the 3-month follow-up. PICS tool scores were compared to 3-month follow-up data from validated questionnaires to evaluate predictive performance. Overall, the screening tool weakly-to-moderately correlated with continuous outcomes of the validated measures at 3-month follow-up. When evaluating sensitivity and specificity for individual domains, the screening tool had an area under curve of >0.7 for all three domains, indicating moderate-to-good sensitivity and specificity.ConclusionsWe developed a brief PICS screening tool that is feasible to use without prior training that modestly predicted the development of PICS following ICU stay.

llm_summary: Survivors of critical illness often experience lasting physical, cognitive, and psychological problems known as post-intensive care syndrome (PICS), yet screening for this condition is rarely performed in routine clinical practice due to the lack of simple assessment tools. Researchers conducted a prospective cohort study at a single academic medical center enrolling 191 adults who spent more than 48 hours in an ICU, administering a newly developed 15-item PICS screening tool at ICU discharge and comparing it to established validated questionnaires administered at both discharge and 3-month follow-up. title: Surgical Reconstruction of Irreparable Hip Abductors With the Use of Allograft: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Clinical Outcomes.
abstract: Chronic hip abductor insufficiency remains a challenging problem to treat and can result in notable disability in some patients. The use of allograft has become an increasingly common option for surgical reconstruction. The purpose of this systematic review was to analyze the clinical outcomes, complications, and revisions rates of patients who underwent allograft reconstruction for irreparable hip abductor tears.PubMed (MEDLINE), Scopus (EMBASE, MEDLINE, COMPENDEX), and Cochrane databases were used to conduct a systematic review. A total of five studies were included, comprising three that used a dermal allograft, one that used an Achilles tendon allograft with a calcaneal bone block, and one that used an extensor mechanism of the knee allograft. Demographics, hip setting (native hip, primary total hip arthroplasty [THA], revision THA), patient-reported outcome measures, presence of Trendelenburg sign, use of walking aids, abduction strength, complication rates, and revision rates were analyzed.A total of 76 patients (76 hips) underwent hip abductor reconstruction with allograft. The mean age was 63.2 years with 84.2% being female. The mean follow-up was 23.6 months. Four studies reported changes in preoperative to postoperative patient-reported outcome measures, all of which demonstrated an improvement in outcomes. The mean preoperative reported abduction strength was 2.7/5, which improved to 3.9/5 postoperatively ( P < 0.001). Two studies demonstrated a persistent postoperative Trendeleburg sign in more than one third of patients. The complication and revision rates were 5.3% (4/76) and 1.3% (1/76), respectively.Allograft reconstruction is a salvage procedure for a challenging problem that provides satisfactory clinical outcomes in patients with chronic hip abductor insufficiency not amendable to primary repair. Complication and revision rates were notably low. Future research should compare the clinical outcomes of allograft reconstruction with other muscle transfer techniques to determine the optimal surgical treatment for chronic hip abductor deficiency.Copyright © 2026 by the American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons.

title: A Tertiary Medical Center Experience with Returning Radiopharmaceutical Therapy Patients.
abstract: After implementing a process for flagging readmitted radiopharmaceutical therapy patients, it was discovered that major assumptions for these patients were not correct, specifically the magnitude of patients and the location of the readmissions. Data collected from May to December 2024 revealed 501 post-therapy patient encounters out of 1,139 administrations. Analysis showed varying return rates across different radiopharmaceuticals and departments, highlighting the need for updated radiation safety response. Results indicated that most encounters occurred in outpatient settings, with contamination above action levels found in 61% of responses. The study underscores the importance of continuous assessment and collaboration among stakeholders to adapt to new radiopharmaceutical therapies and ensure effective radiation safety practices.Copyright © 2026 Health Physics Society.

llm_summary: A tertiary medical center implemented a process to track readmitted patients who had received radiopharmaceutical therapy, a nuclear medicine treatment where radioactive drugs are administered to patients. Between May and December 2024, researchers identified 501 post-therapy patient encounters occurring after 1,139 radiopharmaceutical administrations, revealing that previous assumptions about the frequency and location of these readmissions were incorrect. Most encounters took place in outpatient settings rather than inpatient departments, and contamination levels exceeding action thresholds were detected in 61% of the responses assessed. Return rates varied depending on the specific radiopharmaceutical used and the department involved, indicating that different therapies and clinical settings present distinct radiation safety considerations. The findings highlight the need for updated radiation safety protocols and ongoing collaboration among healthcare stakeholders to address the evolving landscape of radiopharmaceutical therapies.

title: Effects of oxycodone on tonic levels and phasic release of serotonin in the rat nucleus accumbens core.
abstract: Despite widespread oxycodone misuse, the role of serotonin in opioid addiction remains understudied compared to dopamine. This study investigated the acute effects of oxycodone (2.5 mg/kg, i.v.) on serotonergic neurotransmission in the rat nucleus accumbens core using high-resolution electrochemical methods. We employed fast-scan cyclic voltammetry (FSCV) to monitor medial forebrain bundle stimulation-evoked phasic release and N-shaped multiple cyclic square wave voltammetry (N-MCSWV) to measure tonic concentrations in urethane-anesthetized rats. Results demonstrated a distinct dissociation between tonic and phasic dynamics. Tonic serotonin levels increased significantly (+23.4 nM) from baseline 1-h post-administration. Conversely, stimulation-evoked phasic release initially increased (+24%) but subsequently declined below baseline. Kinetic analysis revealed that serotonin production and maximum reuptake rates followed a similar pattern of initial increase followed by a decrease. In conclusion, oxycodone acutely modulates serotonergic signaling in the nucleus accumbens core by differentially affecting phasic and tonic neurotransmission. These findings demonstrate oxycodone induces temporal dynamics in phasic versus tonic serotonergic signaling in the nucleus accumbens core, highlighting the value of multimodal electrochemical approaches for dissecting opioid neurochemical effects.Copyright © 2026 The Authors. title: Extracellular matrix-associated molecules of senescent cells induce a senescence phenotype in proliferative cells via TGF-β signaling pathway.
abstract: Senescent cells accumulate in various tissues as we age and are characterized by growth arrest and a senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP). This phenotype involves the release of various factors, such as pro-inflammatory molecules, reactive oxygen species (ROS) and extracellular vesicles (EVs), which can trigger senescence in neighboring cells. However, it remains unclear whether non-soluble factors produced by senescent cells, such as the extracellular matrix (ECM) or its associated molecules (collectively termed the matrisome), can induce paracrine senescence. In this study, vascular cells were used as an in vitro model system to investigate this hypothesis. These findings reveal that decellularized ECM from senescent vascular smooth muscle cells (S-ECM) or fibroblasts, but not from proliferating cells (P-ECM), robustly induces a senescence phenotype in human proliferative endothelial cells (ECs) over a two-week culture period, whereas ECM from proliferating cells (P-ECM) does not elicit this effect. This induction appears to be at least partially mediated by the transforming growth factor beta (TGF-β) signaling pathway. Notably, inhibiting TGF-β receptor 1 (TGFβR1) in proliferative ECs grown in S-ECM significantly attenuated the senescence phenotype. These results further show that one of the matrisome proteins able to mediate the pro-senescence effect of S-ECM is transforming growth factor beta 1 induced transcript 1 (TGFβ1|1). Importantly, when discs coated with S-ECM were implanted in young mice, an increase in senescence markers was observed compared to mice implanted with discs coated with P-ECM. Overall, this research demonstrates that senescent-derived ECM acts as a potent trigger of cellular senescence, both in vitro and in vivo, with the involvement of the TGF-β signaling pathway playing a crucial role.Copyright © 2026. title: Exploring Environmental Sustainability in Mohs Micrographic Surgery.
abstract: Health care resource use, pollution, and greenhouse gas emissions are increasingly studied to balance quality patient care with environmental, social, and financial impacts. However, consolidated sustainability recommendations for Mohs micrographic surgery (MMS) remain unexplored.To assess current recommendations and studies on environmental sustainability in MMS.Following PRISMA-ScR guidelines, a literature review was conducted across PubMed, ScienceDirect, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane databases from 2014 to 2024. English peer-reviewed studies using keywords "climate change," "margin control," "environment," "sustainability," "waste," "resource," "Mohs micrographic," "Mohs," and "micrographic" were included. Duplicates and conference abstracts were excluded.Of 5,526 articles, nine met inclusion criteria after independent review. Recommendations included standardized surgical sets, limiting instruments to essentials, and redesigning procedure rooms to improve recycling access. Three articles found no significant difference in infection rates between sterile and nonsterile glove use. Other suggestions involved recycling plastics, using microtubules to reduce chromacoding dye waste by minimizing spillage and drying, and scheduling virtual preoperative visits to reduce travel emissions. Insurance reimbursement for virtual visits remains a limitation.Restructuring surgical protocols and procedure room design encourages innovation and addresses workflow inefficiencies rooted in tradition rather than evidence, promoting sustainability in MMS.Copyright © 2026 by the American Society for Dermatologic Surgery, Inc. llm_summary: Environmental sustainability in healthcare is increasingly important as clinicians seek to balance quality patient care with ecological impact, yet specific recommendations for Mohs micrographic surgery, a common skin cancer treatment, have not been systematically reviewed. Researchers conducted a literature review following PRISMA-ScR guidelines, searching five major databases from 2014 to 2024 for peer-reviewed studies addressing environmental sustainability, waste, resources, and climate change in relation to Mohs micrographic surgery. Of 5,526 articles identified, nine met inclusion criteria and yielded recommendations including standardized surgical sets, limiting instruments to essentials, redesigning procedure rooms for better recycling access, reducing chromacoding dye waste through microtubules, and scheduling virtual preoperative visits to decrease travel emissions. The review found that three studies reported no significant difference in infection rates between sterile and nonsterile glove use, suggesting potential opportunities to reduce waste without compromising patient safety. A key limitation is that insurance reimbursement for virtual visits remains uncertain, which may hinder implementation of some sustainability measures in clinical practice.

title: Executive Summary of the American Radium Society Appropriate Use Criteria for Selective Use of Pelvic Radiation Therapy in Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer: A Consensus Statement.
abstract: Pelvic radiotherapy is commonly incorporated in the treatment of locally-advanced rectal cancer to reduce the risk of locoregional recurrence, but can be associated with substantial acute toxicity and long-term morbidity. However, treatment may be personalized for selective use of radiotherapy in a subset of patients identified to be at low to intermediate risk of locoregional recurrence following resection. This multi-specialty-led committee included gastrointestinal radiation and medical oncology, gastroenterology, radiology, and colorectal surgery. Using the Population, Intervention, Comparator, Outcome, Timing and Study Design (PICOTS) framework, evidence regarding treatment outcomes was assessed using Cochrane and Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) methodology. Eligible studies included prospective and retrospective (n ≥ 50) studies published between 1/1/2005 - 6/24/2025 from Embase, Medline and PubMed databases. Study type and quality were assessed. Well-established RAND corportaion/University of California Los Angeles (RAND-UCLA) consensus methodology (modified Delphi) was used to rate the appropriateness of the treatment options. Of the 110 articles identified using the search strategy, 35 were selected that met all inclusion criteria. Of the 35 references used as evidence, 35 are categorized as therapeutic including 14 well-designed studies (Phase II randomized and Phase III), 12 moderately well-designed studies that account for most common biases (matched cohort and Phase II studies), 7 studies with design limitations (retrospective reviews), and 3 meta-analyses. Variant cases were developed as examples to illustrate practical applications of consensus recommendations for when RT can be safely omitted. title: American Gastroenterological Association-North American Society for Pediatric Gastroenterology, Hepatology and Nutrition Pediatric Functional Constipation Clinical Care Pathway.
abstract: Functional constipation (FC) is a prevalent condition in pediatrics that significantly impacts quality of life and health care utilization. The American Gastroenterological Association (AGA) and the North American Society for Pediatric Gastroenterology, Hepatology, and Nutrition (NASPGHAN) collaborated to develop a clinical care pathway for pediatric primary care providers and pediatric gastroenterologists, based on consensus among content experts, for the diagnosis and management of FC in children. This pathway aims to provide a structured, practical approach to streamline clinical decision-making and improve patient outcomes.A multi-disciplinary panel of experts selected based on their clinical experience and leadership and/or scientific contribution to the field conducted a roundtable discussion of the state of the art, identifying key diagnostic and management principles. A consensus-driven approach with agreement between panel members was used to establish standardized recommendations for diagnosis, treatment, and transition to adult care.The pathway integrates Rome IV pediatric FC criteria with a symptom-based approach to enhance clinical utility. Diagnostic recommendations prioritize history and physical examination, with limited use of diagnostic studies. Treatment strategies include dietary modifications, behavioral interventions, pharmacologic therapies, and escalation to subspecialty referrals, and advanced interventions when necessary. The pathway also provides guidance for special populations, including neurodivergent children, and outlines a structured transition process to adult care.The AGA-NASPGHAN Pediatric Functional Constipation Clinical Care Pathway standardizes evaluation and management, ensuring a practical approach for clinicians. Future research should focus on optimizing real-world implementation and evaluating long-term patient outcomes.Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Inc.

llm_summary: Functional constipation is a common condition in children that reduces quality of life and increases healthcare costs, prompting the need for standardized clinical guidance. The American Gastroenterological Association and the North American Society for Pediatric Gastroenterology, Hepatology, and Nutrition convened a multidisciplinary expert panel to develop a clinical care pathway for diagnosing and managing pediatric functional constipation in both primary care and specialty settings. The resulting pathway integrates Rome IV diagnostic criteria with a symptom-based approach and recommends prioritizing history and physical examination while limiting unnecessary diagnostic testing. Treatment recommendations progress from dietary modifications and behavioral interventions through pharmacologic therapies to subspecialty referral and advanced interventions when needed, with specific guidance for neurodivergent children and structured transition planning to adult care. Future research should focus on implementing this pathway in real-world clinical settings and evaluating whether it improves long-term patient outcomes.
llm_summary_expert: The American Gastroenterological Association and North American Society for Pediatric Gastroenterology, Hepatology, and Nutrition convened a multidisciplinary expert panel to develop a consensus-based clinical care pathway for diagnosing and managing functional constipation in children. The pathway integrates Rome IV pediatric functional constipation criteria with symptom-based assessment to guide primary care providers and pediatric gastroenterologists in standardized clinical decision-making. Diagnostic recommendations emphasize history and physical examination with limited diagnostic testing, while treatment strategies incorporate dietary modifications, behavioral interventions, and pharmacologic therapies with escalation to subspecialty referral when indicated. The pathway includes guidance for special populations such as neurodivergent children and establishes a structured transition protocol to adult care. The abstract does not report quantitative outcome data, limiting assessment of the pathway's effectiveness in improving patient outcomes or clinical implementation.

title: Neuromuscular blocking agents for tracheal intubation of critically ill adults: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Emergency tracheal intubation in critically ill adults is associated with a high risk of peri-intubation adverse events, making first-attempt success a key safety target.This study aimed to evaluate whether the use of neuromuscular blocking agents (NMBAs) improves the proportion of first-attempt success and reduces adverse events during emergent intubations outside the operating room.This was a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials or nonrandomized studies comparing sedative-hypnotic plus NMBA versus sedative-hypnotic alone in critically ill adults undergoing emergency endotracheal intubation in nonoperative settings. Animal, cadaveric, manikin/simulation, and pediatric studies were excluded. Articles were screened on 21 August 2025, in Ovid MEDLINE, Ovid Embase, Ovid Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, and the Web of Science Core Collection.Of 4736 screened citations, 13 studies (8 cohort; 5 before-after studies) were included in the quantitative analysis, with 14 072 participants. NMBA use was associated with higher first-attempt success, which ranged from 69 to 92% (pooled odds ratio, 2.72; 95% onfidence interval: 1.42-5.21; low-certainty evidence). Secondary outcomes related to adverse events were rated as very low certainty due to sparse data, inconsistent reporting, and serious imprecision.NMBA use during emergency intubation was associated with improved first-attempt success, although the certainty of evidence was low.Copyright © 2026 Wolters Kluwer Health, LLC. llm_summary: Emergency intubation in critically ill adults carries high risk of complications, making successful placement on the first attempt an important safety goal. Researchers conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of 13 studies involving 14,072 participants to compare whether adding neuromuscular blocking agents (medications that temporarily paralyze muscles) to sedatives improved outcomes compared to sedatives alone during emergency intubation outside operating rooms. The use of neuromuscular blocking agents was associated with higher first-attempt success rates, with a pooled odds ratio of 2.72 (95% confidence interval: 1.42–5.21), though the certainty of this evidence was rated as low. Secondary outcomes regarding adverse events could not be reliably assessed due to sparse data, inconsistent reporting across studies, and serious imprecision in the available information. Future research with more rigorous study designs and standardized outcome reporting would be needed to establish the true benefit of neuromuscular blocking agents and their safety profile during emergency intubation.
llm_summary_expert: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 13 studies (8 cohort; 5 before-after) including 14,072 critically ill adults compared sedative-hypnotic plus neuromuscular blocking agents (NMBAs) versus sedative-hypnotic alone during emergency endotracheal intubation in nonoperative settings. The primary outcome was first-attempt intubation success, while secondary outcomes assessed peri-intubation adverse events. NMBA use was associated with higher first-attempt success ranging from 69 to 92% (pooled odds ratio, 2.72; 95% confidence interval: 1.42-5.21; low-certainty evidence). Secondary outcomes related to adverse events were rated as very low certainty due to sparse data, inconsistent reporting, and serious imprecision. The certainty of evidence supporting improved first-attempt success with NMBA use was low, limiting confidence in the clinical applicability of these findings.

title: The Multiply Revised Knee: Techniques for What to Do Next.
abstract: The multiply revised total knee arthroplasty (TKA) poses unique surgical challenges. Patients who present to the office with a failed TKA or revision TKA expect durable, long-term fixation and improved function, yet bone loss and extensor mechanism insufficiency can easily complicate the reconstruction. The aim of this American Association of Hip and Knee Surgeons symposium was to provide up-to-date guidance for rerevision TKA with a specific focus on (1) safe exposure; (2) improved fixation with impaction grafting; (3) improved fixation using porous metal structural augmentation; and (4) managing the patella. After reviewing this article, the reader should feel comfortable with standard and extensile exposures of a revision knee arthroplasty, understand the technique and outcomes for impaction bone grafting and the use of porous metal augmentation, and develop an algorithm for treating and optimizing patello-femoral kinematics through augmentation and reconstruction techniques.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Inc. llm_summary: Multiple revisions of total knee replacement surgery present significant technical difficulties because patients develop bone loss and weakening of the leg extension mechanism that complicate achieving stable, long-lasting results. This American Association of Hip and Knee Surgeons symposium aimed to provide current surgical guidance for rerevision total knee arthroplasty focusing on four key areas: safe surgical approaches to access the knee, improved implant stability through impaction bone grafting, improved stability using porous metal structural augmentation, and optimal management of the kneecap. The authors reviewed techniques for both standard and extended surgical exposures needed to access a previously revised knee, along with methods for impaction bone grafting and porous metal augmentation to restore bone support for the new implant. After reviewing this article, surgeons should be able to select appropriate surgical approaches, understand how to use bone grafting and metal augmentation techniques, and develop a treatment plan for optimizing kneecap positioning through augmentation and reconstruction. The symposium provides a framework for managing the complex anatomical challenges that arise when patients require multiple knee replacement revisions, though the abstract does not report specific outcome data or comparative effectiveness results.
llm_summary_expert: This American Association of Hip and Knee Surgeons symposium addressed surgical techniques for multiply revised total knee arthroplasty (TKA), a procedure complicated by bone loss and extensor mechanism insufficiency in patients with failed primary or revision implants. The symposium provided guidance on four key technical areas: safe surgical exposure approaches, impaction bone grafting for improved fixation, porous metal structural augmentation for fixation enhancement, and patella management strategies. The authors aimed to enable surgeons to perform standard and extensile exposures, understand impaction grafting techniques and outcomes, apply porous metal augmentation methods, and develop algorithms for optimizing patellofemoral kinematics through augmentation and reconstruction. The symposium synthesized current evidence to address the unique challenges of rerevision TKA where patients require durable long-term fixation and functional improvement despite significant bone loss. The abstract does not report quantitative outcome data, effect estimates, or comparative results from clinical trials.

title: Incidence of secondary intraocular lens implantation in school-aged children left aphakic to age 4.5 years in the Infant Aphakia Treatment Study.
abstract: To determine the incidence of secondary intraocular lens (IOL) implantation in a cohort of children randomized to aphakia after unilateral congenital cataract surgery.12 clinical sites in the United States.Randomized clinical trial. Data regarding secondary IOL implantation were collected retrospectively when patients were age 10.5 years.We calculated the cumulative incidence of secondary IOL implantation in participants in the Infant Aphakia Treatment Study who were randomized to aphakia to age 4.5 years and were followed at age 10.5 years.22 (43%, 95% CI, 29%-58%) of the 51 participants left aphakic to age 4.5 years who had better than light perception vision at age 4.5 years received a secondary IOL by age 10.5. More than half (59%) of these were implanted by age 6 (median 64.5 months, interquartile range 60-80). Secondary IOLs were implanted in children with good visual acuity (≤20/40), as well as those with poor visual outcomes (≥20/200) (39% and 44%, respectively). Children who received a secondary IOL did not report less contact lens wear than those remaining aphakic (average of 94% of waking hours vs 90%, respectively). However, the proportion of children receiving a secondary IOL varied substantially by study center.Many children with unilateral congenital cataract who are initially left aphakic remain aphakic throughout the elementary school years. Practice patterns and family preference seem to be important drivers of the decision to implant a secondary IOL in these children.Copyright © 2026 Published by Wolters Kluwer on behalf of ASCRS and ESCRS.

llm_summary: The Infant Aphakia Treatment Study examined whether children initially left without an intraocular lens (IOL, an artificial lens implant) after congenital cataract surgery would eventually receive one later in childhood. Researchers followed 51 children who were randomized to remain aphakic (without an IOL) until age 4.5 years and collected data on secondary IOL implantation when these children reached age 10.5 years. By age 10.5 years, 22 children (43%, 95% CI 29%-58%) had received a secondary IOL, with more than half of these implantations occurring by age 6 years (median 64.5 months). Secondary IOLs were implanted across a range of visual outcomes, including children with good vision (≤20/40) and those with poor vision (≥20/200), and contact lens wear rates were similar between children who received IOLs and those who remained aphakic. The substantial variation in secondary IOL implantation rates across different study centers suggests that practice patterns and family preferences, rather than clinical outcomes alone, drive the decision to implant.

Among 51 participants left aphakic to age 4.5 years who retained better than light perception vision, 22 (43%, 95% CI, 29%-58%) received a secondary IOL by age 10.5 years, with 59% implanted by age 6 (median 64.5 months). Secondary IOL implantation occurred in children with both good visual acuity (≤20/40) and poor visual outcomes (≥20/200), at rates of 39% and 44% respectively.

title: Baseline Liver Function Predicts Long-Term Survival Beyond Perioperative Outcomes After Liver Resection for Biliary Tract Cancer.
abstract: The aspartate aminotransferase-to-platelet ratio index + albumin-bilirubin (APRI+ALBI) score reflects hepatic functional reserve and is widely used for risk stratification of posthepatectomy liver failure (PHLF). However, whether baseline hepatic function also predicts long-term survival in biliary tract cancer (BTC) remains unclear.Patients undergoing curative-intent liver resection for BTC (perihilar cholangiocarcinoma [pCCA], intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma [iCCA], gallbladder cancer [GBC]) at Mayo Clinic Rochester between 2000 and 2024 were analyzed. Patients were stratified into APRI+ALBI high and low groups using the previously published cutoff (- 2.46). To minimize baseline imbalances, 1:1 direct matching based on tumor type, age, sex, and Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) status was performed. OS and RFS were analyzed using Kaplan-Meier methods with log-rank testing and multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression analysis.Among 683 eligible patients, 616 with available APRI+ALBI scores were included in the analysis. High (poor) APRI+ALBI scores were associated with male sex, pCCA, more frequent major hepatectomy and vascular resection, and higher rates of lymph node positivity and advanced tumor stage. This group also experienced increased rates of major postoperative complications, PHLF grade B/C, and 90-day mortality. Correspondingly, median OS and RFS were significantly worse in the high APRI+ALBI group (OS: 39.8 versus 62.9 months, p = 0.004; RFS: 22.2 versus 27.4 months, p = 0.019). These significant differences persisted after direct matching, and APRI+ALBI remained an independent predictor of both outcomes on multivariable Cox regression.Preoperative APRI+ALBI score independently predicts survival after curative-intent resection for BTC, supporting a clinically relevant link between baseline hepatic functional reserve and oncologic outcomes beyond perioperative risk.© 2026. title: Association of a polygenic risk score with diagnosis and outcomes in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.
abstract: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is characterized by chronic progressive pulmonary fibrosis and high mortality. Genetic markers, summarized into a polygenic risk score (PRS), associate with IPF in well-phenotyped research cohorts.To evaluate the performance of the PRS using real-world data from routinely captured electronic health care records.We conducted an observational study evaluating the association of a PRS for IPF with electronic health care record diagnosis of IPF as well as lung transplant-free survival in 4 independent cohorts: the Mass General Brigham Biobank (MGBB), Mayo Clinic Biobank (MCBB), Mayo Clinic Tapestry Cohort (Tapestry), and U.K. Biobank (UKBB). We used multivariable logistic regression and multivariable Cox proportional hazards models adjusting for age, gender, and principal components of ancestry. The cohorts then underwent fixed and random effects meta-analysis.Of 37 709, 44 195, 43 202, and 447 422 participants from MGBB, MCBB, Tapestry, and UKBB, respectively, 1015 (2.7%), 2879 (6.5%), 1310 (3.0%), and 2742 (0.6%) participants had an IPF diagnosis. Meta-analysis demonstrated a high-risk PRS associated with IPF diagnosis (odds ratio [OR] = 2.88; 95% CI, 2.41-3.44) compared to all other individuals. A high-risk PRS also associated with the composite endpoint of mortality or lung transplant among those with an IPF diagnosis (hazard ratio [HR] = 1.23; 95% CI, 1.11-1.35) compared to all other individuals.A PRS can identify those at risk for an IPF diagnosis and mortality in biobank-scale data, which may have implications for clinical decisions. llm_summary: Researchers examined whether a polygenic risk score (PRS)—a genetic test combining multiple disease-associated genetic markers—could identify individuals at risk for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), a serious lung disease characterized by progressive scarring and high mortality. The study evaluated the PRS across four large biobank cohorts totaling over 572,000 participants, using electronic health records to identify IPF diagnoses and track outcomes including mortality and lung transplantation. A high-risk PRS was associated with an approximately 2.88-fold increased odds of IPF diagnosis and a 1.23-fold increased hazard of mortality or lung transplant among those with IPF, with confidence intervals not crossing the null in either case. These findings suggest that genetic risk scores may help identify individuals at elevated risk for IPF and worse outcomes in large-scale biobank settings, potentially informing clinical decision-making. The authors note that further research is necessary to determine whether incorporating genetic information into routine clinical practice would provide meaningful clinical utility.

title: Clinical pathways for cognitively unimpaired individuals with Alzheimer's disease neuropathological change.
abstract: The recent approval of disease-modifying therapies for symptomatic Alzheimer's disease is a major advance for a condition with few therapeutic options. Anti-amyloid monoclonal antibodies have shown clinically meaningful benefits in slowing cognitive decline. Clinical trials in symptomatic Alzheimer's disease suggest that anti-amyloid therapies might provide the greatest benefit in subgroups who have low baseline levels of Alzheimer's disease pathology; ongoing prevention trials are evaluating these therapies in cognitively unimpaired individuals who have biomarker evidence of Alzheimer's disease neuropathological change (ADNC). However, the possibility of biomarker testing and treatment in cognitively unimpaired people raises key questions about ethics and the consequences that follow from a positive test or an uncertain result (ie, the so-called downstream effects on patients and health systems). Furthermore, test accuracy might be questioned when ADNC has a low prevalence in the population being tested and in the case of intermediate-range biomarker concentrations that might not reliably indicate true ADNC or be false positives. If anti-amyloid therapies prove beneficial for cognitively unimpaired people with ADNC and become part of routine practice, several key knowledge gaps must be addressed to support safe, scalable, real-world implementation of Alzheimer's disease treatment.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Evaluation of radiological lung pattern and disease progression in patients with asbestosis compared to patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.

Lung parenchyma was segmented using CALIPER software, which quantifies reticulations (RET), ground-glass opacities (GGO), and honeycombing (HC), providing an interstitial lung disease (ILD) score based on the percentage of affected lung volume. llm_summary: Researchers examined whether asbestosis and idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), two progressive lung diseases with similar imaging appearances, show different patterns of deterioration on high-resolution CT scans. The study compared baseline and follow-up CT scans from 17 patients with asbestosis and 17 with IPF over a median follow-up period of 35 months, using specialized software to quantify the extent of lung damage including scarring patterns and honeycombing. Patients with asbestosis showed significantly slower disease progression, with a median increase in lung damage of 0.70% per month compared to 2.06% per month in IPF patients (p = 0.024). The two conditions could be distinguished by specific imaging features, with asbestosis characterized by subpleural lines and pleural involvement while IPF showed more honeycombing and enlarged mediastinal fat. These findings suggest that quantitative CT analysis can effectively differentiate disease progression between these two conditions and identify characteristic imaging patterns that may help clinicians distinguish between them.

title: Renal single-nucleus transcriptomic of a new model of cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome in aging swine.
abstract: Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome entails pathophysiological interactions among the heart, the kidneys, and metabolic derangements. The specific cell populations implicated in renal injury have yet to be identified. We leveraged a new model of CKM syndrome in aging swine and single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) to investigate the renal cell-specific transcriptomic profile and set the stage for future testing of potential new targets. Aging pigs with CKM syndrome were studied for 14 wk. Kidneys were harvested, nuclei isolated, snRNA-seq performed, and UMAP plots generated using default parameters. Expression profiles of marker genes were visualized to define renal cell types, ranked by the number of differentially expressed genes (DEGs), and factored by the total number of cells per cell type. Top DEGs/cell type were visualized, and their protein expression was assessed in confirmatory studies. A total of 52,367 nuclei were analyzed. Thirty clusters were identified and filtered by canonical gene markers, revealing 20 renal cell types. Subsequent analysis of CKM syndrome kidneys showed that proximal tubular (PT) and immune (IM) cell subpopulations had 49.1% and 45.8% of cells with DEGs, respectively, which were mainly implicated in microtubule organization and age-related inflammation (IL2-STAT5 signaling). Protein expression of β2-tubulin was downregulated in PT cells, whereas expression of STAT5 was upregulated in IM cells. The renal snRNA-seq transcriptomic landscape of a translational swine model of CKM syndrome identified PT and IM cells with the largest numbers of DEGs. Our observations may guide future studies aimed at modulating specific age-related renal abnormalities in CKM syndrome to slow disease progression.NEW & NOTEWORTHY Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome is a complex disease that affects up to 90% of US adults. This work characterized the renal transcriptomic landscape of a novel model of CKM in aging swine. The cardiovascular, renal, and metabolic parameters in pigs are very similar to those in humans, and our work may guide future studies aimed at modulating specific age-related renal abnormalities in CKM to slow disease progression and reduce mortality.

llm_summary: Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome, a condition affecting up to 90% of US adults, involves harmful interactions between the heart, kidneys, and metabolic systems, but the specific kidney cell types responsible for injury remain unclear. Researchers used single-nucleus RNA sequencing to analyze 52,367 cell nuclei from kidneys of aging pigs with this syndrome, identifying 20 distinct renal cell types and comparing their gene expression patterns. Proximal tubular cells and immune cells showed the highest rates of altered gene expression, with 49.1% and 45.8% of these cells respectively displaying changes primarily related to microtubule organization and age-related inflammation through IL2-STAT5 signaling. Protein validation confirmed that β2-tubulin was reduced in proximal tubular cells while STAT5 was increased in immune cells, suggesting these molecular changes may contribute to kidney dysfunction in the syndrome. These findings identify potential therapeutic targets for slowing kidney disease progression in cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome, though further studies are needed to test whether modulating these specific cell populations can improve outcomes.

title: Management of Rhabdomyosarcoma in Pediatric Patients.
abstract: Treatment of rhabdomyosarcoma (RMS) involves a multimodality approach, including chemotherapy, surgery, and radiotherapy, while minimizing the long-term treatment-related morbidities. This article outlines the key points related to the diagnosis and management of RMS with a focus on current surgical management of RMS at specific tumor sites. There is a need for improved local control approaches and systemic therapy in RMS to reduce locoregional and metastatic relapse, reduce late sequelae of treatment, and improve functional outcomes. title: Arthroscopic Hip Capsular Reconstruction.
abstract: Hip capsular reconstruction is an emerging surgical option for treating irreparable capsular deficiency in the setting of hip microinstability. llm_summary: Hip capsular reconstruction is an emerging surgical technique designed to address hip microinstability caused by irreparable damage to the hip capsule, a tissue that normally stabilizes the hip joint. While the primary approach remains preventing capsular damage through careful surgical technique and repair, reconstruction offers an alternative for revision cases or situations where aggressive capsule removal has occurred. Multiple graft materials, including iliotibial band, dermal allograft, and Achilles tendon, have shown biomechanical ability to restore stability in laboratory and surgical studies. However, the optimal choice of graft material and the long-term effectiveness of these reconstruction approaches remain subjects of ongoing investigation. Successful outcomes depend on careful selection of appropriate patients, strict adherence to established surgical principles, and a structured rehabilitation program following the procedure.

title: Ischiofemoral Impingement: Pathophysiology, Diagnosis, and Treatment.
abstract: Ischiofemoral impingement is an under-recognized source of buttock and groin pain resulting from abnormal contact between the proximal femur and the ischium. Entrapment of the quadratus femoris muscle results in pain, mechanical symptoms and in some cases irritation of the sciatic nerve. Characteristic MRI findings include narrowing of the ischiofemoral space and quadratus femoris edema or atrophy. The diagnosis is confirmed with guided injections. llm_summary: Ischiofemoral impingement, an often-overlooked condition causing buttock and groin pain, occurs when the proximal femur makes abnormal contact with the ischium and traps the quadratus femoris muscle. This entrapment can produce pain, mechanical symptoms, and in some cases irritation of the sciatic nerve, making accurate diagnosis clinically important. Characteristic findings on MRI include narrowing of the ischiofemoral space and evidence of quadratus femoris edema or atrophy, with diagnosis confirmed through guided injections. For patients whose symptoms persist despite conservative management, surgical decompression of the ischiofemoral space can be performed using direct approaches such as open or endoscopic surgery, or indirect methods including femoral osteotomy or hip arthroplasty in rare cases. This review synthesizes the pathophysiology, diagnostic criteria, and treatment options for ischiofemoral impingement to improve recognition and management of this underdiagnosed condition.

abstract: Robotic-assisted surgery is now the standard for elective colorectal procedures, but its use in emergencies remains limited. title: Preoperative Weight Loss Before Total Joint Arthroplasty Using Novel Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Agonists.
abstract: This study determined the prevalence of glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) use before total joint arthroplasty (TJA), measured weight loss of patients on GLP-1s, and evaluated if GLP-1s were associated with outcomes.We identified 6482 patients (2990 hips; 3492 knees) who had primary TJAs between 2019 and February 2023. The mean age was 67 years, 50% were female, and 12% had a body mass index ≥40 kg/m2. Univariable and multivariable models evaluated outcomes. Mean follow-up was 3 years.The prevalence of GLP-1s before TJA was 3%, increasing from 2% in 2019 to 5% in 2022. The mean preoperative weight change on GLP-1s was -9 pounds (range, -110 to +36 pounds). Among patients taking GLP-1s, 19% lost ≥20 pounds prior to surgery, and the mean body mass index change was -1.4 kg/m2 (range, -16.3 to 6.2 kg/m2). In univariable analyses, GLP-1 use was not associated with revisions (P = .35), reoperations (P = .09), or complications (P = .23). In multivariable analyses, GLP-1s were not associated with revisions (P = .66), reoperations (P = .34), or complications (P = .85). There was no difference in the risk of a 90-day postoperative emergency department visit between those on GLP-1s vs not on those medications (odds ratio, 1.5; P = .07).The prevalence of preoperative GLP-1s before TJA increased from 2% in 2019 to 5% in 2022, and preoperative weight change on GLP-1s varied considerably. title: Inhibition of EED enhances osteogenic differentiation and bone formation: a potential therapeutic strategy for osteogenesis imperfecta.
abstract: Osteogenesis imperfecta (OI) is a heterogeneous group of inherited connective tissue disorders primarily caused by dominant mutations in COL1A1 or COL1A2 that impair type I procollagen folding and secretion. Misfolded collagen accumulates in the endoplasmic reticulum (ER), triggering ER stress and osteoblast dysfunction, and bone fragility. Current pharmacologic therapy focuses on inhibiting bone resorption but has limited efficacy and does not address the underlying biology of the disease. The epigenetic regulator polycomb-repressive complex 2 (PRC2) has emerged as an important regulator of bone formation. Genetic and pharmacologic disruption of PRC2 enhanced osteogenic differentiation in WT cells. Here, we demonstrate that inhibition of the PRC2 through targeting its essential component embryonic ectoderm development (EED) enhances osteogenic differentiation, improves bone architecture in male Col1a2 +/G610C OI mouse models, modulates the integrated stress response (ISR), and improves ER morphology in OI cells. These findings identify EED inhibition as a novel epigenetic strategy to restore collagen homeostasis and improve skeletal integrity in OI.© The Author(s) 2026. title: Fluid biomarkers in the evolving care landscape of Alzheimer's disease and related disorders.
abstract: Fluid biomarkers for Alzheimer's disease have advanced rapidly during the past several years driven by breakthroughs including development of ultrasensitive and multiplexing technologies and high specificity antibodies. Blood-based biomarkers, such as neurofilament light for frontotemporal dementia and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, and phosphorylated tau 217 for the diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease, are now being implemented in clinical practice, which is particularly timely because of the increasing clinical availability of amyloid-targeting treatments in Alzheimer's disease. Multiple fluid biomarkers are needed to capture the complexity of disease mechanisms for precise diagnosis and to measure the diverse pathologies that lead to dementia, such as vascular, α-synuclein, and TDP-43 pathologies. Moreover, fluid biomarkers can aid in capturing heterogeneity in treatment course between patients, probably due to copathologies or key intermediates, including microglia and astrocyte dysregulation. Increased focus on biomarker-pathology relationships in experimental models will likely accelerate biomarker development and further the understanding of their precise substrates. title: Recent advances in adult-onset disorders of muscle lipid metabolism.
abstract: To summarize recent advances in adult-onset disorders of muscle lipid metabolism, with particular emphasis on fatty acid β-oxidation disorders (FAODs), multiple acyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency (MADD) and MADD-like disorders, and neutral lipid storage disease with myopathy (NLSDM).Recent studies in FAODs have provided new insights into long-term outcomes, exercise physiology, prognostic biomarkers, and the impact of newborn screening (NBS) on disease management. In MADD, growth differentiation factor 15 (GDF15) has emerged as a potential biomarker. Major advances have occurred in MADD-like disorders, including the identification of COASY as a novel disease gene and the recognition of sertraline-associated acquired MADD-like disorder, challenging the traditional view of FAODs as exclusively genetic diseases. In NLSDM, recent cohort studies have expanded the phenotypic spectrum, highlighted cardiomyopathy as a major determinant of morbidity and mortality, and revealed a critical role of adipose triglyceride lipase (ATGL) in maintaining mitochondrial network integrity and function.Advances in clinical phenotyping, metabolic biomarkers, molecular genetics, and NBS have substantially improved the diagnosis and understanding of adult-onset disorders of muscle lipid metabolism. The recognition of sertraline-associated MADD-like disorder has established that lipid storage myopathies can also arise through acquired toxic mechanisms. title: ERN ReCONNET-SLICC-SLEuro consensus on the therapeutic management of rare systemic lupus erythematosus manifestations (part 2).
abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) guidelines predominantly focus on common major organ involvement. An international taskforce from three SLE expert groups (European Reference Network on Connective Tissue and Musculoskeletal Diseases, Systemic Lupus International Collaborating Clinics, and the European Lupus Society) previously developed consensus therapeutic strategies for 24 rare SLE manifestations. Here, 77 participants contributed to the development of consensus therapeutic strategies for 22 additional rare SLE manifestations, including diffuse pulmonary haemorrhage, rare cutaneous manifestations (bullous lupus, chilblain lupus, lupus tumidus, erythema multiforme, and toxic epidermal necrolysis-like lupus erythematosus), renal manifestations (interstitial nephritis and lupus podocytopathy), rare neurological manifestations (chorea, small fibre neuropathy, catatonia, and intracranial hypertension), rare gastrointestinal manifestations (protein-losing enteropathy, lupus hepatitis, intestinal pseudo-obstruction, and peritonitis), musculoskeletal manifestations (myositis and Jaccoud's arthropathy), and other rare manifestations such as uveitis, angioedema due to anti-C1 esterase inhibitor antibodies, interstitial cystitis, and lupus mastitis. title: Outcomes of Lung Transplant Recipients Hospitalized With COVID-19 Infection in the Post-Acute Pandemic Era: A Nationwide Inpatient Analysis in the United States.
abstract: Lung transplant recipients (LuTRs) remain highly susceptible to severe COVID-19 due to chronic immunosuppression and graft vulnerability. Although early pandemic data described high morbidity and mortality, contemporary nationwide evidence from the post-acute pandemic period is limited.Using ICD-10-CM codes, we identified 9,276 adult LuTR hospitalizations in NRD-2022, of which 12.8% (n = 1185) had COVID-19. Primary outcomes included in-hospital mortality, CLAD, and 90-day readmission. Secondary outcomes included ARDS, invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV), acute kidney injury (AKI), ICU admission, shock, thromboembolic events, and resource utilization (length of stay [LOS], total charges). Multivariable logistic and linear regression models adjusted for patient- and hospital-level covariates.COVID-19-positive LuTRs had significantly higher in-hospital mortality than non-COVID LuTRs (aOR 3.97; p < .001) and markedly increased odds of CLAD (aOR 10.55; p < .001). They also demonstrated higher odds of ARDS (aOR 9.36; p < .001), IMV (aOR 3.07; p < .001), ICU admission (aOR 2.82; p < .001), shock (aOR 1.85; p < .001), AKI (aOR 1.53; p < .001), and superimposed bacterial pneumonia (aOR 1.75; p < .001). Rates of tracheostomy, VV-ECMO use, pulmonary embolism, and deep venous thrombosis did not differ significantly. Ninety-day readmission rates were similar (aOR 1.06; p = .41). COVID-19 hospitalizations were associated with longer LOS (+3.72 days; p = .001) and higher total charges (+$59,350; p = .012).In the post-acute pandemic era, COVID-19 continues to impose a substantial clinical and economic burden on LuTRs, with elevated risks of mortality, CLAD, respiratory failure, multiorgan dysfunction, and greater resource utilization. Continued vigilance, preventive strategies, and tailored management remain essential for this high-risk population.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Inc. All rights reserved.

llm_summary: Lung transplant recipients face heightened vulnerability to severe COVID-19 because their immunosuppressive medications, necessary to prevent organ rejection, impair their ability to fight infections. Researchers analyzed 9,276 hospitalizations of lung transplant recipients in 2022, comparing outcomes between the 1,185 patients with COVID-19 and those without, using statistical models to account for differences in patient characteristics. COVID-19-positive lung transplant recipients experienced nearly four times higher in-hospital mortality (adjusted odds ratio 3.97) and markedly elevated risks of chronic lung allograft dysfunction, acute respiratory distress syndrome, mechanical ventilation, and acute kidney injury compared to non-COVID patients. The COVID-19 group also had longer hospital stays by approximately 3.7 days and incurred approximately $59,350 in additional charges, though 90-day readmission rates were similar between groups. These findings indicate that COVID-19 continues to pose substantial clinical and economic risks to lung transplant recipients even in the post-acute pandemic period, supporting the need for continued preventive measures and specialized management strategies for this population.

title: Review Article: Immune Effector Cell-Mediated Enterocolitis Following CAR-T Cell Therapy-Clinical Features, Pathophysiology and Management.
abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) therapy has revolutionised the treatment of hematologic malignancies, and its use is expanding rapidly into numerous other disease states including autoimmune diseases. However, CAR-T therapy is associated with a spectrum of immune-related toxicities. In addition to the already well characterized cytokine release syndrome and immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome, it has become apparent that rarely, CAR-T can cause gastrointestinal mucosal inflammation, termed immune effector cell-mediated enterocolitis (IEC-EC).This state-of-the-art review highlights the CAR-T mechanism and details the epidemiology, pathophysiology, clinical manifestations, endoscopic and histopathologic features, and management of IEC-EC.This review presents the current state of knowledge through a comperhensive and detailed synthesis of all case series reported in the literature to date.Occurring in up to approximately 6% of patients typically following B cell maturation antigen-targeted CAR-T therapy, IEC-EC presents with severe diarrhoea and malabsorption, responds poorly to treatment, and portends a dire prognosis. Multi-disciplinary management should centre on early diagnosis, supportive cares, assessment and treatment of infections, and step-up pharmacotherapy, often featuring biologics and small molecules drawn from the inflammatory bowel disease pharmacologic armamentarium.Clinicians should maintain a high degree of vigilance for IEC-EC in patients presenting with gastrointestinal symptoms following CAR-T treatment. llm_summary: CAR-T cell therapy has transformed treatment of blood cancers but carries risks of immune-related side effects beyond the well-known cytokine release syndrome and neurotoxicity. This review synthesizes case series from the literature to characterize immune effector cell-mediated enterocolitis (IEC-EC), a rare gastrointestinal inflammation that occurs in approximately 6% of patients receiving CAR-T therapy, particularly those treated with B cell maturation antigen-targeted approaches. IEC-EC presents with severe diarrhea and malabsorption that typically responds poorly to standard treatments and is associated with a poor prognosis. Management requires a multidisciplinary approach emphasizing early diagnosis, supportive care, infection assessment and treatment, and escalating pharmacotherapy including drugs used for inflammatory bowel disease. Clinicians should maintain heightened awareness for gastrointestinal symptoms following CAR-T treatment, as early recognition and coordinated treatment may improve patient outcomes.

title: A Sentiment-Based Comparison of AI- and Physician-Generated Empathic Statements in Palliative Care.
abstract: Empathic communication promotes trust in patient-provider relationships. As healthcare integrates artificial intelligence (AI) into patient communication, we have yet to understand how these models' communication compares to that of physicians.Our primary objectives were to examine patient preferences for AI-generated vs. palliative care physician-generated empathic statements addressing fear and anxiety around cancer treatment, and to analyze associations between linguistic features and patient preferences.We conducted a secondary analysis of the PALL-AI trial, a randomized controlled survey comparing cancer patients' preferences of AI- to physician-generated empathic statements. Physicians and AI were provided the same prompt with a maximum sentence length. Patient preferences for each statement were measured in blinded surveys. We analyzed sentiment of the statements using the Valence Aware Dictionary and Sentiment Reasoner (VADER) and the National Research Council Canada (NRC) Emotion Lexicon. We evaluated associations between sentiment scores and patient preferences using Spearman's correlation coefficients.A total of 105 patients completed blinded surveys, preferring the AI-generated statement 72.4% of the time. VADER sentiment analysis showed all three AI statements displayed positive sentiment, while all three physician statements displayed negative sentiment. Controlling for statement length, AI statements used twice as many positive words as human statements. However, they contained a similar number of negative words. Of the eight NRC emotions, "trust" and "joy" demonstrated the strongest correlations with patient preference.Patients preferred AI-generated statements around cancer care over those from palliative care physicians when standardized for prompt and statement length. Analysis shows AI-generated statements contain more positive language which may be the factor driving patient preference toward AI.Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Inc.

llm_summary: Empathic communication from healthcare providers builds trust with patients, yet as artificial intelligence becomes integrated into clinical settings, it remains unclear how AI-generated messages compare to those written by physicians. Researchers conducted a secondary analysis of the PALL-AI trial in which 105 cancer patients reviewed blinded pairs of empathic statements addressing fear and anxiety around cancer treatment, with one statement generated by AI and one by a palliative care physician, both responding to identical prompts with the same maximum sentence length. Patients preferred the AI-generated statements 72.4% of the time, and sentiment analysis revealed that all three AI statements displayed positive sentiment while all three physician statements displayed negative sentiment, with AI statements using twice as many positive words overall. The analysis identified "trust" and "joy" as the emotions most strongly associated with patient preference for AI statements, suggesting that more positive language in AI-generated messages may explain why patients favored them over physician-written alternatives. Future research should examine whether this preference for positive language translates to improved clinical outcomes and whether physicians might benefit from training in more positive communication approaches.
